body.translated_text: In the Indian language - <s>Āryaśālistambaka Mahāyāna Sūtra Ṭīkā</s> (Commentary on the Noble Rice Stalk Mahāyāna Sūtra).

body.text: bhoṭabhāṣāyām - hphagaspā - salu - jaṅapā - śesvyavā - thegpā - chenapoī - doī - gyācher bśadpā

body.text: atha śālistambavibhāṣāyāḥ prathamaṃ paṭalam
body.translated_text: Now, the first chapter of the <s>Śālistamba Vibhāṣā</s> (Exposition on the Rice Stalk).

body.text: nama āryamañjuśrīkumārabhūtāya |
body.translated_text: Homage to <s>Āryamañjuśrīkumārabhūta</s> (the Noble Mañjuśrī in his youthful form).

body.text: tatra 'anantācintyaguṇyaṃ hi' ityādiṣu anantaguṇyamiti guṇaṃ hi balābhayāsaṃsṛṣṭādiguṇārthe devamanuṣyaiḥ pariceyatvāt, sevyatvāt, abhyasanīyatvād, bhāvanīyatvāt, sākṣātkaraṇīyatvāt prāptakaraṇīyatvācca guṇāḥ | te guṇāstu bahavaḥ | anantācintyeti samastaṃ padam | acintyaguṇatvaṃ tu śrāvaka-pratyekabuddha-sarva-pṛthagjana-sarvatārkikagaṇa-cittagocaraṃ samatikramaṇāt | tataḥ so 'nantācintyaguṇa samanvitaḥ | katama iti cet, ucyate - sambuddhaṃ karuṇātmakam | ityuktam | samyagaviparyastañca buddhatvāt sambuddhaḥ | sarvadharmānityatvasya duḥkha-śūnya-nairātmyādi-dharmān-pudgalanairātmyasvabhāvatayā yathāvad avabodhatvād buddhaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, regarding the verse beginning with 'possessing infinite and inconceivable qualities' and so forth: 'possessing infinite qualities' refers to qualities, for the term <s>guṇa</s> (quality), in the sense of qualities such as the <s>balas</s> (powers), <s>abhaya</s> (fearlessnesses), and other such attributes, denotes that which is to be attended to, served, practiced, cultivated, directly realized, and attained by gods and humans. Those qualities are indeed many. '<s>Anantācintya</s>' (infinite and inconceivable) is a compound word. The inconceivability of these qualities is because they transcend the mental range of <s>Śrāvakas</s> (hearers), <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones), all ordinary beings, and all assemblies of logicians. Therefore, he is endowed with infinite and inconceivable qualities. If one asks 'which qualities?', it is said: 'the fully awakened one whose nature is compassion.' Thus it is stated. He is called <s>Sambuddha</s> (fully awakened) because he has awakened correctly and without error. He is called <s>Buddha</s> (awakened one) because he has realized things as they truly are — the impermanence of all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena), <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering), <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), <s>nairātmya</s> (non-self), and other such qualities of phenomena, through the nature of <s>pudgala-nairātmya</s> (selflessness of the person) and <s>dharma-nairātmya</s> (selflessness of phenomena).

body.text: praphullakamalavad buddhervikāsād buddho, bodhatvād vā buddhaḥ | ajñānanidrā suptajaganmadhye jāgratapuruṣavat, yathāvadaviparyastasamyagjñānodayād buddha iti | athavājñajanāvabodhanād buddhaḥ | yathā - parādhīnasya svayameva pratisaṃvedana-dharmatattvāva-bodhavad unmārgabhrāntacittasya saṃsārāṭavīkāntāre janma-jarā-vyādhi-maraṇādi-pīḍitasya vividhadarśanagahanavane kleśāśīviṣabhayāplutāna itastataḥ paribhramato 'nyāṃścāpi sanmārge sanniveśya mokṣānuttaramahānagare praveśakāritvād buddha iti |
body.translated_text: He is called <s>Buddha</s> because of his blossoming, like a fully opened lotus; or he is <s>Buddha</s> because of his awakening. Just as an awakened person amidst a world asleep in the slumber of ignorance, he is called <s>Buddha</s> because of the arising of correct, unerring, right knowledge. Alternatively, he is <s>Buddha</s> because he awakens the ignorant. Just as one who, though dependent on others, comes to realize the truth of <s>dharma</s> (reality) through direct personal experience — so too for those whose minds have gone astray on wrong paths, who are afflicted by birth, old age, disease, death, and other torments in the wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), who are overwhelmed by the terror of the poisonous snakes of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) in the dense forest of manifold views, and who wander here and there — he is called <s>Buddha</s> because he establishes these others on the right path and causes them to enter the supreme great city of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation).

body.text: karuṇātmakamiti tu karuṇasvabhāvam | kleśakarmaduḥkhanivārakatvāt karuṇaḥ | yasmin karuṇātmakatvaṃ svabhāvataḥ sa karuṇātmakaḥ | sa sambuddhaḥ ; karuṇātmakatāyā api bhūtatvāt saṃbuddhaḥ karuṇātmakaḥ | tasmāt taṃ buddhaṃ karuṇātmakaṃ praṇipatya śālistambamiti ityuktam | praṇipatyeti samyakpūjayitvā vandanā-gaurava-pravaṇatayā praṇipatya | praṇipatya kiṃ karomīti cet- śālistambamiti sūtrasya upanibaddhaśāstrakārikāṃ pravakṣyāmi | ityuktam | tatra anantācintyaguṇyo hi ityanena svārthasampattirdarśitā | karuṇātmaka ityanena parārthasampattiruktā | sambuddhaṃ iti buddho hi (adhigatārthatvāt) sarvajña eva | 'anantācintyaguṇyaṃ hi' ityanena rāgādirahitatvam, kleśopakleśānāmaguṇānāṃ guṇavirodhatvāt | tasmāt tādṛśaṃ sarvajñaṃ viraktaṃ sambuddhaṃ karuṇātmaka iti yaḥ sarvaṃjānan vītarāgaḥ, sa ācāryamuṣṭerabhāvād aparān yathāvagataṃ dharmaṃ diśati | anena tu parahitakāritvāt parārthopasampadā diṣṭā | evaṃ svaparārthopasampannaṃ taṃ sambuddhaṃ praṇamāmi | tathāpi, vivakṣitapadasya vidyamānatvād vivakṣuṇā kimiṣyate? iti praśnaḥ | uttaraṃ - pravakṣyāmi | kiṃ vakṣyāmi? ucyate - śālistambasūtropanibaddha-śāstra-kārikām | śāstraṃ racayitum ādau sambandha-prayojana-abhidhānābhidheyacatuṣṭayaṃ kiṃ na nirvacanīyam?
body.translated_text: 'Whose nature is compassion' means whose essential nature is <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion). He is compassionate because he removes <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), <s>karma</s> (actions), and <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering). He in whom compassionate nature exists inherently is called 'one whose nature is compassion.' He is the <s>Sambuddha</s> (fully awakened one); because even his compassionate nature is real, the fully awakened one is compassionate by nature. Therefore, having prostrated to that <s>Buddha</s> whose nature is compassion, 'the <s>Śālistamba</s> (Rice Stalk)' — thus it is said. 'Having prostrated' means having properly worshipped, having bowed with an inclination of reverence and respect. If one asks 'having prostrated, what do I do?' — 'I shall expound the verses of the treatise composed upon the <s>Śālistamba Sūtra</s> (Rice Stalk Sūtra),' thus it is said. Herein, by the phrase 'possessing infinite and inconceivable qualities,' the accomplishment of one's own purpose (<s>svārtha-sampatti</s>) is shown. By the phrase 'whose nature is compassion,' the accomplishment of others' purpose (<s>parārtha-sampatti</s>) is stated. As for '<s>Sambuddha</s>' — he is indeed <s>Buddha</s> (because he has realized the truth), and thus is omniscient. By the phrase 'possessing infinite and inconceivable qualities,' freedom from <s>rāga</s> (attachment) and other afflictions is indicated, since the non-virtuous qualities of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and <s>upakleśas</s> (secondary afflictions) are opposed to true qualities. Therefore, such an omniscient, dispassionate, fully awakened one whose nature is compassion — he who knows all and is free from attachment, because he holds nothing back in a teacher's closed fist, directs others in the <s>Dharma</s> as he has understood it. By this, because he acts for the benefit of others, the accomplishment of others' purpose is indicated. Thus, I prostrate to that <s>Sambuddha</s> who is endowed with the accomplishment of both his own and others' purposes. Even so, since the intended word exists, the question arises: what does the one who wishes to speak intend? The answer: 'I shall expound.' What shall I expound? It is said: the verses of the treatise composed upon the <s>Śālistamba Sūtra</s>. Should not the four prerequisites — <s>sambandha</s> (connection), <s>prayojana</s> (purpose), <s>abhidhāna</s> (designation), and <s>abhidheya</s> (subject matter) — be stated before composing a treatise?

body.text: atra tadabhāvāt tadārambhaṇam anucitam | asambaddhāditvāt pramattapralāpavad ityanārambhaṇīyamiti dharmaḥ | śāstramiti dharmī | dharmadharmisāmānyaṃ hi pakṣaḥ | asambaddhāditvāditi hetuḥ | avabodhakatvāt hetuḥ, hetvarthasya tu avabodhakatvāt | tasmāt asambandhāditvādanārambhaṇīyamiti | pramattapralāpavaditi upamā | evaṃ vādine ucyate - asambandhāditvāditi yaduktaṃ ityuktahetorasiddham uktāyām atroktau sambandhādayaścatvāraḥ santyeva | te ca katame? ucyate - śālistambasūtropanibaddha-śāstrakārikāyāḥ vakṣyamāṇatvād atra sambandhaḥ syād eva | śālistambasūtramiti tīrthikādyanyeṣu granthaviśeṣaṇatayā anupalabdhatvāt śāstramidaṃ buddhasambaddham | tasmāt hetvaertho 'siddha eva | sambandhabhāvaśca prayojanasyāpyabhāve nāsti | tasmāduktam atra prayojanam - hetupratyayārthāvagamārthaṃ pudgala-nairātmya-dharmanairātmya-grāhya-grāhakābhāvāva gamāt kleśajñeyāvaraṇaṃ vibhajya anuttara-samyaksaṃbuddhopalabdhiḥ atra prayojanamastyeva |
body.translated_text: In the absence of these, undertaking it would be improper. The proposition is: 'This treatise should not be undertaken, because it lacks connection and so forth, like the babbling of a madman.' 'Treatise' is the subject (<s>dharmin</s>); 'should not be undertaken' is the property (<s>dharma</s>); the combination of subject and property constitutes the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>). 'Because it lacks connection and so forth' is the reason (<s>hetu</s>); it is a reason because it produces understanding, for a reason serves to make one understand its meaning. Therefore, 'it should not be undertaken because it lacks connection and so forth.' 'Like the babbling of a madman' is the analogy (<s>upamā</s>). To one who argues thus, it is replied: what you have said — 'because it lacks connection and so forth' — this stated reason is unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>), for in the present discourse, the four — connection and the rest — do indeed exist. And what are they? It is said: since the verses of the treatise composed upon the <s>Śālistamba Sūtra</s> are about to be expounded, the connection (<s>sambandha</s>) certainly exists here. The term '<s>Śālistamba Sūtra</s>' — since it is not found as a distinguishing feature of any treatise among <s>Tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers) and others, this treatise is connected with the <s>Buddha</s>. Therefore, the meaning of the reason is itself unestablished. And without the existence of connection, there is no absence of purpose either. Therefore, the purpose here is stated: from the understanding of the meaning of causes and conditions, by distinguishing the obscurations of <s>kleśāvaraṇa</s> (afflictive obscurations) and <s>jñeyāvaraṇa</s> (cognitive obscurations) through comprehending the absence of <s>grāhya</s> (apprehended object) and <s>grāhaka</s> (apprehending subject) via <s>pudgala-nairātmya</s> (selflessness of persons) and <s>dharma-nairātmya</s> (selflessness of phenomena), the attainment of <s>Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect awakening) — this purpose certainly exists here.

body.text: tasmāt saprayojanatvāt cikitsādiśāstravad viracanīyameva | yadyad sārthakaṃ tat tat tu viracanīyam | yathā cikitsādiśāstravad bhūtatvād upamāsiddhiṃ vakṣyāmi | asyābhidhānena śālistambopamayā ādhyātmika-bāhya-pratītyasamutpāda-samupayogād anenābhidhānena śālistambamiti cāpi bhavati | tasmādapi artho 'siddha eva | abhidheyamiti pratītyasamutpādasya dvādaśāṅgasya sapratyayasya pṛthaktaḥ yathākramaṃ lakṣaṇavyavasthāpanāt kartrādīn ahetūn pratikūlahetūn ca vihāya kleśopakleśa prahāṇāt samyagjñānam utpādya anuttaradharmakāyopalambhād idamabhidheyamapyastyeva | tasmācca hetvartho 'siddha eva | tasmāt cikitsādiśāstravad idaṃ śāstraṃ sambandhādisamanvitatvād, ārambhaṇīyameva| ārambhaṇīyamiti dharmaḥ | śāstramiti ca dharmī | dharmadharmisādhāraṇo hi pakṣaḥ | atra dharmabhāvāddharmī chatrīvat | tathā satyapi śāstramārabdhuṃ praṇāmakaraṇaṃ nirarthakam, prayojanābhāvāt, kākadantaparīkṣādiśāstravat ityasya hetvarthasya siddhatvaṃ darśayitumucyate -
body.translated_text: Therefore, because it has purpose, it should indeed be composed, like a treatise on medicine and the like. Whatever is meaningful should indeed be composed, just as a treatise on medicine and similar works — I shall demonstrate the establishment of the analogy through its being true. By this designation, through the simile of the <s>Śālistamba</s> (rice stalk), because of its applicability to both inner (<s>ādhyātmika</s>) and outer (<s>bāhya</s>) <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), by this designation it is also called '<s>Śālistamba</s>.' Therefore, this meaning too is fully established. As for the subject matter (<s>abhidheya</s>): because the twelve-limbed <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), together with its conditions, is individually and sequentially established in its characteristics — having set aside the creator (<s>kartṛ</s>) and other non-causes as well as contrary causes, and having abandoned <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and <s>upakleśas</s> (secondary afflictions) to generate right knowledge — from the attainment of the unsurpassed <s>Dharmakāya</s> (truth body), this subject matter too certainly exists. Therefore, the meaning of the reason is itself unestablished. Consequently, like a treatise on medicine and the like, this treatise, being endowed with connection and the other prerequisites, should indeed be undertaken. 'Should be undertaken' is the property (<s>dharma</s>); 'the treatise' is the subject (<s>dharmin</s>); their combination is the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>). Here, the subject possesses the property, like one who carries an umbrella. Even granting this, to show that the objection — 'the homage at the beginning of the treatise is meaningless, being without purpose, like examining the teeth of a crow' — has an unestablished reason, it is said:

body.text: śāstrārambhaṇāya śāstṛpūjā kṛtā | kimarthamiti cet, śāstre tatra ca gauravotpādahetubhūtatvād, dharmaśravaṇe jātagauravāṇāṃ śravaṇa-cintana-bhāvanāsu gauravaṃ bhavati | ajātagauravāṇāṃ tu abhūtatvād hetvarthe ca siddha eva | api śiṣṭācāra-nayapradarśanārthaṃ śāstrārambhe śāstuḥ pūjā kṛtā | ayaṃ tu sajjanaviduṣām ācāro 'sti | yadā kaścit prayojanārambhaṇamavatarati prathamam iṣṭadevaṃ praṇamya viśiṣṭaprayojanaṃ praviśati, abhīṣṭārtho 'ciraṃ sidhyati, tasmād anenāpi śāstrakāreṇa tāmeva sadācāranītim anusaratā śāstrārambhaṇe svaśāsturguṇābhidhānapūrvakaṃ praṇāmaṃ kṛtvā śāstravyākhyānāvatārād atra prayojanamastyeva | ucyate - śāstrārambhe śāstre praṇāmakaraṇam na niṣphalam śāstari śāstreṣu ca gauravotpādahetvartham, nānyathā | tataḥ śāstrārambhe śāstuḥ pūjanaṃ vyavasthitameva | tasmācca paraiḥ śāstrādau praṇāmakaraṇaṃ niṣprayojanam iti kimucyate? taddhetorasiddhatāṃ darśayitum kathitam | śāstram ārabdhuṃ praṇāmakaraṇaṃ tu cikitsādiśāstravat saprayojanam eva, na ca kākadantaparīkṣāvat | svaśāstāraṃ praṇamya śālistambasūtropanibaddhāṃ śāstrakārikāṃ pravakṣyāmīti ukte | katamā ca sā iti cet - munī rājagṛhasyaiva ityādi kathitam rājagṛhaṃ tu rājño gṛham rājaprasāda ityarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: The worship of the teacher was performed for the purpose of commencing the treatise. If one asks 'for what purpose?' — it is because it serves as a cause for generating reverence toward the teacher and the teaching. For those in whom reverence has arisen regarding the hearing of <s>Dharma</s>, reverence extends to <s>śravaṇa</s> (hearing), <s>cintana</s> (reflection), and <s>bhāvanā</s> (meditation). But for those in whom reverence has not arisen, this is not the case — and so the meaning of the reason is itself established. Furthermore, the worship of the teacher at the beginning of the treatise was performed for the purpose of demonstrating the way of refined conduct (<s>śiṣṭācāra</s>). This is indeed the custom of the virtuous and learned. When anyone undertakes a purposeful endeavor, by first prostrating to their chosen deity and then entering upon the distinguished purpose, the desired goal is quickly accomplished. Therefore, by this treatise-composer who follows that very tradition of good conduct, having first made obeisance by declaring the qualities of his own teacher at the commencement of the treatise, and then entering into the exposition of the treatise — here the purpose certainly exists. It is said: performing homage to the teacher at the beginning of a treatise is not fruitless; it serves the purpose of generating reverence toward the teacher and the teachings, and for no other reason. Thus, the worship of the teacher at the beginning of the treatise is well established. Therefore, why do others say that performing homage at the beginning of a treatise is purposeless? This has been stated to show the unestablished nature of their reason. The performance of homage for commencing the treatise is purposeful, like a treatise on medicine and the like, and is not like examining the teeth of a crow. Having prostrated to one's own teacher, 'I shall expound the verses of the treatise composed upon the <s>Śālistamba Sūtra</s>' — thus it is said. If one asks 'and what is that?' — it begins with '<s>Munī</s> (the Sage), of <s>Rājagṛha</s> itself' and so forth. <s>Rājagṛha</s> means the house of the king, that is, the royal palace.

body.text: gṛdhranāmakaparvate iti tu gṛdhrakūṭaparvate | tasmādeva saṃgītisūtre 'evaṃ mayā śrutam ityuktam | kasmācchrutamiti | tasmāduktam | bhagavataḥ ekasmin samaye iti ekasmin samaye | bhagavān tu bhagnavān iti bhagavān | kiṃ bhagnavān iti cet | tasmāduktam māracatuṣṭayam | kleśa-skandha-devaputra-mṛtyavo mārā ityākhyātāḥ | kathaṃ bhagnā iti? ucyate - pratipakṣajñānopalabdheḥ | darśana-bhāvanā-mārgāvatāranayena catuḥ smṛtyupasthānādisaptatriṃśadbodhipākṣikadharmabhāvanākrameṇa caturāryasatyabhāvanāvibhāvanatayā skandhatathatāparijñānena anitya-duḥkha-śūnya-nairātmyādīnām aviparīta-jñānānvitatvāt pudgaladharmayornairātmya-grāhyagrāhakābhāva-kalpanād 'idaṃ dhātutrayamapi cittamātram' iti avagamāt kleśajñeyāvaraṇa-rahitadvāreṇa kleśā bhagnāḥ | nitya-sukha-śuci-sātmyāviparyāsacatuṣṭayādirahitaḥ anuttaradharmakāya saṃyukto 'pratiṣṭhita nirvāṇopalabdheḥ skandhaṃ mṛtyumārañca jayati |
body.translated_text: "On the mountain called <s>Gṛdhra</s>" means on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) mountain. Therefore in the <s>Saṃgīti Sūtra</s> it is said "Thus have I heard." Why "heard"? Therefore it is said. "Of the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), at one time" means at one time. <s>Bhagavān</s> means one who has broken (<s>bhagnavān</s>). What has he broken? Therefore it is said: the fourfold <s>Māra</s> (demons). The <s>Māras</s> are declared to be: <s>kleśa</s> (afflictions), <s>skandha</s> (aggregates), <s>devaputra</s> (divine son), and <s>mṛtyu</s> (death). How are they broken? It is said — through the attainment of antidotal knowledge. By the method of entering the paths of seeing and cultivation, through the progressive cultivation of the thirty-seven <s>bodhipākṣika dharmas</s> (factors of awakening) beginning with the four <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness), through the realization by means of cultivating the four noble truths, through the full comprehension of the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), because of being pervaded by non-inverted knowledge of impermanence, suffering, emptiness, non-self and so forth, through the conceptual construction of the non-self of persons and <s>dharmas</s> and the absence of grasped and grasper, from the understanding that "this triple realm is mind-only" — through the gateway of being free from the obscurations of afflictions and knowable objects, the afflictions are broken. Being free from the four inversions of permanence, pleasure, purity, and self, united with the unsurpassed <s>dharmakāya</s> (truth body), through the attainment of non-abiding <s>nirvāṇa</s>, he conquers the <s>skandha</s> and <s>mṛtyu-māra</s> (death-demon).

body.text: sarvadharmān māyā-marīci-gandharvanagara-nirmāṇa-pratibimba-pratiśrutka-alātacakra-svapnavat svavabodhāt saṃkleśālayavijñāna-vāsanā-malāpagatatvācca abhūtasaṃkalpān samucchidya mahāmaitryādi-bāṇākṣepeṇa sasainyaṃ makaradhvajaṃ prahṛtya devaputramāraṃ parājayata | evaṃ caturmārabhañjanād bhagavān iti | punaścoktam -
body.translated_text: Through self-realization that all <s>dharmas</s> are like illusion, mirage, a <s>gandharva</s> city, magical creation, reflection, echo, a whirling firebrand, and a dream, and because the stains of <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impressions) in the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (storehouse consciousness) of defilement have been removed, having cut off false conceptualizations, having struck the banner-bearing <s>Makara</s> (Kāmadeva) together with his army by shooting the arrows of great <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and so forth, he defeats the <s>devaputra-māra</s> (demon of the divine son). Thus, because of shattering the four <s>Māras</s>, he is called <s>Bhagavān</s>. And further it is said —

body.text:
caturmārāribhagnatvād bhavatrayasamudgata-
bhāvyatītaparijñānād bhavastho bhagavāniti |
body.translated_text: Because of shattering the enemy of the four <s>Māras</s>, because of the full comprehension of past and future arising from the three realms of existence, one who abides in existence is called <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: tādṛśo bhagavān rājagṛhe gṛdhrakūṭaparvate viharatisma | kimartha tannagaraṃ rājagṛhamiti cet | ucyate - tannagaraṃ pūrvaṃ kuśīnagaram ityākhyātam | yadā tannagare kupitairamānuṣaiḥ punaḥ punaragniḥ kṣiptastadā rājāvagatya ādiśat, jñānino nāgarikāḥ | adya prabhṛti yasya gṛhaṃ prathamaṃ agninā dahyate, sa śītavanaṃ mahāśmaśānaṃ gatvā gṛhaṃ nirmāya vased ityājñātavān | tataśca karmapratyayavaśena ādau rājaprāsādo 'gniṃ prāptaḥ | tato rājā amātyānāhūyādiśat - jñānina amātyāḥ jānantu evaṃ, mayaiva tannayaprajñāpāt mayaiva tadatikramo mayi na śobhate, anayatvāt | jñānino mantriṇaḥ | śītavane mahāśmaśānamadhye rājaprāsādo nirmīyatām (ahaṃ) tatra gatvā vatsyāmi | tato rājño vacanamātreṇa sarvaistathā kṛtam |
body.translated_text: Such a <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) mountain in <s>Rājagṛha</s>. Why is that city called <s>Rājagṛha</s> (King's House)? It is said — that city was formerly known as <s>Kuśīnagara</s>. When enraged non-human beings repeatedly hurled fire upon that city, the king, understanding, decreed: "Know this, O wise citizens! From this day forward, whosoever's house is first burned by fire shall go to the <s>Śītavana</s> (Cool Grove) great cremation ground and, having built a house there, shall dwell there" — thus he commanded. Then, by the force of karmic conditions, the royal palace first caught fire. Then the king, summoning his ministers, decreed: "Know this, wise ministers! Since this regulation was proclaimed by me myself, its transgression by me is not fitting, as it would be improper. O wise counselors! Let a royal palace be constructed in the midst of the great cremation ground at <s>Śītavana</s>. I shall go there and dwell." Then, merely by the king's word, all did accordingly.

body.text: tadā prathamaṃ rājā tatra gatvā uvāsa | tataḥ parairuṣitatvād rājagṛham iti nāmopacaritam | tatra rājagṛha-mahānagarasya pūrvottarasīmāyāṃ gṛdhrakūṭanāmaka parvate 'sti | yasya parvatasya śikharo gṛdhraśirovat sa gṛdhrakūṭaparvata ityucyate | athavā pāpena māreṇa gṛdhrākāramabhinirmāya bhagavaccīvaraharaṇārambhe bhagavato 'dhiṣṭhānenā - sāmarthyāt tatraiva nikṣiptaṃ, taccīvaram adyāpi pāṣāṇībhūya catuṣpuṭitacīvaramiva avatiṣṭhate | tadupalakṣitaḥ parvato gṛdhrakūṭa ityucyate | muniḥ tadgṛdhrakūṭaparvate viharatisma | kimekākī eva? ucyate | na, bhikṣūṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ saṃghaiḥ sārdhaṃ vyavasthitaḥ | bhikṣūṇāṃ arthāt bhikṣusārdhamardhatrayodaśabhiḥ mahatā bhikṣusaṅghena bodhisattvānāṃ ca iti tu saṃbahulaiśca bodhisattva-mahāsattvaiḥ sārdham | vyavasthitastu utthāna-saṃcakramaṇa-vyavasthiti-śayanādi-caturvidha-caryayā vyavasthitaḥ | ko 'sā viti? muniḥ | munistu kāya-vāk-cittairmaunitvāt | kāya-vāk-cittāpravṛttermuniḥ | kutra na pravartate? tasmāduktam | kāya-vākcittaduścarite na pravartata ityartho darśitaḥ | atra maunitvān muniḥ | yuktārthārthāya daṇḍivaditi | api ca - kimarthaṃ sthāna-kāla-parivāra-nirdeśaḥ? ucyate - cakravartirājasādharmyāt | cakravartirājānām ācārastvevamākhyātaḥ -
body.translated_text: Then the king first went there and dwelt. Thereafter, because others also resided there, the name <s>Rājagṛha</s> (King's House) became current. There, on the northeastern boundary of the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, there is a mountain called <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak). The mountain whose peak resembles a vulture's head is called <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> mountain. Alternatively, the evil <s>Māra</s>, having magically created a vulture form, attempted to steal the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s robe, but by the power of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>adhiṣṭhāna</s> (blessing), it was fixed right there; that robe, even today, having turned to stone, remains as if a fourfold-folded robe. The mountain marked by that is called <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s>. The <s>Muni</s> (Sage) was dwelling on that <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> mountain. Was he alone? It is said: No, he was established together with assemblies of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) and <s>bodhisattvas</s>. "Of <s>bhikṣus</s>" means with a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty <s>bhikṣus</s>; "and of <s>bodhisattvas</s>" means together with many <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattvas</s> (great bodhisattva beings). "Established" means established in the fourfold conduct of standing, walking, sitting, and lying down. Who is he? The <s>Muni</s> (Sage). <s>Muni</s> means one who practices silence of body, speech, and mind. He is a <s>Muni</s> because of the non-engagement of body, speech, and mind. Where does he not engage? Therefore it is said: the meaning shown is that he does not engage in misconduct of body, speech, and mind. Here, because of silence, he is a <s>Muni</s>. Like a staff-bearer for the purpose of meaningful aims. Moreover — for what purpose is the indication of place, time, and retinue? It is said — in accordance with a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch). The conduct of <s>Cakravartin</s> kings is declared thus —

body.text: yadā brāhmaṇeṣu gṛhastheṣu ca anugrahādi kṛtaṃ tadā nivāsa-sthānaṃ grāma-nagarādi, yatra sthitvā tatkāryaṃ, sthānaṃ nirucyate | kasmin sthāne? amuke | ādhipatyaṃ pradarśayituṃ amātyādibhiḥ sārdham iti| kālastu pūrvāparāhṇakālaḥ | kāniti? brāhmaṇa-gṛhasthādīn | tasmāt bhagavato 'pi anuttaradharmacakravartirājatvāt sthāna-kāla-pārivārādaya uktāḥ | kutreti? rājagṛhe | ekasmin samaye tu prātaḥ kāle | kaiścit sārdhamiti?
body.translated_text: When acts of grace and so forth have been performed toward <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders, then the dwelling place such as a village or city where one stays to perform those duties is designated as the place. In which place? In such-and-such a place. To show sovereignty, together with ministers and others. The time is the forenoon or afternoon period. Which ones? <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, householders, and others. Therefore, because the <s>Bhagavān</s> is also an unsurpassed <s>Dharma-Cakravartin</s> (Dharma-wheel-turning king), the place, time, retinue, and so forth are stated. Where? In <s>Rājagṛha</s>. "At one time" means in the morning. Together with whom?

body.text: sārdhatrayodaśaśataiḥ bhikṣubhiḥ bodhisattvaiśca |
body.translated_text: With one thousand two hundred and fifty <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) and <s>bodhisattvas</s>.

body.text: kāniti bhikṣūn | kimuktamiti? śālistambakasūtram | punaścoktam -
body.translated_text: Which ones? The <s>bhikṣus</s>. What was spoken? The <s>Śālistamba Sūtra</s> (Rice Stalk Sūtra). And further it is said —

body.text:
kutra kaiścit samaṃ kvāpi kasmāt kasmai ca deśitam |
upadiśya ca tānyante ānandapadamīritam |
body.translated_text: Where, with whom, at some place, why, and to whom was it taught; and having instructed in those, at the end the state of <s>Ānanda</s> (bliss) is declared.

body.text: śālistambaṃ vilokya ca ityādi | śālistambaṃ vilokya dṛṣṭvā ityarthaḥ | hetupratyayasaṃbhūtam iti hetupratyayajanitam | tadutpādaka īśvarādiḥ ko 'pi anyo nāstītyabhiprāyaḥ | api coktam -
body.translated_text: "Having observed a rice stalk" and so forth. "Having observed a rice stalk" means having seen, that is the meaning. "Born from causes and conditions" means produced from <s>hetu</s> (causes) and <s>pratyaya</s> (conditions). The intended meaning is that there is no other producer such as <s>Īśvara</s> (God) or the like. Moreover it is said —

body.text: bījāderatiriktaṃ hi nānyad heturitīryate |
body.translated_text: It is declared that apart from the seed and so forth, there is no other cause.

body.text: pratyakṣādiviruddhatvād | bījādaṅkurādi janyate, īśvara-pradhāna-svabhāva-kālādirna hetuḥ | pratyakṣānumānābhyām anupalabhyamānatvād ākāśotpalavat |
body.translated_text: Because it contradicts direct perception and other means of valid knowledge. From the seed, a sprout and so forth are produced; <s>Īśvara</s> (God), <s>Pradhāna</s> (Primal Matter), <s>Svabhāva</s> (inherent nature), <s>Kāla</s> (Time), and so forth are not causes — because they are not apprehended by direct perception and inference, like a lotus in the sky.

body.text:
hetupratyayajaṃ tadvad dvādaśāṅgakramodgatam |
pratītyamiti yaḥ paśyet | ityuktam |
body.translated_text: That which is born from causes and conditions, arising in the sequence of the twelve links — whoever sees dependent arising, thus it is said.

body.text: hetupratyayābhyāṃ janito dharmaḥ pratītyasamutpādaḥ, dvādaśāṅgaḥ bhikṣurbhikṣuṇī anyo vā yaḥ kaścit kṛtādikaṃ ahetu-pratikūlahetu-virahitaṃ paśyati, sa
body.translated_text: The <s>dharma</s> born from <s>hetu</s> (causes) and <s>pratyaya</s> (conditions) is <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), having twelve links. Whichever <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk), <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> (nun), or any other person who sees what has been made and so forth as free from no-cause and contrary causes,

body.text:
dharmaṃ buddhaṃ ca paśyati |
ityuktvā nāyako bhikṣūn tūṣṇīṃ bhāvamavasthitaḥ |
body.translated_text: sees the <s>Dharma</s> and sees the <s>Buddha</s>. Having spoken thus, the Guide remained in silence.

body.text: aṣṭāṅgamāryadharmaṃ phaladharmādhigamasvabhāvatāṃ saskandhanirvāṇaṃ aśeṣa skandhābhidhānamapi ca yathāvat paśyati ityuktvā bhagavāṃstūṣṇīṃ bhāvamavasthitaḥ | tadā ityādi tu bhikṣuśāriputro bodhisattvaṃ maitreyam upasaṃkramyedaṃ paryapṛcchat | ityuktvā iti bhagavataḥ śāriputreṇa yatsūtraṃ śrutaṃ tad bhikṣūn uktvā upadiśya | nāyaka iti vividhopāyanayena sattvānām nayanatvān nāyakaḥ | tūṣṇīṃbhāvamavasthitaḥ samādhiṃ samāpadya viharati sm ityadhivacanam | bhikṣuḥ śāriputraḥ śrutvā ityuvāca bhikṣuḥ iti - kleśabhañjanād bhikṣuḥ | śāriputraḥ śrutvā iti tu bhagavataḥ śrutvā | sūtre tadāyuṣmān śāriputro maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo yatretyādinā deśitavān | gatvā maitreyasannidhau tu yatra bodhisattvo maitreyo dine sadāvasthitaḥ, tatra gatvā, ubhau śilātale upaviśatām | athāyuṣmān śāriputro maitreyaṃ bodhisattvametadavocat -
body.translated_text: He sees the noble <s>Dharma</s> of the eightfold path, the nature of attaining the fruit-<s>dharma</s>, <s>nirvāṇa</s> together with the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), and also the complete designation of the <s>skandhas</s> as they truly are — having spoken thus, the <s>Bhagavān</s> remained in silence. Then the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Śāriputra</s> approached the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> and asked this. "Having spoken" means that <s>Śāriputra</s>, having heard the <s>sūtra</s> from the <s>Bhagavān</s>, spoke it to the <s>bhikṣus</s> and instructed them. "Guide" (<s>Nāyaka</s>) — because he leads beings by various skillful means, he is the Guide. "Remained in silence" is a designation meaning he entered <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) and dwelt therein. The <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Śāriputra</s>, having heard, spoke thus — "<s>bhikṣu</s>" because of shattering afflictions. "<s>Śāriputra</s> having heard" means having heard from the <s>Bhagavān</s>. In the <s>sūtra</s>, then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> taught the <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> with "where" and so forth. Having gone to the presence of <s>Maitreya</s> — where the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> always remained during the day — having gone there, the two sat upon a stone slab. Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said this to the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> —

body.text:
tathāgate 'dya maitreya uktyarthaṃ na vibhajya ca |
tṛṣṇīṃbhāve sthite cātra tadartho gamyate katham | ityuktam |
body.translated_text: Today, O <s>Maitreya</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, without analyzing the meaning of what was spoken, has remained in silence; how then is that meaning to be understood? Thus it is said.

body.text: adya maitreya ityuktvā bhikṣūn bhagavān śālistambopamādeśanayā yaduktam - maitreya! sugatoktasūtrāntārthaḥ katamaḥ? bhagavatāpyartho na vibhaktaḥ | sarvajñagocara-viṣayāṇāmapi sarvaśrāvaka-pratyekabuddha-viṣayātikrāntatvāt pratītyasamutpādaḥ katamaḥ? dharmaḥ katamaḥ? buddhaḥ katamaḥ? ityādi apṛcchat | ayameva sūtrakāreṇa sūtrasambandha uktam -
body.translated_text: Having said "Today, O <s>Maitreya</s>," the <s>Bhagavān</s> spoke to the <s>bhikṣus</s> through the teaching by the analogy of the rice stalk — "O <s>Maitreya</s>! What is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> spoken by the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One)?" The meaning was not analyzed by the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Because even the domain and scope of omniscient knowledge transcends the domain of all <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones) — what is <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination)? What is <s>Dharma</s>? What is <s>Buddha</s>? And so forth, he asked. This connection of the <s>sūtra</s> is stated by the <s>sūtrakāra</s> (author of the verse treatise) —

body.text: kiṃ pratītyaṃ ca dharmaḥ kaḥ buddho 'pi katamastathā | ityuktam |
body.translated_text: What is dependent origination, and what is <s>Dharma</s>, and likewise what is the <s>Buddha</s>? Thus it is said.

body.text: kathaṃ ca pratītyasamutpādaṃ paśyan dharmaṃ paśyati | dharmaṃ paśyan buddhaṃ paśyati? iti tu
body.translated_text: And how does one who sees <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) see the <s>Dharma</s>? And how does one who sees the <s>Dharma</s> see the <s>Buddha</s>? This indeed

body.text:
pratītyaṃ tu kathaṃ dṛṣṭvā dharmaṃ buddhaṃ ca paśyati |
sandeho me 'tra brūhīti ūce śārisuto 'jitam |
body.translated_text: 'But how does one, having seen dependent [origination], see the <s>Dharma</s> and the <s>Buddha</s>? I have a doubt here—please explain,' said <s>Śāriputra</s> to <s>Ajita</s>.

body.text: sthaviraśāriputraḥ tatsandehotpādād ajitamāha | ajitastu maitreyaḥ | kiṃ viśeṣaṇako maitreyaḥ?
body.translated_text: The elder <s>Śāriputra</s>, due to the arising of that doubt, addressed <s>Ajita</s>. <s>Ajita</s> is indeed <s>Maitreya</s>. What is the distinguishing quality of <s>Maitreya</s>?

body.text: bhāvātmikā hi maitrī syān maitreyo 'brūta nirṇayam |
body.translated_text: <s>Maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) is indeed of the nature of being; <s>Maitreya</s> spoke the definitive conclusion.

body.text: maitrī samādhyanvitatvāt supratiṣṭhatvāt maitrī bhāvātmikā | nirṇayamiti tu niścayaḥ | abrūteti udīritavān | kamiti cet? śāriputram | kimuktamiti cet anna bhagavatā ityādi uktam | yo bhikṣavaḥ pratītyasamutpādam ityādi | katama pratītyasamutpādo nāma | yadidam - avidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārāḥ | saṃskārapratyayaṃ vijñānam | vijñānapratyayaṃ nāmarūpam | nāmarūpapratyayaṃ ṣaḍāyatanam | ṣaḍāyatanapratyayaḥ sparśaḥ | sparśapratyayā vedanā | vedanāpratyayā tṛṣṇā| tṛṣṇāpratyayamupādānam |
body.translated_text: Because <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) is pervaded by <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration) and well-established, <s>maitrī</s> is of the nature of being. '<s>Nirṇaya</s>' means certainty. 'Abrūta' means 'he uttered.' To whom? To <s>Śāriputra</s>. If asked 'what was said?'—it was said: 'This was [taught] by the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One)' and so forth. 'O <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), [whoever sees] <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination)' and so forth. What is <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination)? It is as follows: conditioned by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) arise <s>saṃskāras</s> (volitional formations); conditioned by <s>saṃskāras</s> arises <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness); conditioned by <s>vijñāna</s> arises <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form); conditioned by <s>nāmarūpa</s> arise the <s>ṣaḍāyatanas</s> (six sense bases); conditioned by the <s>ṣaḍāyatanas</s> arises <s>sparśa</s> (contact); conditioned by <s>sparśa</s> arises <s>vedanā</s> (feeling); conditioned by <s>vedanā</s> arises <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving); conditioned by <s>tṛṣṇā</s> arises <s>upādāna</s> (clinging).

body.text: upādānapratyayo bhavaḥ | bhavapratyayā jātiḥ | jātipratyayaṃ jarāmaraṇam | jarāmaraṇapratyayāḥ śoka-parideva-duḥkha-daurmanasyopāyāsāḥ sambhavanti | evamasya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya samudayo bhavati | ayamucyate pratītyasamutpādo bhagavatā | tatra pratītyasamutpādo nāma sahetukaḥ sapratyayo nāhetuko nāpratyayaḥ |
body.translated_text: Conditioned by <s>upādāna</s> (clinging) arises <s>bhava</s> (becoming); conditioned by <s>bhava</s> arises <s>jāti</s> (birth); conditioned by <s>jāti</s> arise <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> (aging-and-death); conditioned by <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> arise sorrow, lamentation, suffering, mental anguish, and despair. Thus arises this entire great mass of suffering. This is called <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) by the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One). Therein, <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> means that which has causes and has conditions, and is not without cause or without conditions.

body.text: tasmāt pratītyasamutpāda ityucyate | api ca - avidyādibhavāṅgādīnām ayaṃ sambhavakramaḥ kathamavagantavyaḥ? lakṣaṇaṃ katamat? karma ca katamad iti cet? ucyate | tatra pratītyasamutpādo dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāmutpanno 'vagantavyaḥ | katamābhyāṃ dvābhyām? ucyate? hetūpanibandhataḥ pratyayopanibandhataśca | sa ca pratītyasamutpādo bāhya ādhyātmikaśca pṛthaktvād dvividho vyavasthāpitaḥ | kathamiti? ucyate | " bījādaṅkurotpādāt phalotpādaparyantam | bīje sati aṅkuraḥ prādurbhavati phalaprādurbhāvaśca | asati ca bīje aṅkurānutpādāt, na hi phalotpāda iti | bījasya naivaṃ bhavati ahamaṅkuramabhinirvartayāmīti | aṅkurasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati ahaṃ bījenābhinirvartita iti | evaṃ yāvat puṣpasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati phalamabhinirvartayāmīti | phalasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati ahamaṅkura-puṣpābhyām abhinirvartita iti | atha punarbīje sati aṅkurāt phalaparyantaṃ prādurbhavati | evaṃ bāhyapratītyasamutpādaḥ pratyayopanibandho draṣṭavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therefore it is called <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination). Moreover—how should the order of arising of the limbs of existence beginning with <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) be understood? What is their characteristic? And what is their action? It is said: Therein, <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> should be understood as arising from two causes. Which two? It is said: from the binding of causes (<s>hetu</s>) and from the binding of conditions (<s>pratyaya</s>). And that <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> is established as twofold—external and internal—due to their distinctness. How? It is said: From the seed arises the sprout, up to the production of fruit. When the seed exists, the sprout appears, and the fruit also appears. When the seed does not exist, since the sprout does not arise, there is no production of fruit either. The seed does not think thus: 'I produce the sprout.' Nor does the sprout think thus: 'I have been produced by the seed.' Likewise, even the flower does not think: 'I produce the fruit.' Nor does the fruit think: 'I have been produced by the sprout and the flower.' But rather, when the seed exists, from the sprout up to the fruit appears. Thus external <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) should be viewed as the binding of conditions.

body.text: bāhyapratītyasamutpādaḥ pratyayopanibandhaḥ kathaṃ draṣṭavyaḥ? ucyate | ṣaṇṇāṃ dhātūnāṃ samavāyāt | katameṣāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ dhātūnāmiti | yadidaṃ pṛthivyādi ca kālaśca | evaṃ bāhyapratītyasamutpādaḥ pratyayopanibandho draṣṭavyaḥ | bījaṃ pṛthivyādau kiṃ hitaṃ kṛtvā hetoḥ pratyayaṃ matamiti | pṛthivyādi tu saṃdhāraṇamityādi, snehanaṃ, pācanaṃ, nirharaṇam, anāvaraṇaṃ pariṇāmanāṃ ca kramaśaḥ karoti | asatsveṣu na bhavati | yadāvikalo bhavati, tataḥ sarveṣāṃ samavāyād tadbhavati | pṛthivyādau rnaivaṃ bhavati vayaṃ bījasaṃdhāraṇādi karomīti | bījasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati ahaṃ eteṣāṃ pratyayena saṃdhāraṇādi kāryeṇa hitaṃ karomi | atha punaḥ pṛthivyādiṣu satsu bījādaṅkurādi prādurbhavati, asatsu ca na bhavati | tasmādeva sūtrakāreṇa uktam |
body.translated_text: How should external <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) as the binding of conditions be viewed? It is said: through the convergence of six <s>dhātus</s> (elements). Which six elements? Namely, earth and so forth, and time. Thus should external <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> as the binding of conditions be viewed. What benefit does the seed gain from earth and so forth as cause and condition? Earth and so forth perform, respectively: sustaining, moistening, ripening, extracting, non-obstruction, and transformation. When these are absent, it does not occur. When nothing is lacking, then from the convergence of all, that [sprout] comes into being. Earth and so forth do not think: 'We perform the sustaining of the seed and so forth.' Nor does the seed think: 'I, through the condition of these, perform the beneficial function of sustaining and so forth.' But rather, when earth and so forth are present, from the seed the sprout and so forth appear, and when they are absent, they do not. Therefore it was stated by the <s>sūtrakāra</s> (author of the sūtra):

body.text: dvādaśāṅgamavidyādimaraṇāntaṃ yathākramam |
body.translated_text: The twelve limbs, beginning with <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and ending with death, in due order—

body.text: ityādi | bhavāṅgo yeṣāmavidyādimaraṇāntam asti, te avidyādi maraṇaparyantāḥ |
body.translated_text: And so forth. Those whose limbs of existence extend from <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) to death—they are those extending from <s>avidyā</s> through to death as the terminus.

body.text: tasmāttarhi bhavantyeva duḥkhaskandhā hi kevalam | tasmād iti tu avidyādi kramaśaḥ prādurbhavati |
body.translated_text: Therefore indeed, the aggregates of suffering arise as merely [that]. 'Therefore' means that beginning with <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), [each link] appears in due order.

body.text: duḥkhaskandhastu duḥkha-samūhaḥ | kevalamiti ātmātmīyaviyuktaḥ | bhavati iti tu utpadyate |
body.translated_text: <s>Duḥkhaskandha</s> (aggregate of suffering) means the mass of suffering. '<s>Kevala</s>' (mere) means devoid of self and what belongs to self. '<s>Bhavati</s>' means it is produced.

body.text: dharmaścāṣṭāṅgiko mārgaḥ phalaṃ nirvāṇamucyate | ityuktam |
body.translated_text: And the <s>Dharma</s> is the eightfold path; the fruit is called <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. Thus it was said.

body.text: dharmastu svalakṣaṇadhāraṇād dharmaḥ | aṣṭāṅgamārga iti tu mithyādṛṣṭi-mithyāsaṃkalpa-mithyāvāk-mithyākarmānta-mithyājīva-mithyāvyāyāma-mithyā-smṛti-mithyāsamādhayaḥ | tatra mithyādṛṣṭiriti mithyādarśanam | pañcadṛṣṭayastu satkāya-anta-dṛṣṭi-śīla-mithyāśceti | etāḥ sarvā api mithyāśravaṇacintanādiṣu praviṣṭāḥ | tasmāt kudṛṣṭitvāt mithyā mārgācaraṇena aniṣṭavipākābhinirvartitatvāt hetu-karma-phalāni apavādāropākāreṇa praviṣṭatvān mithyādṛṣṭiriti | tatpratikūlatvāt samyakdṛṣṭiḥ mārgāṅga eva vyavasthāpitā | yoniśaḥ sthita-samyakśravaṇa-cintanādayaḥ śraddhāpūrvagatvāt hetu-phala-satya-ratna-karmaphaladi-bhāvadarśanaṃ hi samyakdṛṣṭiḥ | samyakmārgopayogād abhīṣṭaphalābhinirhāratvād anitya-duḥkha-śūnya-nairātmyā-dyākāreṇa praviṣṭa tvāt samyakdṛṣṭiriti |
body.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> is so called because it bears (<s>dhāraṇa</s>) its own characteristic (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>). The eightfold path (<s>aṣṭāṅgamārga</s>) consists of: <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> (wrong view), <s>mithyāsaṃkalpa</s> (wrong intention), <s>mithyāvāk</s> (wrong speech), <s>mithyākarmānta</s> (wrong action), <s>mithyājīva</s> (wrong livelihood), <s>mithyāvyāyāma</s> (wrong effort), <s>mithyāsmṛti</s> (wrong mindfulness), and <s>mithyāsamādhi</s> (wrong concentration). Therein, <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> means wrong seeing. The five [wrong] views are: <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (view of the perishable collection), <s>antadṛṣṭi</s> (extreme view), <s>dṛṣṭi</s> (speculative view), <s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s> (adherence to rites and rituals), and <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> (wrong view). All of these are included in wrong hearing, contemplation, and so forth. Therefore, because of being wrong views, through practicing the wrong path, because of producing undesirable results, because of entering through the mode of denial and superimposition regarding causes, actions, and fruits—it is called <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> (wrong view). Because it is the opposite of that, <s>samyakdṛṣṭi</s> (right view) is established as a limb of the path itself. Properly established right hearing, contemplation, and so forth, preceded by faith—seeing the reality of causes, fruits, truths, the [three] jewels, <s>karma</s> and its fruits, and so forth—this is <s>samyakdṛṣṭi</s> (right view). Through the application of the right path, because of accomplishing the desired fruit, because of entering through the aspects of impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self—it is called <s>samyakdṛṣṭi</s> (right view).

body.text: tatra mithyāsaṃkalpaḥ-saṅkalpa-viparyayaḥ | saṅkalpo gocara-viṣayālambanānām adhivacanam | gocaramiti ṣaḍviṣayā rūpādayaḥ | mithyeti viparyāsaḥ | nitya-sukha-śuci-ātmādyākārālambanād rāga-dveṣa-mohavṛddheḥ mithyāsaṃkalpaḥ | tadviparītaḥ samyaksaṃkalpaḥ | samyaṅnāma aviparyāsaḥ | saṃkalpastu kriyā, cintanaṃ ca idamidaṃ kariṣya iti ādau citte nidhāya kāya-vāk-citta-caryākuśalaḥ, rāga-dveṣa-moha-rahita-svabhāvaḥ, anitya-duḥkha-śūnya-nairātmyādisu niyojito yo yoniśomana sikārayogaḥ (sa) samyaṅmārgāṅgam ityucyate | mithyāvāgiti durvacanam | svaparavisaṃvādākārapravṛttā yā vāk sā mithyāvāk | rāga-dveṣa-mohādyākārasambaddhatvād ātmastuti-parapaṃsana-svabhāvena pravṛttā, caturvidha-vāgdoṣamiśritā samyak-satya-tathatā-sarvadharmaprahīṇā, rāja-caura-strī-gṛhastha-janakathāsvarūpā tuccha-vyarthatā-bahulā sarvāryajana-ninditatvān mithyāvāg ityucyate | tatpratikūlatvāt svaparāvisaṃvādākārā rāga-dveṣa-mohādi-rahita-svabhāvā, caturvidhavāgdoṣarahita-tvāt satya-samyak-tathatānusāriṇī, catuḥsatyānukūlakaraṇā, sarvakuśaladharmasaṃgrahā hita-paricchinna-svarūpatvād ātmastuti-parapaṃsanavihīnā anitya-duḥkha-śūnya(tā)-nairātmyādi-rūpeṇa pravṛtteḥ sarvārya janāvisaṃvādinī samyaṅmārgānusāritvāt samyagvāg ityucyate |
body.translated_text: Therein, <s>mithyāsaṃkalpa</s> (wrong intention) is the reversal of intention. <s>Saṃkalpa</s> (intention) is a designation for objects, domains, and supports of cognition. 'Object' refers to the six sense objects: form and so forth. 'Wrong' means perverted. Due to grasping at objects under the aspects of permanence, pleasure, purity, and self, and because of the increase of desire, hatred, and delusion—this is <s>mithyāsaṃkalpa</s> (wrong intention). The opposite of that is <s>samyaksaṃkalpa</s> (right intention). 'Right' means non-perverted. <s>Saṃkalpa</s> is action and contemplation—first placing in the mind 'I shall do this and that,' being skilled in bodily, verbal, and mental conduct, of a nature free from desire, hatred, and delusion, engaged in impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self—such proper application of the mind is called a limb of the right path. <s>Mithyāvāk</s> (wrong speech) means harmful speech. Speech that proceeds in the manner of deceiving oneself and others is <s>mithyāvāk</s> (wrong speech). Because it is bound to the aspects of desire, hatred, and delusion, proceeding with the nature of self-praise and disparagement of others, mixed with the four kinds of verbal faults, having abandoned right truth and suchness regarding all <s>dharmas</s>, being of the nature of idle talk about kings, thieves, women, and householders, full of triviality and meaninglessness, censured by all noble persons—therefore it is called <s>mithyāvāk</s> (wrong speech). Because it is the opposite of that—speech that does not deceive oneself and others, of a nature free from desire, hatred, and delusion, free from the four kinds of verbal faults, conforming to truth, rightness, and suchness, conducive to the four truths, gathering all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, of a beneficial and well-defined nature, devoid of self-praise and disparagement of others, proceeding in the form of impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self, not deceiving any noble persons, following the right path—it is called <s>samyagvāk</s> (right speech).

body.text: mithyā-karmānto viparītakarmakaraṇam | karmeti kāya-vāk-citta-duṣkṛta-bījavapanād akṣayavipākaphalābhinirvartita-svabhāvākuśala-karmānta-kāritvāt kṣārādidoṣasaṃsṛṣṭakukṣetre kubījavapanavad anabhīṣṭavipākābhi-nirvartitatvāt paṃsanīyaḥ karmāntastu mithyākarmānta ityucyate | karmarati-nidrārati-vādaratyādi-svabhāvaṃ mithyākarma ityucyate | svaparāspṛṣṭa duḥkhapratiṣṭhādhārasvabhāvam, tadviruddhatvāt samyakkarmāntaḥ | aviparītakarmakṛttvāt kāya-vāk-citta-sukṛtabījavapanāt satkṣetrasadṛśasukṛtakarmakṣetre 'bhīṣṭavipākābhinirvartita-vidhi-pravṛtteḥ, anitya-duḥkha-śūnya(tā)-nairātmyādi-svarūpeṇa pravṛtteḥ, samyak karmānta-kāritvāt, samyak karmāntaḥ, sanmārgānusaraṇatvāt samyakmārga ityucyate |
body.translated_text: <s>Mithyākarmānta</s> (wrong action) means performing perverted actions. 'Action' (<s>karma</s>)—because of sowing seeds of bodily, verbal, and mental misdeeds, because of being an unwholesome doer of actions that produce inexhaustible fruits of results, like sowing bad seeds in a field contaminated with alkaline and other defects, because of producing undesirable results—such action is called <s>mithyākarmānta</s> (wrong action). Action whose nature is delight in [mere] activity, delight in sleep, delight in disputes, and so forth is called wrong action (<s>mithyākarma</s>). That whose nature is the foundation and basis for suffering untouched by oneself and others—because it is the opposite of that, it is <s>samyakkarmānta</s> (right action). Because of performing non-perverted actions, because of sowing seeds of bodily, verbal, and mental good deeds, like good seeds sown in a good field of well-performed actions, because of proceeding according to the method that produces desired results, because of proceeding in the nature of impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self, because of performing right action—it is <s>samyakkarmānta</s> (right action); because of following the true path, it is called the right path (<s>samyakmārga</s>).

body.text: mithyājīvastu viparītājīvaḥ | kapaṭa-lapana-naiṣpeśikatva-naimittikatvena pravṛtya avipanna-kāya-vāgādyupajīvikayā puruṣa-stryādi-nimittadeśanena astra-aśva-kāvya-cikitsāparīkṣā-saṃkhyā-gṛhasthaparīkṣā-kumāraparīkṣā-sāmudrika-lakṣaṇaparīkṣā-nimittajñānādau svaparavisaṃvādarūpeṇa pravṛtteḥ tannayena cīvara-piṇḍādi-sādhanānuvṛttyā vihārastu mithyājīva ityucyate | tatpratikūlatvāt samyagājīvastu mārgāṅgamityucyate | samyak tu vidyāviyukta-kāya-vāk-cittapravṛtyā cīvarādi-sādhanam, tannayena ājīvaḥ samyagājīvānusaraṇatvāt svaparāvi-saṃvādasvarūpākāratvād āryamārgānuvartitvāt, samyagājīvastu mārgasyāṅgameva vyavasthāpitaḥ | mithyāvyāyāmaḥ-vyāyāmastu prayatnaḥ | mithyā iti viparyāsaḥ | asatkāya-vāk-citta-pracāraiḥ svaparāpakāro, yuddhādiprajñaptiḥ, dūtādigamanaṃ, cāraḥ, utpātaḥ, nikṣepotkṣepāpohānapoha-sandhi-vidhinotpādaḥ, kṣetra-vidyā-vyāpāra-rājyādi-svaparāpakāri-kāya-vāk-citta-pravṛtta-vividhākārārabdhāḥ kriyāḥ prayatnāśca mithyāvyāyāma ityucyante | tadviruddhabhūtatvāt samyakvyāyāmaḥ |

samyak-vyāyāmastu mārgāṅgaeva vyavasthāpitaḥ | yā kāyavākcittacaryāsvaparopakāra-mātrakuśalapravṛtyā āryamārgam anusarati sā samyagvyāyāmatvāt samyakvyāyāmaḥ | sa mārgāṅgameva ucyate | mithyā smṛtiriti kutsanīyā smṛtiḥ mithyāsmṛtiḥ | smṛtistu smaraṇam | iyam mithyā smṛtiścāpi bhūtatvān mithyāsmṛtiḥ | kālatrayaviṣayeṣu pūrvahāsa-ānandānubhūta-rūpa-śabda-gandha-rasa-sparśādīn anusmaran anukathanam | tatrāpi adhyavasāna-anurāga-pratighatādi-paridveṣatvāt svaparāpakārakāritvād, abhīṣṭavipākasambaddhatvācca mithyā-nimitta-manasikārastu mithyāsmṛtiḥ | tadviruddhatvāt samyak-smṛtistu mārgāṅgameva kathitā | guṇānusmaraṇaṃ pūrvīkṛtya buddha-dharma-saṃgha-śīla-tyāga-devādyanusmaraṇaṃ samyaksmṛtiḥ mārgāṅgam eva ucyate | samādhikāryaṃ-samādhistu dhyānam | sarvathā samādhāya dhāraṇatvāt samādhiḥ | sa tu mithyāpi san, samādhirapi bhūtatvān mithyāsamādhiḥ mithyeti tu viparyayaḥ | īśvara-svabhāva-kāla-pradhānādhyātmātmādyasatsu tatrālambanapūrvakaṃ yaccitta-spharaṇaṃ syāt, api tu-rūpādi-bāhyavastūni anitya-duḥkha-śūnya-nairātmyākārīṇi nitya-sukha-śucyātma dṛṣṭayāditayā adhyavasīya teṣu ālambanapūrvakaṃ yaccittaspharaṇam, sādhyavasāya pūrvakaṃ yaccittādhiṣṭhānaṃ tattu mithyāsamādhirityucyate | tadviruddhaṃ cittādhiṣṭhānaṃ samyaksamādhirityucyate | skandha dhātvāyatanātmātmīyatāśūnyādiṣu anitya-duḥkha-śūnya(tā)-nairātmyādyākārapūrvakaṃ cittapratiṣṭhānam | cittaikāgratā tu samyak samādhirityucyate | sarvadharmasamatāpratipatteḥ samādhiḥ | cittaikāgratā ekālambanatvañceti | adhivacanam | sa samyak-samādhirmārgāṅgameva ucyate | evam yaḥ pratītyasamutpādaṃ paśyati sa dharmaṃ paśyati |

darśanādyaṣṭasetvaṅgaṃ hetudvādaśapūrvagam |
viśuddhātmā hi yaḥ paśyed dharmatathyaṃ sa paśyati |

phalaṃ tuṃ śrāmaṇyaphalam | tatprāptistu sākṣātkaraṇam | sarvasaṃkleśālaya-vijñānabījavāsanāmalāpagatatvād āśrayaparāvṛttimayaṃ manogocarācintyā-prameyaguṇamaṇyalaṅkṛtāyāḥ svaparādhīnātmaka pratyātmavedyasarvasattvārthanirantarānābhoga kṛtātma-sarvaprapañcarahitāyāḥ śamathavipaśyanā-yuganaddha-sarvadharma-tathatāyāḥ adhigamatvāt kleśa-jñeyāvaraṇagirigahvaravanamūla-vidahanasvabhāvatānuttarasamyak-saṃphalaṃ śaikṣajñānaṃ tu phala dharma ityucyate |
atha śālistamba-vibhāṣāyā dvitīyaṃ paṭalam |

nirvāṇaṃ nāma sopadhiśeṣa-nirupadhiśeṣa-svabhāvatāpratiṣṭhitanirvāṇamityuktam | ajaram, amaram, atāpaṃ, sthiraṃ, śāntaṃ, nityam, asaṃhāryam, akṣayātmakam, ādimadhyāntarahitam advayaṃ dhātutrayavirahitaṃ kāya-vāk-cittakarmasamatikrāntaṃ maṇiratnarājavividharūpasadṛśaṃ guṇamaṇivividhaprabhābhiḥ nirantaraṃ jagadarthakāri śāntaṃ, dharmātmaka-kāya-bhūtaṃ nirvāṇaṃ manyate |
sarvasyādhigamādevaṃ dharmajaṃ buddhameva ca |
evaṃ tadvat-saṃkleśa-vyavadānātmaka-sarvadharmāṇāṃ dharma-tathatāyāḥ yathāsthitivadavagatatvād buddha ityucyate | dharmajaṃ nāma dharmebhyo janitatvād dharmajam | dharmeṇa janitam ityadhivacanam |
tathoktamāryaṃ dṛṣṭatvād yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati |

tatheti buddhamiti tathoktatvāt, tādṛśo bhagavān | āryaṃ dṛṣṭatvāditi jñānacakṣuṣā | āryastu lokottaraḥ | paśyatīti cakṣuṣā | yaḥ paśyatīti yaḥ pratītyasamutpādaṃ dharmañcaivaṃ paśyati sa dharmajaḥ, dharmajatvād buddhaṃ paśyatīti bhāṣyate |

tatrātra pratītyasamutpādaḥ kīdṛśa ukta iti cet | yaḥ pratītyasamutpādam idamityādi | prāṇādirahitād yaśca iti tu yaḥ pratītyasamutpādaṃ satataṃ prāṇādirahitaṃ prāṇarahitam, apaśyad yuktyanumānābhyāṃ caryāṃ, māpanam, kalpanām, upaparīkṣaṇañca karoti, satatamajīvamiti tu nirjīvam | ajīvaṃ ārhatā evaṃ kalpayanti | imāni sarvāṇi bāhyābhyantarāṇi vastūni sajīvāni indriyānvitāni | tasmāt sarvāścaitāḥ bhūmayaḥ sūkṣmaprāṇibhiḥ pūrṇāḥ | tasmāt sarve prāṇino jantūn bhakṣanti | ye prāṇinaḥ prāṇino na bhakṣanti te prāṇinastu mokṣaṃ prāpnuvantīti ucyate | tasmāt tannirākaraṇāya ajīva-nirjīvetyādi uktam | ajīva iti nirjīvaḥ, niṣprāṇasyādhivacanam, hetupratyayotpādadharmitvāt | hetustu bījādi | pratyayaśca pṛthivyādi | te 'pi parasparamanyonyakalpanā-parikalpanā-vikalpa-rahitvāt tṛṇa-vṛkṣa-bhitti-dharmasadṛśā acalāḥ niṣkriyāśca tasmāt prāṇādirahitatvād ajīvāḥ | parasparaṃ hetupratyayopanibaddhajā anyonye cācetanāḥ | kriyā karmāpyavabhāsate |

hetupratyayasantatiriyam anāditaḥ pravṛttā | yathājīvakānām ārhatānāṃ vṛkṣā sacetanāḥ santi, calatvāt, suptatvāt, chinne 'pi utpādatvāditi, yā vyavahāraprajñaptistādṛśī nāsti | bāhyavastuṣu sūryasya candrasya ca sparśavaśena layo vistaraśca anumīyete | kva teṣāṃ śayanotthānam? vāyusañcāravaśād vṛkṣa-śākhādi-kampanānumānāt teṣāṃ gamanāgamanaṃ kuta upalabhyate | artho 'siddha eva | chinne utpāda iti ayam artho 'siddha eva iti darśayitum ucyate | yadi so 'pi sacetanaḥ syat, kasmāt chedanāvasthāyāṃ prāṇātipattītyādi duḥkhaṃ nānubhavati | anicchādicaryāṃ prārthanādiṃ vā tato 'nyatragamanaṃ vālpamapi na kurvanti | chinne utpādatvāt sacetanatvābhyupagamaścet, tarhi yacchede 'nutpādaḥ, tannivartanād acetanatvameva syāt | sacetanānām aṅga-pratyaṅgādicchedānutpāda-dharmitvād acetanatāyā eva prasaṅgo jāyate | tasmāt taddhetvartho 'siddha eva | tasmādajīvaṃ, nirjīvam itīdaṃ vyavasthitam | yathāvadaviparītamiti ahetoḥ pratikūlahetorviyuktatvāt | ajātamiti tu janyajanakarahitatvāt | abhūtamiti śāśvatocchedarahitatvāt | akṛtamiti tu kartṛrahitatvāt | ābhyantarakartṛpuruṣeśvarādipravṛtti-saṃskāra-rahitattvācca | apratighamiti tu anāvaraṇasvabhāvatvāt | anālambanamiti tu ālambyālambanarahitatvāt | vyupaśamasvabhāvamiti tu karmakleśarahitatvāt | ekāntaśamasvabhāvamiti sarvaprapañcarahitam sarvakalpanājālarahitam | satatasthitam, abhayam utpādavināśarahitañca | ya etādṛṅnayena dharmamapi paśyati | vyupaśāntyanta-saṃyutam ityuktam | vyupaśāntyantamiti tu upaśamam ante darśayituṃ vyupaśamaparyantam | yastu etādṛśanayena dharmaṃ satatam ajīvādisvabhāvaṃ paśyati |
pratītyaṃ dharmabuddhau ca śuddhibuddhayā hi paśyati |

so 'nuttaradharmaśarīraṃ buddhaṃ paśyati | iti bhagavatā uktam | ityasyārthastu yaḥ paśyati | āryadharmamabhisaṃbudhya iti tu yo pāpadharmāṇāṃ pāre arthāt dūre sa āryaḥ | teṣāṃ dharma āryadharmaḥ, samyakdṛṣṭirityādiḥ | abhisaṃbudhyeti abhimukhe ekāgratākaraṇāt sākṣātkaraṇācca samādhiprāpterityadhivacanam | samyagjñānopanayenaiva iti samyagaviparyayeṇa sarvadharmanairātmyatathatāvagamatvāt | anuttaramiti tatpūrvaṃ viśiṣṭadharmasya abhāvaḥ, tasmāt tad evānuttaramityuktam | dharmakāya iti dharmakāya eva dharmakāyaḥ, niśādā-putravat | buddha iti dharmāvabodhāt | tathāpi yaḥ pratītyasamutpādaṃ paśyati sa dharmakṛtānuttarabodhyaśaikṣasvabhāvatāṃ paśyati | yena sa āryajñānagocaradharmaṃ tādṛśaṃ svayathāvad abhisaṃbodheḥ dharmajñaḥ, dharmanirmāṇaṃ dharmadarśanam buddhadarśanam iti bhagavatā uktam | pratītyasamutpādalakṣaṇaṃ bhedavyavasthāpanārthaṃ pratītyalakṣaṇaṃ tāvad ityuktam | kasmāt pratītyasamutpāda ucyate iti cet | tasmāduktam -
sahetvādipadānvitam |
sahetukaḥ sapratyaya (ucyate) nāhetuko nāpratyayaḥ | bhagavatā pratītyasamutpādalakṣaṇaṃ saṃkṣepeṇoktam, etatpratyayasyaiva phalam | tasmāduktam |
buddhotpādo bhavenno vā sthiteyaṃ dharmatā yataḥ |

hetupratyaya-pravāho 'vicchinnaḥ | hetuphalamavicchinnaṃ anyonyaṃ pravartate | atrāhetuḥ pratikūlahetuḥ vā pravartako nivartako vā ko 'pi nāsti | tasmāt tathāgatānāmutpādādvā anutpādād vā dharmato dharmasthitito dharmaniyamataśca eṣa pravāhaḥ, ityuktam | yadi pratyayarahitena ekenaiva hetunā bhāvā utpadya tiṣṭhanti, yadi pratyayo 'pi hetumanapekṣya kiñcidutpādayituṃ samarthaḥ cettadā te sthitā asthitā iti vaktuṃ yujyeta, teṣāmutpādaḥ phalodbhavo 'pi nāhetor na cāpratyayāt tathāgatānāmutpādo vānutpādo vā eṣā dharmatā dharmasthitatā ca āditaḥ pravartete ||

tadyathā - pratītyasamutpādasya dharma etatpratyayatāphalamiti bhagavatā pratītyasamutpādaḥ saṃkṣepeṇa uktaḥ | atra dharmatā tu hetupratyayaryordharmatā | dharmasthitateti avipraṇāśadharmatā | dharmaniyāmateti idaṃpratyayatākramaniyāmatā | hetupratyaya-kramavat pratītyasamutpādasamateti hetvabhāve pratyayāpravṛttiḥ pratyayābhāve ca na hetu-pravṛttiḥ | parasparasāmagryāṃ ca pravṛttiḥ | ananyatathateti anyatāvirahitatvāt | bhūtateti avisaṃvādatvāt | satyatā iti satyānukūlatvāt | tathateti arthānvitatvāt | aviparītateti tu caturvidhaviparyayarahitatvāt | aviparyayateti anukūlatvāt | evamapi pratītyasamutpādo 'yam ityādi hetupratyayadvividhatvād hetupratyayobhayārtha pratītyasamutpādasya kramo 'bhyupagantavyaḥ | katamau dvāviti? ucyate | hetūpanibandhataḥ pratyayopanibandhataśca| tacca bāhyādhyātmika-bhedena caturvidho 'vagantavyam -
bāhya ādhyātmikaścāpi dvividho hetupratyayaḥ | ityuktam |
evaṃ bāhyādhyātmikaviśeṣeṇa pṛthag hetupratyayānāṃ lakṣaṇa-bhedaḥ kīdṛśa iti cet |
bāhyo hetustu bījādi ityuktam |
tatra katamo bāhyaḥ sahetukaḥ pratītyasamutpāda iti uktvā tadidam - bījādaṅkuraḥ | aṅkurāt patram | patrāt kāṇḍam | kāṇḍānnālam | nālādgaṇḍaḥ gaṇḍād garbham [garbhācchūkaḥ] puṣpāt phalam ityuktam |
pratyayaḥ ṣaḍvidho mataḥ |
iti tvavasthātvād bāhyapratītyasamutpāda iti yojyam | ṣaḍvidha iti tu pṛthivyādayaḥ ṣaḍvidhāḥ | tasmāttūktam -
bījāṅkuraprakāṇḍādiḥ phale yadvat pravartate |

bīje sati aṅkura-kāṇḍādi-phala-paryantānāṃ prādurbhāvād, bīje 'sati aṅkurakāṇḍādiphalaparyantam na prādurbhavati | tatra bījasya naivaṃ bhavati ahamaṅkurādi abhinirvartayāmi iti | aṅkurasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati ahaṃ bījādinā abhinirvartitaḥ iti | evaṃ yāvat puṣpasya naivaṃ bhavati ahaṃ phalamabhinirvartayāmīti | phalasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati ahaṃ puṣpeṇābhinirvartita iti | atha punarbīje sati aṅkurāditaḥ phalādi paryantaṃ prādurbhāvaḥ | asati na bhavati | evaṃ bāhyasya pratītyasamutpādasya hetūpanibandho draṣṭavyaḥ |
pratyayastu pṛthivyādi kālāntaṃ hi yathā kramam |

tasmādeva kathaṃ bāhyapratītyasamutpādasya pratyayopanibandho draṣṭavya ityādi uktam | bāhyapratītyasamutpādasya pratyayopanibandhāḥ katidhā draṣṭavyā ityuktam ṣaṇṇāṃ dhātūnāṃ samavāyāt | katameṣāṃ ṣaṇṇāmiti | pṛthivyaptejovāyvākāśartudhātūnāṃ yathākramaṃ samavāyād bāhyapratītyasamutpādasyeti pratyayatā yathākramam | kramo yathāvad jñātavyaḥ | eṣām hetupratyayānāṃ katamasya karma katamad iti cet? tasmād uktam |

tatra pṛthivīdhāturbījasya saṃdhāraṇakṛtyaṃ karotīti bījamaṅkurotpādonmukhamāśrayatvāt kaṭhinatvameva ucyate | abdhātuḥ snehayatīti abhiṣyandayatīti bhāṣitaḥ | tejo dhātuḥ paripācayatīti paripuṣṭayavasare upapadyamāne paraspara-sparśeṇoṣṇatā eva paripāka iti ucyate |
body.translated_text: Therein, the earth element (<s>pṛthivīdhātu</s>) performs the function of holding together (<s>saṃdhāraṇa</s>) the seed — since it is the substrate oriented toward the arising of the sprout from the seed, hardness itself is what is meant. The water element (<s>abdhātu</s>) moistens it, that is, causes it to become saturated, as stated. The fire element (<s>tejodhātu</s>) ripens it — when the occasion for full nourishment arises, the heat produced by mutual contact is what is called ripening.

body.text: vāyudhātur abhinirharatīti vardhanatvād, svāvasthāyāḥ samuddhṛtya bahirā nayanād vāyudhāturbījamabhinirharati vardhayatīti ucyate | ākāśadhāturbījāṅkurādīnām anāvaraṇakṛtyaṃ karotīti | ākāśadhāturvighnākaraṇatvād anukūlapravṛteḥ bījāṅkurādyanāvaraṇakṛtyaṃ karotītyucyate | ṛturapi bījasya pariṇāmanakṛtyaṃ karotīti ṛturapi sarvākāraṃ abhinirharati | ṛtau yathāvat parivartamāne bījapariṇāmakṛtyaṃ karotīti | sarveṣāmapyavaikalye prādurbhāvaḥ | vaikalye tu na prādurbhāvaḥ | tasmādeva uktam |
body.translated_text: The wind element (<s>vāyudhātu</s>) brings it forth, meaning that due to its capacity for growth, having drawn it up from its [initial] state, the wind element brings forth and causes the seed to grow outward, as stated. The space element (<s>ākāśadhātu</s>) performs the function of non-obstruction for seeds, sprouts, and so forth. Since the space element prevents hindrance and enables favorable activity, it performs the function of non-obstruction for seeds, sprouts, and the rest, as stated. The season (<s>ṛtu</s>) also performs the function of transforming the seed — the season brings about everything in all aspects. When the season turns in due course, it performs the function of transforming the seed. When all of these are complete, there is manifestation; when they are incomplete, there is no manifestation. Therefore it is said:

children.text: no cet pratyayasāmagrī bīje bhūte 'pi nāṅkuraḥ |
children.translated_text: If the assemblage of conditions is not [present], even though the seed exists, there is no sprout.
And if the seed is absent, likewise the conditions too are of that same [ineffectual] nature.

body.text: tasmādeva uktam | sarvasamavāyād bīje niruddhe tato 'bhinirhāraḥ syāt |
body.translated_text: Therefore it is said: from the complete conjunction of all [elements], when the seed ceases, from that the bringing forth occurs.

children.translated_text: Causes and conditions likewise are devoid of grasping at self and the like.
Through the assemblage of causes and conditions, the fruit of action does not perish.

body.text: tatra pṛthivīdhātornaivaṃ bhavati ahaṃ saṃghātakṛtyaṃ karomīti | tadvat jale agnau, vāyau, ākāśe, ṛtau cāpi naivaṃ bhavati | ātmātmīyagrahābhāvānna karmaphala-prajñapti-praṇāśaḥ, sarvatra hetupratyayavaikalyābhāvād ityavagantavyam | so 'ṅkuro 'pīti bījahetukatadaṅkurādīnām utpādo
body.translated_text: Therein, the earth element (<s>pṛthivīdhātu</s>) does not think 'I perform the function of holding together.' Likewise, water, fire, wind, space, and season also do not think thus. Due to the absence of grasping at self and mine (<s>ātmātmīyagraha</s>), there is no destruction of the designation of action and its fruit; because in all cases there is no deficiency of causes and conditions — this should be understood. That sprout too — the arising of the seed as cause and its sprout and so forth —

body.text:
na svato parato nāpi na dvayoḥ kartṛkālataḥ |
īśvarādikṛtaṃ naivaṃ svabhāvānnāpyahetutaḥ || ityuktam |
body.translated_text:
Not from itself, not from another, not from both, not from an agent or time,
not created by <s>Īśvara</s> or the like, nor from inherent nature, nor without a cause — so it is said.

body.text: svata iti hetupratyayābhāve svata utpādaḥ | svabhāvavādina evaṃ kalpanta iti śrūyate |
body.translated_text: 'From itself' means arising from itself in the absence of causes and conditions. The <s>svabhāvavādins</s> (essentialists) are heard to conceive it thus.

body.text:
bhāvānāṃ svabhāvata satatamatra tiṣṭhati |
atra na kaścidutpadyate na ca kaścin nirudhyate |
body.translated_text:
Entities exist perpetually here by their own nature;
here nothing arises and nothing ceases.

body.text:
māyūrasya patravaicitryaṃ, kamalādiṣu raktatā,
kāṇḍādīnāṃ taikṣṇyādikaṃ kena pūrvanirmitamityucyate |
body.translated_text:
The variegation of the peacock's feathers, the redness in lotuses and the like,
the sharpness and such properties of stalks — by whom were these previously fashioned? So it is said.

body.text: tasmāt tanmatanirākaraṇāyoktam | bhāvānāṃ svata utpādo na yujyate | pūrvādhyavasitatvāt | utpattimattvena abhyupagamyate, hetupratyayatābhyupagamaḥ | tasmād vastūnāṃ svabhāvata utpādo na yujyate, utpattimatvād ghaṭādivat | yasyānusāraṃ bhāvāḥ satataṃ sthitāḥ tadanusāram utpāda-kriyā-karma-sthiti-vināśā api na yujyante, utpāda-kriyā-karma-sthiti-vināśā api sākṣād avabhāsante |
body.translated_text: Therefore, in order to refute that view, it is said: the arising of entities from themselves is not tenable. Because they are already established previously, it is accepted that they possess the nature of arising, [which implies] acceptance of causes and conditions. Therefore the arising of things from their own nature is not tenable — because they are subject to arising, like a pot and so forth. If according to that [view] entities exist perpetually, then according to that same [view], arising, activity, action, persistence, and destruction are also not tenable — yet arising, activity, action, persistence, and destruction are directly manifest.

body.text: tasmād atra doṣasya prasajyamānatvān na svata ityuktam | bhāvānām svata utpādaścet nityamutpādaprasaṃgaḥ syāt, ākāśavat | kasyacidapi kutrāpi kadāpi utpādo nirodho vā nāstīti cet- ucyate- pratyakṣavirodhaḥ | evaṃ bhāvānāṃ hetupratyayād utpādo bhāsate, tasmāt tāvad bhāvānāṃ na svabhāvata utpādaḥ | parataḥ iti ātmataḥ | pareṣāmutpādako vināśakaścātmāstīti śrūyate | bāhyābhyantarasarvavastūni tu ātmaguṇāḥ | ātmā antaḥ karaṇapuruṣo 'sti |
body.translated_text: Therefore, since this fault follows, it is said 'not from itself.' If entities arose from themselves, there would be the consequence of perpetual arising, like space. If nothing whatsoever arises or ceases anywhere at any time — it is replied — this contradicts direct perception. Thus the arising of entities from causes and conditions is manifest; therefore, entities do not arise from their own nature. 'From another' means from a self (<s>ātman</s>). Others hold that entities arise from the conjunction of self and other. Therefore they assert [arising] from both. Yet since [arising] from itself is not apprehended, and since there is absence [of arising] from another, 'not from both' is said. Beyond causes and conditions, 'not from itself, not from another' — so the Blessed One stated.

body.text: tathā sati gamana-āgamana-calana-kampana-nirākaraṇa-manyanā-kriyā-karmāṇi tatraiva anyatrāpi ca pravartante | cakṣurādiḥ ātmaguṇaḥ, parārthatvāt, śayanādyaṅgavaditi | parasaṃjñā tu ātmani satyevocyate | cakṣurādiḥ tadguṇatvāt, tadarthastu parārthaḥ | yathā śayanādi parairupayuktatvāt parārthamitivat parārthatvāditi | ayaṃ hetuḥ śayanopamayā na yujyate saṃghātatvāt | ātmātvasaṃghātasvarūpaḥ | katham ātmā asaṃghātaḥ san svaśarīrābhāve śayanādīn aṅgasaṃghān svarūpeṇopakartuṃ yujyate | tasmāt sa hetvartho 'siddhaḥ, asaṃghātasya parārthaniṣpādakatvāt | śayanabhedena śayanopamā saṃghātasya parārthatvameva sādhayati | ātmanaḥ saṃghātatvād hetupratyayayorutpādopalabdha ātmātmīya iti manyanākārapravṛtteḥ cittamevātmā ityucyate | atrāntaḥ karaṇapuruṣaḥ kūrmakeśasvabhāvavad yuktyanumānarahitastu kvacinnāstīti darśayitum bhagavatā bāhyādhyātmikabhāvānāṃ parata utpādo na yujyata ityuktam | yadi bhāvānāṃ svato 'pi notpādo na ca parato 'pi, tadā bhāvānāṃ dvividha utpāda iti cet, tasmāt tanmataniṣedhārthamuktam | na dvayoḥ na ca kālata ityuktam |
body.translated_text: That being so, movement, coming, motion, shaking, removal, thinking, activity, and action operate there and elsewhere as well. The eye and other [senses] are properties of the self, because they serve another's purpose, like limbs such as a bed — so [the opponents argue]. The designation 'other' (<s>parasaṃjñā</s>) is used only when a self exists. The eye and so forth, being its properties, serve its purpose, which is another's purpose. Just as a bed and the like, being used by others, serve another's purpose — so because they serve another's purpose, [they are properties of the self]. This reasoning involving the bed analogy is not tenable, because [a bed] is a composite. The self (<s>ātman</s>) is by nature non-composite. How can the self, being non-composite, serve as limb-composites like beds and the like in its own form in the absence of its own body? Therefore that logical ground is unestablished, since a non-composite cannot accomplish another's purpose. The bed analogy with its distinctions establishes only the purpose-serving nature of composites. Since the self is [claimed to be] composite, and since arising is apprehended from causes and conditions, because of the engagement of thought in the form of 'self and mine,' the mind itself is called the self. Herein, the 'inner person' (<s>antaḥkaraṇapuruṣa</s>), like a tortoise's hair, is devoid of reasoning and inference — to show that it exists nowhere, the Blessed One said: the arising of external and internal entities from another is not tenable.

body.text: na svataḥ parataśca na | anye tu svaparayoḥ sambandhād bhāvotpādaṃ manyante | tasmād ubhayata eva vadanti | tathāpi svato 'nupalabdhatvāt parataścābhāvāt na dvayoḥ ityuktam | hetu-pratyayātiriktaṃ na svato na parata iti bhagavatā uktam | yadi ubhayasaṃyoge 'pi utpādavināśau neṣṭau, tadā paratantreṇa kartrā utpādavināśau bhaviṣyata iti kaiściducyate | anye tīrthikāstu karttā nāma kaścid ādyaḥkartā, nityo 'navacchinno vyāpakaścātmeti kaścidasti, sa eva bāhyamābhyantarañcedaṃ sarvam utpādayati vināśayatīti manyante | tasmāt tanmatakhaṇḍanārtham uktam | bhāvānāmutpādaḥ sthitirvināśaścaiva na kartradhīnāḥ | atha kasyeti cet- hetupratyayasambandhād bhāvānāṃ pravṛttirbhāsate | kartustu ākāśavan nirvikāratvāt tadadhīnā utpāda-sthitivināśāśca naiva yujyante |
body.translated_text: Not from itself and not from another. Yet others hold that entities arise from the conjunction of both self and other. Therefore they assert [arising] from both. Even so, since [arising] is not apprehended from itself, and since there is absence from another, 'not from both' is said. Beyond causes and conditions, 'not from itself, not from another' — so the Blessed One stated. If arising and destruction are not accepted even in the conjunction of both, then some say that arising and destruction will occur through a dependent agent. Other <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers) hold that there is some primordial agent, eternal, unlimited, all-pervading, and a self — he alone creates and destroys all this, both external and internal. Therefore, to refute that view, it is said: the arising, persistence, and destruction of entities are not dependent on an agent. If one asks, on what then? — from the connection of causes and conditions, the activity of entities is manifest. Since the agent, like space, is without change, arising, persistence, and destruction dependent on it are simply not tenable.

body.text: kasmāditi cet, karttari nirvikāra-niṣkriyākāśātmani kriyā karma ca kiñcidapi nāsti | utpadyamānā bhāvā hetupratyayāpekṣāḥ pravṛtti-kramodbhūtā eva bhāsante | yadanusāraṃ karttāramapekṣate pravṛttistadanusāraṃ bhāvānām utpāda-sthiti-vināśāśca sadā āsannā bhavanti | karturnityatvād bhāvānām utpādao-sthiti-vināśā yugapad bhaviṣyanti athavā utpāda-sthiti-vināśā na bhaviṣyanti | nityatvāt kvacidapi kiñcidapi utpādo vā vināśo vā na syāt | hetuṃ pratyayañca apekṣya pravartamānānāṃ bhāvānāmeva kartṛ-kriyā-hetuphalotpādasamaḥ kramodbhava upalabhyate | anutpannā-kāśotpalādīnāntu utpāda-sthiti-vināśā na yujyante | avikārahetubhiḥ parasparamāśritya pravartamānaiḥ utpādaniyamo na yujyate |
body.translated_text: Why? Because in the agent — an unchanging, actionless, space-like self — there is no activity or action whatsoever. Entities that arise appear as having emerged in sequential order depending on causes and conditions. Insofar as activity depends on an agent, insofar arising, persistence, and destruction of entities would always be imminent. Due to the agent's eternality, arising, persistence, and destruction of entities would occur simultaneously, or else arising, persistence, and destruction would not occur at all. Due to eternality, nowhere would there be any arising or destruction whatsoever. For entities that operate depending on causes and conditions, a sequential emergence equal to that of agent, action, cause, and fruit is observed. But for unproduced [things] like sky-lotuses, arising, persistence, and destruction are not tenable. Through unchanging causes operating in mutual dependence, a fixed rule of arising is not tenable.

body.text:
nityabhāvādanityo hi samutpādo na yujyate |
hetutastvavikāratvāt samasyaivodbhave sati |
hetau phale ca saṃbhinne 'vikārastu kathaṃ bhavet |
body.translated_text:
From an eternal entity, non-eternal arising is not tenable.
Since the cause is without change, and arising occurs only of the whole,
if cause and fruit are distinct, how can there be non-change?

body.text: hetau vikārasyāpi bhūtatvāt tadasādṛśyapakṣo naṣṭaḥ | kriyānanvitavandhyāputrātmani kasyāścit kriyāyāḥ karmaṇo vā niyatena ayuktatvād bhagavaddharmeṣu avisaṃvāditvād bhāvotpādakriyā karttāraṃ nāpekṣate, kintu sati hetupratyayasaṅgrahe bhāvānāmutpādavināśau yujyeta ityuktam | yadyevam atra bhāvotpāda-sthityanyathā-bhāvatādirabhyupagantavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Since change in the cause is also real, the position of its dissimilarity [from the effect] is destroyed. Since it is unreasonable to attribute any activity or action with certainty to a self that is like the son of a barren woman, devoid of action — and since [this view] is inconsistent with the teachings of the Blessed One — the arising of entities does not depend on an agent. Rather, when there is a gathering of causes and conditions, the arising and destruction of entities is tenable, so it is said. If that is so, then the arising, persistence, and alteration of entities and so forth should be accepted here.

children.translated_text: <s>Īśvara</s> (God) should be known as the cause of the arising and persistence of entities.
The contradictions of others are stated just as they are.

body.text: anyaiḥ sattvabhājanalokayorutpāda-sthiti-vināśāstu īśvarakṛtapraṇāśā avagamyante, tadīśvarecchāvaśāt kāya-bhūmitraya-kartrādisaṃbhavaḥ syāditi śrūyate | anye tasyaiva cittotpādamātreṇa naraka-preta-tiryak-deva-manuṣyadayāśca sattvāḥ jvara-viṣa-vyādhi-strī-puruṣa-napuṃsaka-sukṛtarūpa-vikṛtarūpa-dasyu-jihma-caurāḥ kāmamithyācāra-prāṇātipāta-mṛṣāvāda-madyapāna-dyūtapraveśa-pratyanta-śabara-ḍombī-nirdaya-krūra-pāruṣyavāda-brahmaghāta-mātṛpitṛghātaka-vyādhādayaḥ, yakṣa-rākṣasa-ḍākinyādayaḥ sarve paraghātakāḥ, sukha-duḥkhādayaḥ svargo vimokṣaśca tāni sarvāṇi cittotpādamātreṇoddhṛtānīti vadanti | īśvarakartṛtvavādino 'tisukumāraprajñā eva, atimandaprajñā eva, gatānugatikāścaiva yuktiviśeṣarahite tasmin gauravapravaṇatvāt pūrvottaraviruddhaṃ bālayuvakacāṇḍālavadayathārtha pratyakṣādiviruddhaṃ, dāna-vinaya-saṃyama-iṣṭāniṣṭaphalaṃ, sukṛtaduṣkṛtakarma, gamyāgamyaṃ, bhakṣyābhakṣyaṃ, svargāpavargādiphalaviruddhaṃ, yuktyāgamādiviruddhaṃ ca vāṅmātreṇa pakṣīkṛtya nijājñānapaṭalena netrācchādanatvād asamarthatvāt paśubhūtāstu paśubhyo 'pyatichudratarāḥ paśavaḥ | nigūḍhavandhyāputrasvabhāvaṃ paśupatimāśritya, janmasthitivināśānāṃ hetutāṃsyaapi tūccatām | utpāde sthitau ca sahetuka evābhyupagamyamāne sati nityavādabhaṅgatvād vādotsargaḥ, viparītasiddhatvād īśvarasya ahetutvameva sidhyati | icchāmātreṇa utpāde sati yugapadeva sampūrṇajagata utpādasthiti-vināśāḥ syuḥ |
body.translated_text: Others understand that the arising, persistence, and destruction of the world of beings and the receptacle world are caused by <s>Īśvara</s> (God), and it is heard that by the force of <s>Īśvara's</s> will, the existence of the three realms of body, the earth, the creator, etc. would come about. Others say that by the mere arising of His thought, all beings — those in <s>naraka</s> (hell), <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost), <s>tiryak</s> (animal), <s>deva</s> (god), and <s>manuṣya</s> (human) realms — as well as fever, poison, disease, woman, man, neuter, those of good form and deformed, bandits, the crooked, thieves, those given to sexual misconduct, killing, lying, drinking, gambling, those of border regions, <s>Śabaras</s>, <s>Ḍombīs</s>, the merciless, the cruel, those of harsh speech, slayers of <s>Brahmins</s>, killers of mothers and fathers, hunters, etc., as well as <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>ḍākinīs</s>, and all destroyers of others, along with pleasure, suffering, etc., heaven and liberation — all these are produced by the mere arising of thought. The proponents of <s>Īśvara</s> as creator are of extremely delicate intellect — nay, of extremely dull intellect — mere followers of tradition, inclined toward authority in that [doctrine] which is devoid of any special reasoning, [holding views that are] contradicted by what comes before and after, like children, youths, and outcasts, contrary to reality and opposed to perception and other [means of valid cognition], [asserting that] the fruits of giving, discipline, and self-restraint, whether pleasant or unpleasant, meritorious and evil actions, what is proper and improper, what is fit and unfit to eat, and the fruits of heaven, liberation, etc. [all come from Īśvara] — contradicting reasoning and scripture alike, having adopted [this view] by mere words, covering their eyes with the veil of their own ignorance, being incapable — they are indeed like animals, nay, even more contemptible than animals!
