Having taken refuge in <s>Paśupati</s> (Lord of Animals), whose nature is like the son of a barren woman hidden in secret, even the status of being a cause of birth, persistence, and destruction is exalted. When arising and persistence are accepted as having a cause, since the eternalist position is broken, the thesis is abandoned; since the opposite is proved, the causelessness of <s>Īśvara</s> itself is established. If arising occurs by mere will, then the arising, persistence, and destruction of the entire world would occur all at once.

body.text: tasmādapi asiddhārthataiva syāt, sarveṣāṃ nityotpādaprasaṅgatvāt | duḥkha-kuhanā-jihma-aśuci-akṛtajñatādyuddharaṇānāṃ tu prayojanaviśeṣābhāvācca asiddhārthatā | taduddharaṇāyāso niṣphalaḥ | prayojanābhāve hi kalpanāpūrvaṅgamānāṃ pravṛttirnāsti, prayojanāvyāpteḥ | tatprayojanavadvyāvṛttau kalpanāpūrvaṅgamānāṃ pravṛtterapi nivṛtteḥ asiddhārthatāsti |
body.translated_text: Therefore from that too, the thesis remains unestablished, since there would be the absurd consequence of eternal arising for all things. And since there is no specific purpose for the removal of suffering, deceit, crookedness, impurity, ingratitude, etc., the thesis is unestablished. The effort to remove those is fruitless. For in the absence of purpose, there is no activity preceded by intention, since [activity] does not pervade purpose. When that which possesses purpose ceases, the activity preceded by intention also ceases — hence the thesis is unestablished.

body.text:
hetupratyayavaikalye kramotpādavināśau
pratyakṣatayā bhāsete, avaikalye cānutpādaḥ |
body.translated_text:
When there is deficiency in causes and conditions, sequential arising and destruction
are manifest as directly perceptible; and when there is no deficiency, there is non-arising.

body.text: sattvabhājanalokayorutpadyamānasukhaduḥkhādīnāṃ sthitivināśau kramaśa upalabhyete, tasmānna īśvaro hetuḥ | kasyacidapi bhāvasya utpāda-sthiti-vināśā na yujyante| tasmādapi pratyakṣavirodho 'siddhārtha eva | nānyat pratyakṣato garīyaḥ pramāṇamiti sarvavādiprasiddham |
body.translated_text: The persistence and destruction of pleasure, suffering, etc. that arise in the world of beings and the receptacle world are observed sequentially; therefore <s>Īśvara</s> is not the cause. The arising, persistence, and destruction of any entity whatsoever are not tenable [from <s>Īśvara</s>]. Therefore this too contradicts direct perception, and the thesis is simply unestablished. It is acknowledged by all disputants that there is no means of valid cognition greater than direct perception.

body.text:
naikānte 'rthakriyā | dayāpratāpābhāve
gambhīryaguṇa-darśana-caryā-cintanādi na yujyate |
body.translated_text:
There is no purposeful action in an absolute [creator]. In the absence of compassion and power,
depth of qualities, observation, conduct, contemplation, etc. are not tenable.

body.text: ekāntakriyāyuktā yuktayorgāmbhīryaguṇasya rūpādervā ālambana cintanasyaiva ayuktatvāt, tattu pratikūlam |
body.translated_text: Since contemplation that takes as its object the quality of profundity, or form, etc., which would be consistent with absolute action, is itself untenable — that [argument] is actually contrary [to the Īśvara thesis].

body.text:
hetāvasati sarvatra pratyaya eva kathaṃ bhavet |
ahetau kārakābhāvāt kathamīṣṭe maheśvaraḥ |
bhāvakartā maheśaścet so 'pi kartā na manyate |
pitrabhāve sutotpattiḥ sā neṣṭā dṛśyate na ca |
hetuniṣyandasādṛśyaṃ manyante yuktivādinaḥ |
nityānnityaphalaṃ yuktamanityāccāpyanityakam |
śālibījātphalaṃ tasmādaṅkurotpāda īkṣyate |
tathā maheśvare nitye bhāvānāṃ syāt sadodbhavaḥ |
yathāgnirdāhayetsarvaṃ tathācedīśvaro mataḥ |
agnihetustathānyo 'gniḥ īśvare nāsti hetukam |
kramapravṛttajvālābhiḥ sarvadāho 'pi manyate |
īśvarasyāvikāritvād agnivattvaṃ na yujyate |
body.translated_text:
When the cause is absent, how can the condition exist anywhere?
In the absence of a cause, since there is no agent, how does <s>Maheśvara</s> create?
If <s>Maheśvara</s> is the maker of beings, even he is not considered a [true] maker.
The birth of a son in the absence of a father — that is neither desired nor observed.
Those who reason rightly hold that the effect resembles the outflow of the cause.
From what is eternal, an eternal fruit is logical; and from what is non-eternal, a non-eternal one.
From a rice seed, a fruit [arises] — therefore a sprout is seen to arise.
Likewise, if <s>Maheśvara</s> is eternal, there would be perpetual arising of things.
If <s>Īśvara</s> is considered to burn everything as fire does,
then just as fire has another fire as its cause, in <s>Īśvara</s> there is no [such] cause.
Even universal burning is accepted through flames that proceed sequentially;
since <s>Īśvara</s> is unchanging, the analogy with fire is not tenable.

body.text: tasmādīśvarakartṛtvābhyupagame bahudoṣasaṃbhavād bhagavatā bhāvānām utpādaḥ īśvarakṛto na yujyate ityuktam | pare tu sarvaṃ kālena vivartitaṃ manyante | tairevamucyate |
body.translated_text: Therefore, since accepting <s>Īśvara</s> as creator leads to many faults, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) has said that the arising of things as caused by <s>Īśvara</s> is not tenable. Others, however, hold that everything is transformed by <s>kāla</s> (time). They state as follows:

body.text:
sthitirbhāvān samutpādya kālenaiva vivartyate |
bhāvotpādasthitī cāpi kālenaiva vivartite |
body.translated_text:
Persistence, having produced beings, is transformed by <s>kāla</s> (time) alone;
the arising and persistence of beings too are transformed by <s>kāla</s> alone.

body.text: tadevam ucyate | atra kāla iti kiṃ nāma? nityo vā anityo vā, puruṣaḥ strī napuṃsakasvabhāvo vā, devo piśāco vā, mūrto 'mūrto vā, sakriyo niṣkriyo vā |
body.translated_text: To this, the following is said: Here, what is this thing called '<s>kāla</s>' (time)? Is it eternal or non-eternal? Male, female, or neuter in nature? A god or a <s>piśāca</s> (demon)? Corporeal or incorporeal? With activity or without activity?

body.text:
sa nityaścettadā tatra kriyāpekṣā na yujyate |
utpādaścetsakṛt so 'pi viruddhatvān na manyate |
anityatve 'kālasya hetupratyayayogataḥ |
yadi puṃstrīnapuṃsādi yatkiñcitsyād virudhyate |
dehyadehikriyādau ca pārasparaviruddhatā |
nityatve nirvikāratvāt kriyākarma virudhyate |
body.translated_text:
If it is eternal, then the expectation of action with regard to it is not tenable.
If arising occurs [from it], that too occurring just once is not accepted, since it is contradictory.
If <s>kāla</s> is non-eternal, [it requires] the conjunction of causes and conditions.
If it is male, female, neuter, or anything whatsoever, it is contradicted.
In the body, the self, action, etc., there is mutual contradiction.
If eternal, since it is changeless, action and its object are contradicted.

body.text: evaṃ kālavādināṃ kālavaśena bhāvānāmutpāda-sthiti-vināśābhyu-pagamasyāpi ayuktatvāt tadapyasamañjasameva | sūryacandra-nakṣatra-parva-vatsarādi-bāhyābhyantarabhāvānāṃ gatagamyasvabhāvatvāt kālākhyayā bhāvānāmutpāda-sthiti-vināśāstu kālapariṇāmatvena na yujyante|
body.translated_text: Thus, even the acceptance by the proponents of <s>kāla</s> (time) that the arising, persistence, and destruction of things occur through the power of time is untenable — so that [position] too is entirely incoherent. Since external and internal entities such as the sun, moon, constellations, conjunctions, years, etc. are by nature past and passing, the arising, persistence, and destruction of things designated as '<s>kāla</s>' are not tenable as transformations of time.

body.text: anyacca, svabhāvavādina āntarabāhyān sarvabhāvān svabhāvodbhavān manyante | bhāvānāṃ svabhāva eva, kasyacidbhāvasya utpādasya vināśasya vā kaścidapi heturnāsti | khara-snigdha-uṣṇa-laghutva-ślakṣṇa-tīkṣṇāni svabhāva eva | madhura-amla-lavaṇa-kaṭukāni asattvabhedā eva |
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the proponents of <s>svabhāva</s> (inherent nature) hold that all internal and external entities arise from their own inherent nature. The inherent nature of things is just that [what they are]; there is no cause whatsoever for the arising or destruction of any entity. Hardness, smoothness, heat, lightness, softness, and sharpness are simply inherent nature. Sweet, sour, salty, and pungent are merely distinctions of non-being.

body.text:
deva-mānuṣa-tiryañco rājabrahma-kujātayaḥ |
sukṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ cāpi sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ sadā sthitam |
svabhāvavaimatyā tebhyo bhrāntacittebhya evaṃ vaktavyam |
svabhāve vikṛte dṛṣṭe pratyakṣādiviruddhatā |
vikāro vartate yatra nirvikāraḥ kathaṃ bhavet |
vyaktyanekaprabhedācca janma nāśaśca bhāsate |
jātervināśasambandhān nirvikāraḥ kathaṃ bhavet |
svabhāve nirvikāratvāt puruṣādau nirarthake |
kule rājani kṣetrādau tatphalaṃ cāpi bhāsate |
svabhāve vikṛte jāte nityavādī tu bhraṃsate |
mārgo 'yaṃ yujyate tasmād hetupratyayavādinām |
body.translated_text:
Gods, humans, and animals, kings, <s>Brahmins</s>, and low-born,
merit and demerit, pleasure and suffering are always established [by nature].
To those of confused minds who disagree about <s>svabhāva</s> (inherent nature), the following should be said:
When inherent nature is seen to be modified, there is contradiction with perception and other [pramāṇas].
Where transformation exists, how can there be changelessness?
From the many divisions of individuals, both birth and destruction are manifest.
Since birth is connected with destruction, how can there be changelessness?
If inherent nature is changeless, then person etc. become purposeless.
In family, kingship, field, etc., their fruits too are manifest.
When inherent nature is born modified, the eternalist falls.
Therefore this path is tenable for those who maintain causes and conditions.

body.text: evaṃ svabhāvavādiṣvapi parasparavirodhatvād utpāda-sthiti-vināśānāṃ svabhāvād udbhavo na yujyata ityuktam | atha bhāvānām utpāda-sthiti-vināśā ahetuto bhavanti ityapare 'hetuvādino hetuṃ vinaiva kevalam bhāvānāmutpāda-nirodhau kalpayanti | ahetuvādo 'bhyapagamyeta cet, hetoḥ aniścitatvāt kṛtapraṇāśa-akṛtābhyāgama-anavasthāśca bhaviṣyanti | sukṛta-duṣkṛtādi-pitṛ-putra-brāhmaṇa-rājanya-vaiśya-śūdra-śvapacādi-śucyaśuci-gamyāgamya-bhakṣyābhakṣya-devapiśācādi-dāna-vinaya-saṃyama-japa-tapasyā-upavāsa-niścaya-yāgajñānājñāna-hetvaniścayāt parasparabhedanirṇaya-vyavasthāpi na saṃbhavati | tasmāttasyaiva doṣasya prasajyamānatvād ahetuvādo 'pi lokādi-viruddhatvād asiddha eva |
body.translated_text: Thus, even among the proponents of <s>svabhāva</s> (inherent nature), since there is mutual contradiction, it has been stated that the arising, persistence, and destruction [of things] from inherent nature is not tenable. Now, others who are <s>ahetuvādins</s> (proponents of causelessness) hold that the arising, persistence, and destruction of things occur without any cause, and they postulate the arising and cessation of things merely without any cause at all. If the doctrine of causelessness were accepted, then since causes would be uncertain, there would be destruction of what has been done, arrival of what has not been done, and infinite regress. The determination of distinctions and the establishment of order among merit and demerit, father and son, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Kṣatriya</s>, <s>Vaiśya</s>, <s>Śūdra</s>, and outcaste, pure and impure, proper and improper [conduct], edible and inedible, gods and demons, giving, discipline, self-restraint, recitation, austerity, fasting, resolve, sacrifice, knowledge and ignorance — since the cause of all these would be uncertain, the determination of mutual distinctions and orderly arrangement would not be possible. Therefore, since precisely this fault would ensue, the doctrine of causelessness too, being contrary to the world etc., is simply unestablished.

body.text: ye cānye pradhāna-paramāṇvādyahetu-pratikūlahetuvādādayaste 'pi tenaiva niṣedhitavyāḥ | tasmān |
body.translated_text: And others who are proponents of contrary causes such as <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter), <s>paramāṇu</s> (atoms), etc. — those too should be refuted by that very [reasoning]. Therefore:

body.text:
na svataḥ parato nāpi na dvayoḥ kartṛkālataḥ |
īśvarādikṛtaṃ naiva svabhāvānnāpyahetutaḥ || ityuktam |
body.translated_text:
Not from self, not from other, not from both, not from a creator or time,
not made by <s>Īśvara</s> and the rest, not from inherent nature, nor from the absence of a cause — thus it has been stated.

body.text: hetupratyayayorvṛttirbhāsate 'nādikālataḥ ||
body.translated_text: The operation of causes and conditions is manifest from beginningless time.

body.text: iti tu anādi-kālataḥ prapañca-vāsanābījasya avicchinna-nadīstrotaḥ-pravāhavad anupravṛtteḥ
body.translated_text: That is, from beginningless time, because the seed of <s>prapañca</s>-<s>vāsanā</s> (latent impressions of phenomenal proliferation) continues uninterruptedly like the current of a river,

body.text: hetupratyayayorvṛttirbhāsate 'nādikālataḥ | ityuktam |
body.translated_text: "The operation of causes and conditions is manifest from beginningless time" — thus it has been stated.

body.text: tasmādeva sūtre atha punaḥ pṛthivyaptejovāyvākāśartudhātusamavāyād bīje nirudhyamāne aṅkurasyābhinirvṛttirbhavati ityuktam | 'atha punaḥ' iti tu abhāvādudbhava-sva-para-dvaya-īśvarādi-rahita-bīja-pṛthivyādi-sāmagryā eva aṅkurādi utpadyata iti uktam |
body.translated_text: Therefore, in the <s>sūtra</s> it is said: "Now then, when the seed ceases through the conjunction of earth, water, fire, wind, space, season, and elements, the production of the sprout occurs." The phrase 'now then' means: it is stated that the sprout etc. arises from the aggregate of the seed, earth, etc. alone — free from [theories of] arising from non-existence, self, other, both, <s>Īśvara</s>, etc.

body.text: pañcabhirhetubhirbāhyaḥ pratītyotpāda iṣyate | iti |
body.translated_text: External <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) is accepted as having five causes.

body.text: pañcabhirhetubhiriti tu hetupañcakairiti, bāhyasyeti bījādeḥ | 'pratītyotpāda' iti pratītyam |
body.translated_text: 'By five causes' means by the five causes; 'of the external' means of the seed and so forth. '<s>Pratītyotpāda</s>' means 'arising dependently.'

body.text:
śāśvatato na cocchedān na saṅkrānteḥ parīttataḥ |
hertormahāphalāvāptiḥ sadṛśānuprabodhataḥ | ityuktam |
body.translated_text: Not from eternality, nor from annihilation, not from transference; from a small [cause] a great fruit is obtained, from the awakening of what is similar. Thus it was said.

body.text: 'śāśvatato na' iti yasmādanyadbījam, anyo 'ṅkuraḥ, na ca ya evāṅkurāstadeva bījam, bījamevāpi nāṅkuraḥ | aniruddhād bījādapi aṅkuro notpadyate | na ca niruddhād, tathāpi bījanirodhe aṅkura utpadyate | tasmān na śāśvatato, na cocchedāditi na ca pūrvaniruddhādbījādaṅkuro niṣpadyate nācāpyaniruddhād | api tu bījād niruddhāt tasminneva samaye 'ṅkuro utpadyate | ato nocchedataḥ | na saṃkrāntitaḥ iti tu bījāṅkurau tu asadṛśau eva | tasmāt 'na saṃkrāntitaḥ | parīttataḥ hetoriti- parīttabījavapanān mahāphalāvāptiriti tatparītta-hetorbahuphalābhinirvṛttiḥ, parīttānmahāphalābhi-nirvṛttitvāt, tasmāt parīttahetormahāphalābhinirvṛtiḥ | sadṛśānuprabodhād iti tu yādṛśaṃ bījamupyate tādṛśameva phalābhinirvṛtiriti | atastatsadṛśānuprabandhaḥ | sadṛśāphalābhinirvṛttiḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Not from eternality' — because the seed is one thing and the sprout another; it is not the case that the sprout itself is the seed, nor is the seed itself the sprout. The sprout does not arise from an unceased seed, nor from a ceased one; nevertheless, when the seed ceases, at that very moment the sprout arises. Therefore not from eternality. 'Nor from annihilation' — the sprout does not come forth from a previously ceased seed, nor from an unceased one. Rather, when the seed has ceased, at that very moment the sprout arises — hence not from annihilation. 'Not from transference' — the seed and the sprout are indeed dissimilar. Therefore 'not from transference.' 'From a small cause, a great fruit' — from sowing a small seed, a great fruit is obtained; that is, from a small cause, an abundant fruit is produced; because from something small a great fruit is produced, therefore from a small cause a great fruit is produced. 'From the awakening of what is similar' — whatever kind of seed is sown, that same kind of fruit is produced. Therefore there is a continuity of what is similar — a production of a similar fruit.

body.text:
bījāṅkurayorbhinnatvād bījaṃ nityaṃ na vartate |
yataścocchedato nāsti bīje sati tathāṅkuraḥ |
bījasādṛśyasiddhatvāt tadbhinnaṃ na ceṣyate |
aṅkurasya phalādīnāṃ saṅkrāntiścāṅkurasya na |
ekabījaṃ parīttāṇoḥ bījatvenaiva sambhavet |
tasmāt parīttato hetorjāyate hi mahatphalam |
upte śālyādi bīje hi śyāmākādiphalaṃ na hi |
body.translated_text: Because of the distinctness of seed and sprout, the seed does not persist as permanent; and since there is no annihilation when the seed exists, thus the sprout [arises]. Because of the established similarity to the seed, it is not accepted as different from that. And there is no transference from the sprout to the fruit and so forth. From one small seed, the possibility of becoming a seed itself [for further growth] — therefore from a small cause, a great fruit indeed arises. When rice and such seeds are sown, millet and such fruits do not [appear].

body.text:
tasmādeva -
aṅkuro bījavanneṣṭo nirheturno 'ṅkurodbhavaḥ |
samo nirodha utpādas tulonnāmāvanāmavat | ityuktam |
body.translated_text: Therefore — the sprout is not accepted as being like the seed; without a cause, the arising of the sprout does not occur. Cessation and arising are equal, like the rising and falling of a balance. Thus it was said.

body.text: evam bāhyapratītyasamutpādaḥ parikalpanātmakena anupacayatvena draṣṭavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus external <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) should be viewed as being of the nature of conceptual construction and non-accumulation.

body.text: tathaivādhyātmikasyāpi hetuśca pratyayo dvidhā |
body.translated_text: Likewise for the internal also, cause and condition are twofold.

body.text: tathaivādhyātmikasyāpi bāhya-pratītyasamutpādavad hetupratyayākāradvayopa-nibandhanatvāt pṛthak dvividho 'vagantavyaḥ | dvidhā hetuścapratyaya iti tu ādhyātmikaḥ pratītyasamutpādo hetūpanibandhanaḥ pratyayopanibandhanaśca dvayākāro 'vagantavyaḥ | iṣṭa iti abhīṣṭasya ca abhipretasya abhimatasya cetyadhivacanam | tatrādhyātmikasya pratītyasamutpādasya hetūpanibandhaḥ kathamavagantavyaḥ? ucyate -
body.translated_text: Likewise for the internal also — because, like external <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), it is bound by two aspects of cause and condition, it should be understood as twofold and distinct. 'Twofold as cause and condition' means that internal <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> should be understood as having two aspects: the binding of causes (<s>hetu</s>) and the binding of conditions (<s>pratyaya</s>). '<s>Iṣṭa</s>' is a designation for what is desired, intended, and approved. Therein, how should the binding of causes of internal <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> be understood? It is said:

body.text: ādiheturavidyāsya mṛtyurantyo yathākramam |
body.translated_text: The initial cause is <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), death is the end, in due order.

body.text: tatrādāvavidyādeśanād ādau avidyā, ante maraṇāṅgadeśanatvān mṛtyurante | yattayormadhye syāt tat tu madhya iṣyate | tasmāt sūtre avidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārāḥ, saṃskārapratyayaṃ vijñānam, vijñānapratyayaṃ nāmarūpam, nāmarūpapratyayaṃ ṣaḍāyatanam, ṣaḍāyatanapratyayaḥ sparśaḥ, sparśapratyayā vedanā, vedanāpratyayā tṛṣṇā, tṛṣṇāpratyaya mupādānam, upādānapratyayo bhavaḥ, bhavapratyayā jātiḥ, jātipratyayā jarāmaraṇa-śoka-parideva-duḥkha-daurmanasyopāyāsāḥ saṃbhavanti | evamasya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya samudayo bhavati | ityuktam |
body.translated_text: Therein, because <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is taught at the beginning, <s>avidyā</s> is first; because the limb of death is taught at the end, death is at the end. Whatever lies between those two is considered the middle. Therefore, in the <s>sūtra</s>: conditioned by <s>avidyā</s> arise <s>saṃskāras</s> (volitional formations); conditioned by <s>saṃskāras</s> arises <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness); conditioned by <s>vijñāna</s> arises <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form); conditioned by <s>nāmarūpa</s> arise the <s>ṣaḍāyatanas</s> (six sense bases); conditioned by the <s>ṣaḍāyatanas</s> arises <s>sparśa</s> (contact); conditioned by <s>sparśa</s> arises <s>vedanā</s> (feeling); conditioned by <s>vedanā</s> arises <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving); conditioned by <s>tṛṣṇā</s> arises <s>upādāna</s> (clinging); conditioned by <s>upādāna</s> arises <s>bhava</s> (becoming); conditioned by <s>bhava</s> arises <s>jāti</s> (birth); conditioned by <s>jāti</s> arise aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, mental anguish, and despair. Thus arises this entire great mass of suffering. So it was said.

body.text:
sajanmakleśakarmātmā dvādaśāṅgastrikāṇḍakaḥ |
hetupratyayasambhūtaḥ karttetyādivivarjitaḥ |
body.translated_text: Consisting of birth, afflictions, and action, the twelve limbs are a threefold division, arising from causes and conditions, devoid of agent and so forth.

body.text: kleśa-karma-jāti-paratantro 'yamātmāpi aṃśatrayeṇa vyavasthāpyate | kleśa-paratantrasvabhāvatayā, karmaparatantrasvabhāvatayā janmaparatantrasvabhāvatayā ca | tatra kleśa paratantra-svabhāvatāyā aṅgāni trīṇi-avidyātṛṣṇopādānāni | karma-paratantra-svabhāvatāyāḥ dve aṅge-bhavasaṃskārau | jāti-paratantra lakṣaṇamapi śeṣasaptāṅgam-vijñānam, nāmarūpam, ṣaḍāyatanam, sparśo, vedanā, jātiḥ, jarāmaraṇañceti | apītipadaṃ saṃgrāhyatāṃ darśayati | śoka-paridevanā-daurmanasya-upāyāsādīnāṃ priyaviyogā-priyasaṃprayoga-kāmavipattyādīnāṃ ca saṃgrahaḥ | evam ayaṃ pratītyasamutpādo dvādaśāṅgaḥ trisvabhāvatayā veditavyaḥ | so 'pi kartrādi-svabhāvatā-rahito jñātavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: This [dependent origination], dependent on afflictions, <s>karma</s> (action), and birth, is also established by three portions. By the nature of dependence on afflictions, by the nature of dependence on <s>karma</s>, and by the nature of dependence on birth. Therein, the limbs of the nature dependent on afflictions are three: <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), and <s>upādāna</s> (clinging). The limbs of the nature dependent on <s>karma</s> are two: <s>bhava</s> (becoming) and <s>saṃskāras</s> (volitional formations). The characteristic of dependence on birth comprises the remaining seven limbs: <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form), <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s> (six sense bases), <s>sparśa</s> (contact), <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>jāti</s> (birth), and <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> (aging-and-death). The word 'also' indicates inclusiveness. Sorrow, lamentation, mental anguish, despair, and so forth, as well as separation from the beloved, union with the unpleasant, failure of desires, and so forth — all are included. Thus this <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) of twelve limbs should be understood as having a threefold nature. And it should be known as devoid of the nature of agent and the like.

body.text: atha śālistambasūtraṭīkāyāṃ tṛtīyaṃ paṭalam |
body.translated_text: Thus ends the third chapter of the <s>Śālistamba-sūtra-ṭīkā</s> (commentary on the Rice Seedling Sūtra).

body.text: avidyā yadi nādau syādante mṛtyurna saṃbhaved |
body.translated_text: If <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) were not at the beginning, death would not occur at the end.

body.text: 'avidyā yadi nādau syād' iti tu yadi avidyā cennābhaviṣyan naiva saṃskārāḥ prajñāsyante | tadvad jarāmaraṇaparyantaṃ cennābhaviṣyan naiva śokādi prajñāsyate |
body.translated_text: 'If <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) were not at the beginning' — if <s>avidyā</s> had not existed, <s>saṃskāras</s> (volitional formations) would never have been known. Likewise, up to aging-and-death — if they had not existed, sorrow and so forth would never have been known.

body.text: tebhyo bhinno na kutrāpi hyātmātmīyaśca vidyate |
body.translated_text: Apart from these, nowhere whatsoever is there a self or what belongs to self.

body.text: tatrāvidyāyā naivaṃ bhavati ahaṃ saṃskārādi abhinirvartayāmītyato jarāmaraṇaparyantaṃ naivaṃ bhavati ahaṃ śokādi abhinirvartayāmīti | saṃskārādīnāmapi naivaṃ bhavati vayamavidyādibhyo 'bhinirvartitāḥ | evam yāvajjarāmaraṇasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati vayaṃ jātyādibhirabhinirvartitā iti |
body.translated_text: Therein, <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) does not think: 'I produce <s>saṃskāras</s> (volitional formations) and so forth' — likewise up to aging-and-death, it does not think: 'I produce sorrow and so forth.' Nor do the <s>saṃskāras</s> and so forth think: 'We have been produced by <s>avidyā</s> and so forth.' Likewise, even aging-and-death does not think: 'We have been produced by birth and so forth.'

body.text: avidyāsaṃbhavādādāvante mṛtyuśca bhāsate |
body.translated_text: From the arising of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) at the beginning, death appears at the end.

body.text: atha ca satyāmavidyāyāṃ saṃskārādyabhinirvṛttirbhavati, prādurbhāvaḥ | evaṃ yāvajjarāmaraṇaṃ, śokaparidevādyabhinirvṛttirbhavati |
body.translated_text: And yet, when <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is present, the production of <s>saṃskāras</s> (volitional formations) and so forth occurs — their manifestation. Likewise, up to aging-and-death, the production of sorrow, lamentation, and so forth occurs.

body.text: heturādhyātmikasyāsya |
body.translated_text: The cause of this internal [dependent origination] —

body.text: evamādhyātmikasya pratītyasamutpādasya hetūpanibandho draṣṭavyaḥ | kathamādhyātmikasya pratītyasamutpādasya pratyayopanibandho draṣṭavyaḥ? ucyate -
body.translated_text: Thus should the binding of causes of internal <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) be viewed. How should the binding of conditions of internal <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> be viewed? It is said:

body.text: pratyayāḥ ṣaṭprakārakāḥ |
body.translated_text: The conditions are of six kinds.

body.text: asyeti tu ādhyātmikasya| pratyayastu sāmagrī ṣaṭ prakārakā iti ṣaḍvidhāḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Of this' means of the internal. The conditions — that is, the assemblage — are of six kinds, meaning sixfold.

body.text: pratyayo 'dhyātmikastvante vijñānaṃ cādike dharā |
body.translated_text: The condition of the internal [dependent origination]: <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) at the end, and the sustaining [earth element] at the beginning.

body.text: vijñānasyānte parideśanatvād 'ante vijñānam' | ādike dharā ityucyate |
body.translated_text: Because <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) is taught at the end, 'consciousness at the end.' 'The sustaining [earth element] at the beginning' — so it is said.

body.text: tasmāt sūtre -ṣaṇṇāṃ dhātūnāṃ samavāyāt pṛthivyaptejovāyvākāśa-vijñānādistvādhyātmikasya pratītyasamutpādasya pratyayopanibandho draṣṭavyaḥ | ityuktam |
body.translated_text: Therefore, in the <s>sūtra</s>: through the convergence of six <s>dhātus</s> (elements) — earth, water, fire, wind, space, and <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) — the binding of conditions of internal <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) should be viewed. Thus it was said.

body.text: kāṭhinyānugrahau pākaḥ śvāsavṛddhiranāvṛtiḥ |
body.translated_text: Hardness, support, ripening, breathing, growth, and non-obstruction.

body.text: tatra adhyātma-pṛthivīdhātuḥ katamaḥ? yatkāyasambaddha-kaṭhina-karkaśa-rūkṣa-kharagata-keśa-roma-nakha-danta-sveda-mala-carma-māṃsa-snāyu-asthayādi-sadṛśam, anyacca asmin kāye yatkiñcidasti tatsarvaṃ saṃgṛhya pṛthivīdhāturucyate | anugraha tu saṃgrahaḥ, sambandho-mṛduḥ, āliṅganaṃ, piṇḍīkaraṇaṃ snigdhatā ca | tadyathā-aśru-sveda-kapha-siṃghāṇaka-majjā-śukra-mūtra-uccāra-rakta-lasīkā-mastaka-grahaṇī-pakvāśayādiḥ anyaccāsmin kāye tādṛśaṃ snigdha-svabhāvaṃ syājjaladhāturucyate |
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the internal earth element (<s>pṛthivīdhātu</s>)? Whatever is connected with the body that is hard, rough, coarse, and harsh — hair of the head, body hair, nails, teeth, sweat, dirt, skin, flesh, sinews, bones, and the like — and whatever else of such nature exists in this body, all that taken together is called the earth element. 'Support' means gathering, binding, softness, embracing, solidifying, and oiliness. Such as: tears, sweat, phlegm, mucus, marrow, semen, urine, feces, blood, lymph, brain matter, intestinal contents, the cooked food receptacle, and so forth — whatever else of such oily nature exists in this body is called the water element (<s>jaladhātu</s>).

body.text: pāko nāma pācanam-pāka-pācana-pācaka-uṣṇāgnistāpa-tāpana-vṛtiryaścaitatkāyamadhye aśita-pīta-khāditānāṃ samyaksupācakaḥ | anyacca yatkiñcitkaṃ tādṛśaṃ tatsarvaṃ tu tejodhāturucyate | śvāsa iti vāyudhātuḥ | śvāsastu ucchvāsaḥ, āśvāso, bhāṣaṇaṃ, pralāpo, gamanāgamanaṃ kṣayo vṛddhiriti | kāyasya vistāraḥ, saṅkocaḥ, kampanaṃ, calanaṃ, utkṣepaḥ, poṣaṇaṃ, vṛddhiḥ, pīnasaḥ, kāsaḥ, chikkā, ūrdhvavāyuradhovāyuranyaccāpi etatkāyamadhye yatkiñcit tādṛśamasti tatsarvam ekataḥ piṇḍīkṛtya vāyudhāturityucyate | ākāśamiti anāvṛtatvādākāśam | āvaraṇaṃ sapratighaṃ saṃvṛtañca | rājī-koṣa-antārandhra-mukharandhra-karṇapuṭa-nāsāpuṭa-netrachidrādayaḥ kāyāntaḥ koṣaścāyam ākāśadhāturityucyate |
body.translated_text: 'Ripening' means cooking — ripening, cooking, the digestive fire, heat, and warming — that which within this body properly digests what is eaten, drunk, and chewed. Whatever else of such nature exists — all that is called the fire element (<s>tejodhātu</s>). 'Breathing' refers to the wind element (<s>vāyudhātu</s>). Breathing means: inhalation, exhalation, speech, babbling, coming and going, decrease and increase, the body's expansion, contraction, trembling, movement, upward lifting, nourishment, growth, nasal congestion, coughing, sneezing, upward-moving wind, downward-moving wind — and whatever else of such nature exists within this body, all that taken together is called the wind element. 'Space' means non-obstruction — the space element (<s>ākāśadhātu</s>). Obstruction is [that which is] resistant and covered. The spaces between the joints, the cavities within, the mouth opening, the ear cavities, the nasal cavities, the eye openings, and so forth — and this inner cavity of the body — is called the space element.

children.translated_text: And the continuation of <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form), conjoined with the five <s>vijñānas</s> (consciousnesses),
And the afflicted mind (<s>kliṣṭamanas</s>) — these are the internal conditions.

body.text: tatra nāmānuvṛttiḥ rūpānuvṛttiśca ādhyātmikavijñānadhāturityucyate | pañcavijñānasaṃyutaḥ iti tāni pañcavijñānakāyāni, tataḥ kliṣṭaṃ manaścāpi iti kleśamayaṃ manaḥ, tāni ca caturmahābhūtāni ekataḥ piṇḍīkṛtya naḍakalāpayogena nāmarūpamityucyate | tatra nāmeti catvāro 'rūpaskandhāḥ-vedanā, saṃjñā, saṃskāro vijñānaṃ ceti | rūpaṃ nāma pitroḥ śukraśoṇitodbhūtaṃ antarābhavamāśritya yat prathamaṃ nāmarūpābhinirvartanaṃ tanniśritya pūrvaṃnāmarūpābhinirvartanaṃ-manovijñānaṃ sāsravaṃ nivṛta-vyākṛta svabhāvam ātmamohādicatuḥkleśātmakam | ātmamohaḥ, ātmamānam, ātmadṛṣṭiḥ, ātmotkarṣaścetyetatkleśasaṃyutaṃ kliṣṭaṃ mana iti ekataḥ piṇḍīkṛtaṃ nāmarūpamityucyate |
body.translated_text: Therein, the continuity of name and the continuity of form are called the inner consciousness element (<s>ādhyātmikavijñānadhātu</s>). 'Conjoined with the five consciousnesses' refers to the five consciousness-groups; 'and the afflicted mind (<s>kliṣṭa manas</s>) as well' means the mind consisting of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). Those and the four great elements, gathered together into a single mass, are called <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form) by the analogy of a bundle of reeds. Therein, 'name' (<s>nāma</s>) refers to the four formless aggregates — <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), <s>saṃskāra</s> (formations), and <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness). 'Form' (<s>rūpa</s>) refers to what arises from the father's semen and mother's blood; relying on the intermediate existence (<s>antarābhava</s>), the first production of name-and-form — depending on that, the prior production of name-and-form is the mental consciousness (<s>manovijñāna</s>), which is with outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>), of an obstructed-indeterminate nature, constituted by the four afflictions of self-delusion and the like: self-delusion (<s>ātmamoha</s>), self-conceit (<s>ātmamāna</s>), self-view (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>), and self-aggrandizement (<s>ātmotkarṣa</s>). Conjoined with these afflictions, the afflicted mind, gathered into a single mass, is called <s>nāmarūpa</s>.

body.text: dhātūnāṃ sannipātād vai śarīrotpāda iṣyate |
body.translated_text: From the conjunction of the elements indeed, the arising of the body is accepted.

body.text: anantaroditāḥ ṣaḍdhātavaḥ | sannipātād vai iti tu vaikalyābhāvāt | śarīramiti tu bhūta-bhautika-saṃnipāta-piṇḍam | utpādo nāma prādurbhāvaḥ | iṣyate iti tu anumatam | asya kartrādi na vartate iti bhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: The six elements just mentioned — 'from the conjunction indeed' means due to the absence of any deficiency. 'Body' (<s>śarīra</s>) refers to the mass formed by the conjunction of elements and their derivatives. 'Arising' means manifestation. 'Is accepted' means it is approved. The meaning is that there is no agent or the like involved in this.

body.text: ātmātmīyavikalpānāmutpādastairna manyate |
body.translated_text: The arising of conceptualizations of self and mine is not conceived by them.

body.text: iti tu asmābhirete utpāditā iti ca tairvayamutpāditā iti te 'nyonya vikalpaṃ notpādayanti |
body.translated_text: That is to say, they do not generate mutual conceptualization such as 'we have produced these' or 'we have been produced by them.'

body.text: teṣu satsu samutpādaḥ teṣvasatsu na saṃbhavaḥ |
body.translated_text: When those [conditions] are present, there is arising; when they are absent, there is no occurrence.

body.text: pratyayeṣu asatsu śarīrotpādo na yujyate | yadā ādhyātmikapratyayādi-vaikalyābhāvastadā saṃnipātāt śarīramutpadyate | vaikalye śarīraṃ na utpādyate |
body.translated_text: When conditions are absent, the arising of the body is not tenable. When there is no deficiency in the inner conditions and the like, then from their conjunction the body arises. When there is deficiency, the body does not arise.

body.text: naivātmādimayāste hi nāpyanyaccāpi kiñcana |
body.translated_text: They are not constituted by a self or the like, nor is there anything else whatsoever.

body.text: tatra pṛthivīdhātustu nātmā ahaṃmameti manyanā-viyuktatvāt | 'na sattvāstu' citta-mano-vijñāna-viyuktatvāt | na jīvaḥ calatvābhāvāt | na jantustu janyajanaka virahitatvāt | 'na manujo' manuviyuktatvāt | 'na mānava' stu antaḥ sthitamānavāsadṛśatvāt | 'na strī', na pumān - na napuṃsakastu ādhyātmikastrī puruṣa-napuṃsakātmakaḥ | na cāhaṃ mam iti tu ātmātmīya-manyanā-viyuktatvāt |
body.translated_text: Therein, the earth element (<s>pṛthivīdhātu</s>) is not a self, because it is devoid of the thought 'I' and 'mine.' It is 'not a sentient being' because it is devoid of mind (<s>citta</s>), mental faculty (<s>manas</s>), and consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>). It is 'not a life-force' (<s>jīva</s>) because there is no movement. It is 'not a creature' (<s>jantu</s>) because it is devoid of producer and produced. It is 'not a human' (<s>manuja</s>) because it is devoid of <s>Manu</s>. It is 'not a descendant of Manu' (<s>mānava</s>) because it is not similar to the <s>mānava</s> dwelling within. It is 'not female, not male, not neuter' because the inner [element] is not of the nature of female, male, or neuter. 'Not I, not mine' — because it is devoid of the conceptualization of self and what belongs to self.

body.text: nāpyanyaccāpi kiñcana iti tu īśvarādi-kartṛ-kriyā-karma-virahitatvāt | tadvat jalam, agnirvāyurākāśo vijñānadhātuścāpi nātmā, na sattvo, na jīvo, na jantuḥ, na manujo, na mānavo, na strī, na pumān, na napuṃsakam na cāhaṃ na mama syāt | na ceśvarādi anyat kiñcid iti jñātavyam |
body.translated_text: 'Nor is there anything else whatsoever' — because it is devoid of any agent, action, or deed such as <s>Īśvara</s> and the like. Likewise, water, fire, wind, space, and the consciousness element (<s>vijñānadhātu</s>) are also not a self, not a sentient being, not a life-force, not a creature, not a human, not a descendant of Manu, not female, not male, not neuter, and there is neither 'I' nor 'mine.' Nor is there <s>Īśvara</s> or anything else — this should be known.

body.text: yaikapiṇḍādisaṃjñā sāvidyā tribhavachādikā |
body.translated_text: That which is the designation as a single mass and the like — that is <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), which covers the three realms of existence.

body.text: tatra katamāvidyā? ucyate | tribhavachādiketyucyate | tribhavastu bhavatrayam kāmabhavaḥ, rūpabhavaḥ, arūpabhavaśca | te 'pi sattvabhājanaloke vyavahāreṇa dvividhāḥ vyavasthāpitāḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, what is <s>avidyā</s>? It is said: it is called 'that which covers the three realms of existence.' The three realms (<s>tribhava</s>) are the three planes of existence: the desire realm (<s>kāmabhava</s>), the form realm (<s>rūpabhava</s>), and the formless realm (<s>arūpabhava</s>). These too are established as twofold through convention in the world of sentient beings and the world as their vessel.

body.text: atha ca dhātu-gati-yoni-bhedena krama-trayeṇa sthāpitaḥ | kathamiti cet | ucyate - tatra kāmadhātuḥ ṣaṭtriṃśadāśrayanikāyavijñaptyavabhāsaṃ sādhāraṇāsādhāraṇa-svabhāvena ekapiṇḍatvena kalpayan saṃjñayā grahaṇatvād avidyeti ucyate | tatra ṣaṭtriṃśadāśrayanikāyāstu aṣṭau uṣṇasvabhāvā mahānarakāḥ, śītasvabhāvāḥ aṣṭau mahānarakāḥ | saṃjīva-kālasūtra-saṃghāta-raurava-mahāraurava-tapana-pratāpanāvīcayo-'ṣṭoṣṇanarakāḥ | hāhādhara-apapa-aṭaṭa-hāhāvat-arbuda-nirarbuda-padma-mahāpadma-utpalāni śītasvabhāvatvād aṣṭau śītanarakāśca | pratyekaḥ prādeśikaśca narakaḥ, pretāśrayaḥ, tiryagāśrayaḥ, asurāāśrayaḥ | caturdvīpāḥ, aṣṭau antardvīpāśca |
body.translated_text: Furthermore, they are established through three sequences by the distinctions of realms (<s>dhātu</s>), destinies (<s>gati</s>), and modes of birth (<s>yoni</s>). How so? It is said: therein, the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>), conceiving through designation the appearances of consciousness in thirty-six types of bases and groups as a single mass, by its nature of shared and unshared [experiences] — because it grasps through conceptualization, it is called <s>avidyā</s>. Therein, the thirty-six types of bases and groups are: eight great hells of hot nature and eight great hells of cold nature. The eight hot hells are <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, and <s>Avīci</s>. The eight cold hells are <s>Hāhādhara</s>, <s>Apapa</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hāhāvat</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Padma</s>, <s>Mahāpadma</s>, and <s>Utpala</s> — because they are of cold nature. And each has subsidiary hells; the hungry ghost realm (<s>pretāśraya</s>), the animal realm (<s>tiryagāśraya</s>), and the <s>asura</s> realm (<s>asurāśraya</s>). The four continents and the eight sub-continents.

body.text: tatra pretāśrayastu marau aṭavīkāntāre ca | tadbhinnastu vibhāgaḥ - grāma-nagara-nigama-śmaśāna-parvata-aṭavī-karvaṭa-dvīpa-nadī-vāyu-sāgara-palvala-taḍāga-kūpa-udyānasthāna-devālaya-mātṛgṛha-nāgaloka-maru-saras-vṛkṣa-śūnyālaya-mahāpatha-nadītaṭa-araṇyavāsa-prapāta-setu-kaulasthāna-mukha-mahāpatha-āpaṇa-catvara-śrṛṅgāṭaka-pāvanatīrthasthāna-jalāśayādiṣu sthitvā svakarmavaśena vijñaptyavabhāsa-vikalpodbhavānāṃ yadajñānaṃ seyamavidyā ityucyate | tiryaksthānaṃ madhye-sāgaram | yonisthānāni catvāri-aṇḍajo, jarāyujaḥ, saṃsvedajaḥ, upapādukaśca | yonyāśrayabhedena vividhā tiryagjagad vijñaptyavabhāsita-vikalpavāsanāliptasantānāḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, the hungry ghost realm is in deserts and wilderness. Its further classification is: those dwelling in villages, cities, towns, cremation grounds, mountains, forests, hamlets, islands, rivers, winds, oceans, marshes, ponds, wells, gardens, temples, maternal shrines, <s>nāga</s>-worlds, deserts, lakes, trees, empty dwellings, highways, riverbanks, wilderness abodes, precipices, bridges, ancestral places, cave mouths, great roads, shops, crossroads, intersections, sacred pilgrimage sites, and water bodies — whatever ignorance arises through the proliferation of conceptualizations of consciousness-appearances driven by their own <s>karma</s> while dwelling in such places, that is called <s>avidyā</s>. The animal realm is in the mid-ocean. The four modes of birth are: egg-born (<s>aṇḍaja</s>), womb-born (<s>jarāyuja</s>), moisture-born (<s>saṃsvedaja</s>), and spontaneously born (<s>upapāduka</s>). Distinguished by modes of birth, the various beings of the animal world have their continuums tainted by habitual tendencies of conceptualization manifested through consciousness-appearances.

body.text: tadanyathāvibhaktāḥ - gardabha-sūkara-vānara-gaja-uṣṭra-aśva-mṛga-mahiṣa-gau-gavaya-camarī-śva-śrṛgāla-nakula-mūṣaka-siṃha-vyāghra-tarakṣu-ṛkṣa-vṛka-mārjāra-mīna-kacchapa-makara-śiśumāra-sarpa-pipīlikā-lūtā-pataṃga-tittiri-pipīlaka-kṛmi-valmīka-godhā-kīṭa-jalavāsi-śuka-śārikā-kokilā-mayūra-haṃsa-krauñca-vaka-kāka-gṛdhra-ullūka-jīvañjīva-suparṇādayo 'niścita-gatitvāt svakarmavāsanā-pāratantryeṇa avabhāsākāraṃ sthitaṃ tu yadajñānaṃ tadapi avidyā ityucyate | asurāṇāṃ caturāśrayastu sumeroścatuḥ pariṣaṇḍamadhye 'sti |
body.translated_text: Distinguished otherwise, they are: donkeys, pigs, monkeys, elephants, camels, horses, deer, buffaloes, cows, gayal, yak, dogs, jackals, mongooses, mice, lions, tigers, hyenas, bears, wolves, cats, fish, turtles, <s>makaras</s> (sea creatures), crocodiles, serpents, ants, spiders, moths, partridges, termites, worms, anthills, monitors, beetles, aquatic creatures, parrots, <s>śārikā</s>-birds, cuckoos, peacocks, geese, <s>krauñca</s>-herons, egrets, crows, vultures, owls, <s>jīvañjīva</s>-birds, <s>suparṇas</s> (garuḍas), and others — since their destinies are uncertain, whatever ignorance subsists in the form of appearances through the subjection to the habitual tendencies of their own <s>karma</s>, that too is called <s>avidyā</s>. The four abodes of the <s>asuras</s> are in the middle of the four mountain ranges surrounding <s>Sumeru</s>.

body.text: tadbhinnavibhāgena sthitaṃ parvata-aṭavī-vana-udyāna-nadī-grāmādiṣu svakarma-vaśāt prajñaptāvabhāsa-vikalpanodbhūtamanyasthānānāṃ yadajñānaṃ tadapi avidyetyucyate | naraka-sattvānāṃ svakarmavaśitānukūlavikalpanodbhavānāṃ tu anavataptamahāsāgarād viṃśatisāhasra-yojanādhobhājanasya vijñapti-svabhāvamūlabhūteṣu anyasthāneṣvabhi-nirvṛttiḥ | tato 'nyatra pratyekasattvasya narakādi-bhājanasya vijñapti-vikalpanodbhūtasya parvata-aṭavī-maru-darī-prapāta-nadī-tīrādisthānābhinirvṛttaṃ yadajñānamidamapya-vidyetyucyate | catvāro dvīpāstu pūrvasyāṃ videhaḥ, dakṣiṇasyāṃ jambūdvīpaḥ, paścimāyāṃ aparagodānīyaḥ, uttarasyāṃ, ca kururiti | aṣṭāvantardvīpāstu pūrvayāṃ videhaparṣado deho videhaśca | dakṣiṇasyāṃ-jambūdvīpa-parṣadaḥ capalaka uttaramantrī ca | paścimasyāma-paragodānīya-parṣadaḥ cāmaraścāparacāmaraśca |
body.translated_text: Dwelling in various locations distinguished by mountains, forests, groves, gardens, rivers, villages, and the like, through their own <s>karma</s>, whatever ignorance arises from the proliferation of conceptualizations of designated appearances in other realms, that too is called <s>avidyā</s>. For hell beings, driven by the proliferation of conceptualizations favorable to their own <s>karma</s>, manifestation occurs in other places that are the basis of the consciousness-appearance nature, [located] twenty thousand <s>yojanas</s> below the vessel of the great ocean <s>Anavatapta</s>. Beyond that, for each individual being, the ignorance arising from the proliferation of conceptualized consciousness-appearances of their hell-vessel and other realms, manifesting in mountains, forests, deserts, caves, precipices, rivers, banks, and other places — this too is called <s>avidyā</s>. The four continents are: <s>Videha</s> in the east, <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> in the south, <s>Aparagodānīya</s> in the west, and <s>Kuru</s> in the north. The eight sub-continents are: in the east, <s>Deha</s> and <s>Videha</s> of the <s>Videha</s> assembly; in the south, <s>Cāpalaka</s> and <s>Uttaramantrī</s> of the <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> assembly; in the west, <s>Cāmara</s> and <s>Aparacāmara</s> of the <s>Aparagodānīya</s> assembly.

body.text: uttarasyāṃ kuru-parṣadaḥ kuruḥ kauravaśca | tedvīpopadvīpānāṃ prabhedena vividhā-kāreṇa bhinnāḥ | svavijñānāvabhāsavikalpanāvaśenodbhūtaṃ vibhinnaprapaṃca-vāsanāliptaṃ tādṛśaṃ yadajñānam idamapi avidyetyucyate | ṣaḍdevānāṃ sattva-bhājanāvabhāsa-vijñaptyavabhāsaviśeṣa-sādhāraṇāsādhāraṇāśeṣasvabhāveṣu piṇḍagrahaṇa-kalpanā-vaśenodbhūtam yadajñānamidamapi avidyetyucyate | tatra ṣaḍdevanikāyā iti | caturmahārājakāyikāḥ - trāyastriṃśo, yāmaḥ, tuṣito, nirmāṇaratayaḥ paranirmitavaśavartinaśca | anye ca vidyādhara-siddhaḥ, ṛṣirgaruḍa-gandharvaḥ-kinnara-mahoraga, yakṣādayaḥ, nakṣatra-graha-tārā-candra-sūryā saparivārāḥ saprāsādāḥ, utpāda-vināśa-svakarmavaśena vijñaptyākārāvabhāsa-vikalpanā-vāsanānugāmino 'ṇḍaja-jarāyuja-saṃsvedaja-upapādukāśca | yonyāśraya bhedena vividha-tiryagjagad-vijñaptyavabhāsita-vikalpa-vāsanāliptasantānāḥ gadarbha-sūkara-vānara-gaja-uṣṭra-aśva-mṛga-mahiṣa-gau-gavaya-camarī-śva-śrṛgāla-nakula-mūṣaka-siṃha-vyāghra-tarakṣu-ṛkṣa-vṛka-mārjāra-mīna-kacchapa-makara-śiśumāra-sarpa-pipīlikā-lūtā-pataṃga-tittiri-pipīlaka-kṛmi-vālmīki-godhā-yūkā-kīṭa-jalavāsi-śuka-śārikā-kokila-mayūra-haṃsa-krauñca-vaka-kāka-gṛdhra-ulūka-jīvañjīva-suparṇādayo-'niścitagatitvāt svakarma-vāsanāpāratantryeṇa prajñaptyavabhāsākāra-sthitāḥ | evaṃ pṛthaggati-yoni-bahutva-bhedena vibhinna-sattvabhājanalokā ityākhyātāḥ sādhāraṇā-sādhāraṇaviśeṣādipiṇḍagrahodbhūta ekataḥ saṃkṣipya kāmadhāturityucyate | parañcoktam -
body.translated_text: In the north are the <s>Kuru</s> assembly — <s>Kuru</s> and <s>Kaurava</s>. These are divided in various ways by the classification of continents and sub-continents. Whatever ignorance has arisen through the force of one's own consciousness-appearance-conceptualization, smeared with the <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impressions) of differentiated <s>prapañca</s> (phenomenal proliferation) — this too is called <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). Whatever ignorance has arisen through the force of grasping aggregates and conceptualization regarding the shared and unshared natures of the appearance of beings and receptacle-worlds and the specific consciousness-appearances of the six [classes of] gods — this too is called <s>avidyā</s>. Therein, the six classes of gods are: the <s>Cāturmahārājikāyika</s> gods, <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, and <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>. And others: <s>Vidyādharas</s>, <s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Ṛṣis</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, etc., constellations, planets, stars, moon, and sun with their retinues and palaces — all following consciousness-appearance-conceptualization-<s>vāsanā</s> through the power of their own <s>karma</s> of arising and destruction, whether egg-born, womb-born, moisture-born, or spontaneously born. By the division of womb-bases, the various animal realms — donkeys, pigs, monkeys, elephants, camels, horses, deer, buffalo, cows, wild oxen, yaks, dogs, jackals, mongooses, mice, lions, tigers, leopards, bears, wolves, cats, fish, turtles, sea-monsters, crocodiles, serpents, ants, spiders, moths, partridges, termites, worms, wasps, monitor lizards, lice, beetles, aquatic creatures, parrots, mynas, cuckoos, peacocks, geese, cranes, herons, crows, vultures, owls, <s>jīvañjīvas</s>, <s>suparṇas</s>, etc. — their continuums smeared with conceptualization-<s>vāsanā</s> illuminated by the consciousness-appearance of the various animal worlds, being of uncertain destination, abide in the form of designation-appearance through dependence on their own <s>karma</s>-<s>vāsanā</s>. Thus, by the division of the multiplicity of different destinies and birth-types, the differentiated world of beings and receptacle-world is described; arising from the grasping of shared and unshared particulars etc., condensing all together, it is called the <s>kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm). And furthermore it is said:

body.text:
dhātugatiyonibhedaiḥ kāmabhavastu ṣaṭtriṃśat |
narā dvādaśa, ṣaḍ devāḥ ṣoḍaśa narakāstathā |
body.translated_text:
By the divisions of realm, destiny, and birth-type, the <s>kāmabhava</s> (desire existence) has thirty-six [divisions]:
twelve for humans, six for gods, and sixteen for hells likewise,

body.text: sāsurapretatiryañcaḥ |
body.translated_text: together with <s>asuras</s>, <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), and animals.

body.text: tādṛśa-vibhinna-vikalpavāsanodbhūtaṃ yadajñānam, aparicchinnam, avyaktā-varaṇam, anavabodham, aparijñātāmisraṃ pūrvānta-aparānta-madhya-hetu-karma-phala-satya-ratna-duḥkha-samudaya-nirodha-mārgakaṃ yadajñānaṃ sāvidyā| tridhātvavacchādi ketyucyate | tasmāt sūtre- yeṣāmeva ṣaṇṇāṃ dhātūnāmeka-saṃjñā, piṇḍasaṃjñā, nityasaṃjñā, dhruvasaṃjñā, śāśvatasaṃjñā, sukhasaṃjñā, ātmasaṃjñā, satva(saṃjñā), jīva(saṃjñā), puruṣasaṃjñā, pudgala(saṃjñā), manuja(saṃjñā), mānava(saṃjñā), ahaṃkāra-mamakārasaṃjñā | evamādi vividhamajñānamiyamucyate 'vidyeti deśitam | tatra pṛthivīdhātoraṣṭadravyatvād ekasaṃjñā na yujyate | paramāṇūnāṃ parasparaṃ saṃcayātmakatvāt piṇḍagrāho na yujyate | hetupratyayayoḥ sambaddhapravṛteḥ nityasaṃjñā na yujyate | cirakālam asthitatvād dhruvasaṃjñā na yujyate | sahotpāda-vināśatvān na śāśvatasaṃjñā | saṃskāra-vipariṇāma-duḥkhānvitatvān na sukhasaṃjñā | ṣaṭtriṃśad-vidhāśucidravyasamavāyān na śuci saṃjñā | bhūta-bhautika-dravya-vaipulyān na ātmasaṃjñā | cittacaitasikādhiṣṭhānatvān na sattvasaṃjñā | kriyābhāvān na jīvasaṃjñā | api ca | gamanāgamanarahitatvān na pudgalasaṃjñā asti | ahaṃmamamanyanāvirahitvān na manuja-mānavasaṃjñā | ahaṃmametyādi-rahitatvān manujādisaṃjñā na yujyate | evaṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ dhātūnāṃ tadanityādisvabhāvasya yadajñānaṃ iyamavidyetyucyate |
body.translated_text: Whatever ignorance has arisen from such differentiated conceptualization-<s>vāsanā</s> — unlimited, with unclear obscuration, without understanding, with unrecognized darkness regarding the past, the future, the middle, cause, <s>karma</s>, fruit, truth, the [three] jewels, suffering, origination, cessation, and the path — that ignorance is <s>avidyā</s>. It is said to encompass the three realms. Therefore in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'With regard to those very six <s>dhātus</s> (elements), the perception of unity, the perception of aggregation, the perception of permanence, the perception of stability, the perception of eternality, the perception of pleasure, the perception of self, the perception of being, the perception of soul, the perception of person, the perception of individual, the perception of human, the perception of descendant, the perception of ego-making and mine-making — such various ignorance is taught as <s>avidyā</s>.' Therein, since the earth element consists of eight substances, the perception of unity is not tenable. Since atoms are mutually aggregative in nature, grasping them as a mass is not tenable. Since [things] operate connected with causes and conditions, the perception of permanence is not tenable. Since they do not abide for a long time, the perception of stability is not tenable. Since they arise and perish simultaneously, the perception of eternality [is not tenable]. Since they are pervaded by the suffering of formations and transformation, the perception of pleasure [is not tenable]. Since they consist of the combination of thirty-six impure substances, the perception of purity [is not tenable]. Since they consist of the abundance of elemental and derivative substances, the perception of self [is not tenable]. Since they are governed by mind and mental factors, the perception of a being [is not tenable]. Since there is no [independent] activity, the perception of a soul [is not tenable]. Moreover, since they are devoid of coming and going, the perception of a person does not exist. Since they are not free from the conceptualization of 'I' and 'mine' and others, the perception of human and descendant [is not tenable]. Since they are devoid of 'I,' 'mine,' etc., the perception of human etc. is not tenable. Thus, whatever ignorance of the nature of impermanence etc. of the six <s>dhātus</s> — this is called <s>avidyā</s>.

body.text: tatra avidyeti tu vidyā na bhūtatvād avidyā | na tu vidyābhāvaḥ, abhāvastu na kiñcidapi | avidyā vidyābhinnā vidyāntaramevasti | tasmād abhāvo niṣedho 'pi nāsti, paratvamapi nāsti | atha kimiti cet? virodhaḥ | avidyā tu na vidyābhāvaḥ vidyādharmato viruddhā avidyeti ucyate | paranirmitavaśavarti taddevo - pariprabhṛti saptadaśāśrayākāravijñaptyavabhāso rūpadhātuḥ | tadudbhavaḥ sattva bhājanaloka-svabhāvaḥ sādhāraṇaḥ, asādhāraṇaśca viśeṣavikalpavaśasambhavaḥ | āśrayāstu caturdhyānānāṃ trividhabhāvanānvitatvād brahmakāyikādayo dvādaśa, caturthadhyānasya miśrabhāvanānvitatvāt pañcāvāsāḥ pañcaśuddhāvāsāḥ | tatra prathame tu brahmakāyika-brahmapurohita-mahābrahmāṇaḥ | dvitīye tu parīttābha-apramāṇābha-ābhāsvarāḥ | tṛtīyestu parīttaśubha-apramāṇaśubha-śubhakṛtsnāḥ | caturthe -anabhraka-puṇyaprasava-bṛhatphalāḥ | śuddhāvāsāstu avṛha-atapa-sudarśana-sudṛga-kaniṣṭhāḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, '<s>avidyā</s>' means: <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) is not [real], because of its non-true nature, hence <s>avidyā</s>. But it is not [merely] the absence of <s>vidyā</s>, for absence is nothing at all. <s>Avidyā</s> is not different from <s>vidyā</s>; it is merely another [form of] <s>vidyā</s>. Therefore neither is there negation as absence, nor is there otherness. If one asks: then what? [The answer is:] contradiction. <s>Avidyā</s> is not the absence of <s>vidyā</s>; it is called <s>avidyā</s> because it is contrary to the nature of <s>vidyā</s>. From <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>, that god, onward — [the realm] with seventeen support-form-consciousness-appearances is the <s>rūpadhātu</s> (form realm). The world of beings and receptacle-world arising from that, with its shared and unshared natures arising from the force of particular conceptualization. The supports of the four <s>dhyānas</s>, being pervaded by three types of cultivation, are the twelve [heavens] beginning with <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, and since the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> is pervaded by mixed cultivation, there are five ordinary abodes and five pure abodes (<s>Śuddhāvāsa</s>). Therein, in the first [<s>dhyāna</s>]: <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>. In the second: <s>Parīttābha</s>, <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>. In the third: <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>. In the fourth: <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>. And the pure abodes: <s>Avṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>.

body.text: caturdhyānabhūmayaḥ-savitarka-avitarka-sukha-upekṣāsaṃprayuktāḥ-dhyānāntara-anāgamyabhūmaya imā yā ajñānam, adarśanam, anabhisamitā imā apyavidyetyucyante | yāśca nāmamātraṃ saṃjñāvabhāsa-vijñapti-vikalpodbhavāḥ catasra ārūpyasamāpattaya ākāśa-vijñānākiñcana-naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanam yaccājñāna-anabhisamiti-adarśana-midamapyavidyetyucyate | tasmādeva bhagavatā-
body.translated_text: The grounds of the four <s>dhyānas</s> — associated with <s>vitarka</s> (applied thought), without <s>vitarka</s>, with <s>sukha</s> (pleasure), and with <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity) — the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s> and the <s>anāgamya</s> (preparatory) ground: whatever in these is non-knowledge, non-seeing, non-comprehension — these too are called <s>avidyā</s>. And the four formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>) — the sphere of infinite space, infinite consciousness, nothingness, and neither-perception-nor-non-perception — arising from mere name, designation-appearance-consciousness-conceptualization: whatever in these is non-knowledge, non-comprehension, non-seeing — this too is called <s>avidyā</s>. Therefore by the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

body.text:
caturdhyānānyānāgamyamāntarā bhūmayastathā |
ārūpyāyāḥ samāpatteḥ pṛthaksaṃjñācatuṣṭayam |
caturbhuvo viśuddhīnāṃ daśabhūdeśanātmikam |
maheśaprāptisaṃsthānaṃ tattu nānyattridhātutaḥ |
svacittayogayogeśo viśuddhayudbhavabhūstathā |
jñānaṃ samādhiḥ rūpaṃ ca vaśitāprativedinaḥ | ityuktam |
body.translated_text:
The four <s>dhyānas</s>, the <s>anāgamya</s>, and the intermediate grounds likewise,
the four distinct perceptions of the formless attainment,
the four existences, the teaching of the ten grounds of purification,
the attainment and configuration of <s>Maheśa</s> (great lordship) — that is none other than the three realms.
The lord of the yoga of one's own mind, and the ground of arising of purity likewise,
knowledge, <s>samādhi</s>, form, and mastery — for those who have realized [them]. Thus it is stated.

body.text: tatrāpi yadakliṣṭamajñānam, adarśanam, anabhisaṃmatam, anavabodhabhāvanāmārga-jñānotpāda-bādhakaṃ tadapyavidyā ityucyate | tasmādavidyātamastimirapaṭalena nayanāvṛtatvād viṣayeṣu rūpa-śabda-gandha-rasa-sparśa-dharmākāravijñaptiviparyaya-vikalpavāsanāvabhāsatvena nitya-ātma-sukha-śucyādi-viparyāsatvād rāga-dveṣa-moha-vistārād rāgajaṃ karmāpi abhisaṃskaroti | iṣṭavighātakatvād dveṣotpannaṃ karmāpi abhisaṃskaroti | amārge mārgasaṃjñatvād, aśuciṣu śucisaṃjñatvād, amuktau mukti saṃjñatvācca mohajamapi abhisaṃskaroti | taddvayavyāvṛttyā aniñjyamapi abhisaṃskaroti |
body.translated_text: Therein too, whatever non-afflicted ignorance — non-seeing, non-comprehension — that obstructs the arising of knowledge on the <s>bhāvanāmārga</s> (path of cultivation), that too is called <s>avidyā</s>. Therefore, because the eyes are covered by the darkness, obscurity, and veil of <s>avidyā</s>, through the appearance of <s>vāsanā</s> of conceptual inversion of form, sound, smell, taste, touch, and mental objects in the sense-fields — due to the inversion of [seeing things as] permanent, self, pleasant, and pure — from the expansion of <s>rāga</s> (attachment), <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), and <s>moha</s> (delusion), one fashions (<s>abhisaṃskaroti</s>) <s>karma</s> born of attachment. Because [sense objects] are obstructors of what is desired, one fashions <s>karma</s> born of aversion. Because of perceiving a path where there is no path, purity where there is impurity, and liberation where there is no liberation, one fashions [<s>karma</s>] born of delusion. By the avoidance of both of those [attachment and aversion], one fashions the imperturbable (<s>āninjya</s>) as well.

body.text: tatpratyayāt tannidānācca vidyāyāṃ rāga-dveṣa-moha-ahaṃkāra-dṛṣṭi-saṃśaya-īrṣyā-mātsaryānugāmanād akuśala-kāyakarmata ātmano jñānasya ca paritrāṇārtha prāṇātipātaḥ adattādānaṃ, kāmamithyācāraḥ, unmādahetukaṃ madyapānam anyathā-nīpsita-vipākābhinirvartanamapi abhisaṃskaroti | vāco mṛṣāvāda-paiśunya-pāruṣya-pralāpairaniṣṭavipākābhinirvartanamapi abhisaṃskaroti | mānasa-karmaṇo 'bhidhyā-vyāpāda-mithyādṛṣṭi-samprayogo 'pi abhisaṃskaroti | kāya-vāk-citta-duścarita-dharma-samādāna-hetubhiḥ sattvāḥ naraka-preta-tiryag-deva-manuṣyāsureṣu utpatsyante | tasmāda-jñāna-viṣaye rāga-dveṣa mohādiḥ pratyakṣaḥ, ityuktam | tatra avidyayā iti avidyā-pratyayena saṃskārabhāvābhisaṃskāritvād vibhāvitaṃ saṃskārabhāva-prativijñaptisvabhāvaṃ vijñānamabhinirvartate | tasmādeva
body.translated_text: From that condition and that cause, following upon <s>avidyā</s> through attachment, aversion, delusion, ego, views, doubt, jealousy, and stinginess — from unwholesome bodily <s>karma</s>, for the sake of protecting oneself and one's knowledge, one fashions killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, drinking liquor that causes madness, and the production of undesired results. Through the speech [actions of] lying, slander, harsh speech, and idle chatter, one fashions the production of unpleasant results. Through mental <s>karma</s>, one fashions the conjunction of covetousness, ill-will, and wrong views. Through the causes of bodily, verbal, and mental misconduct and the undertaking of [unwholesome] <s>dharmas</s>, beings will be born among hell-beings, <s>pretas</s>, animals, gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>. Therefore, in the domain of ignorance, attachment, aversion, delusion, etc. are directly perceived — thus it is stated. Therein, 'conditioned by <s>avidyā</s>' means: because <s>avidyā</s> as condition fashions the <s>saṃskāra</s>-nature, <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) arises, whose nature is the counter-cognition of the <s>saṃskāra</s>-nature. Therefore:

body.text: tataḥ saṃskṛtabhāvānāṃ jñaptirvijñānasaṃbhavā |
body.translated_text: From that, the cognition of conditioned things is the arising of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness).

body.text: iti uktam | tataḥ iti tu saṃskāramāśritya bhāvānāṃ vijñaptiriti tu vijñāpakatvād vijñaptiḥ | vijñāne karmavāsanā-sthāpanam ityadhivacanam |
body.translated_text: Thus it is stated. 'From that' means: depending on <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), the cognition (<s>vijñapti</s>) of things — '<s>vijñapti</s>' because of its nature of making known. The designation means: the depositing of <s>karma</s>-<s>vāsanā</s> (action-impressions) in consciousness.

body.text: vijñānena sahodbhūtāścatusskandhā arūpiṇaḥ |
body.translated_text: Together with <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) arise the four formless <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates).

body.text: iti vijñānena sahodgatā iti tu vijñānasya hetuta udbhūtāḥ | catuḥskandhā arūpiṇaḥ | iti tu catvāro vijñāna-skandhāḥ vedanā-saṃjñā-saṃskāra-vijñānamityādayaḥ | arūpiṇastu-bhūta-bhautika-saṃcayākāra-rahitatvāt santi, na tu nityam |
body.translated_text: "Arisen together with <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness)" means arisen from <s>vijñāna</s> as their cause. The four <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) are formless — that is, the four <s>vijñāna-skandhas</s> (consciousness-aggregates) are <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), <s>saṃskāra</s> (formations), and <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), and so forth. They are "formless" because they are devoid of the form of accumulation of gross and subtle elements, yet they exist, though not permanently.

body.text: atha kimiti cet? cittacaitasikasvabhāvo 'sti | skandhatvaṃ tu vipula-dravyātmakatvāt | rūpaṃ tu dhātucatuṣṭayam | pitṛmātṛ-śukraśoṇitodbhūtāḥ pṛthivyāpte-jovāyudhātavaḥ | tān saṃgṛhya vijñānapratyayaṃ nāmarūpamityucyate |
body.translated_text: Then what is their nature? Their nature is that of <s>citta</s> (mind) and <s>caitasika</s> (mental factors). Their aggregate-nature is due to being constituted of manifold substances. <s>Rūpa</s> (form), however, consists of the four <s>dhātus</s> (elements) — the elements of earth, water, fire, and air, which arise from the father's and mother's semen and blood. Encompassing all of these, it is called "<s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form) conditioned by <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness)."

body.text: nāmarūpamupādāya cendriyāyatanodbhavaḥ |
body.translated_text: Depending on <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form), there arises the sense-faculty bases.

body.text: iti yatpūrvaṃ indriye satṛṣṇavāsanānāmarūpaṃ sthāpitaṃ tannāmarūpaṃ saṃniśritya cakṣurādi-ṣaḍindriyābhinirvartanena indriyasya ṣaḍāyatanāni prādurbhavantīti | indriya-ṣaḍāyatanāni ṣaḍvijñānāśritāni | rūpādi-viṣayālambana-vijñaptyavabhāsagrahaṇa-svabhāvānāmabhinirvartanād bhagavatā
body.translated_text: That is, the <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form) with craving-imprints that was previously established in the sense faculties — depending on that <s>nāmarūpa</s>, through the production of the six sense faculties beginning with the eye, the six <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases) of the faculties come into being. The six <s>āyatanas</s> of the faculties are the supports of the six <s>vijñānas</s> (consciousnesses). Because they produce the nature of apprehending the appearance of cognition that takes objects such as form and so forth as its support, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) said:

body.text:
nāmarūpasaṃniśritānīndriyāṇi ṣaḍāyatanamityuktam |
viṣayendriyavijñāna-saṃghātāt sparśa sambhavaḥ |
body.translated_text: "The six <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases) are the faculties that depend on <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form)." From the conjunction of object, sense faculty, and consciousness, <s>sparśa</s> (contact) arises.

body.text: ṣaḍindriyāyatanam apekṣya viṣayeṣu indriyavijñānasaṃnipātāt sparśaḥ | indriyavijñānaṃ rūpādiviṣayeṣu sparśa iva nirāntarameva pravartate | atra sparśastu kiñcidapi nāsti | asaṃcita-pañcavijñānāni saṃcita viṣayendriyaiḥ saha yugapadekatra bhūtatvāt sparśavanti santi, na tu sparśa ityucyate | tasmādeva bhagavatāpi trayāṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ saṃnipātaḥ sparśa ityuktam | ālambanāvabhāsākāreṇa sparśo jātaḥ | tadvat sparśarasāsvādaniyantraṇe ṣaṭsparśā kāyānāśritya ṣaḍvedanākāyā utpadyante | tasmād vedanā sparśajā jñeyā | ityuktam | vedanā tu sparśeṇa janitā sparśahetūdbhavā ityadhivacanam |
body.translated_text: In dependence on the six sense-faculty <s>āyatanas</s> (bases), <s>sparśa</s> (contact) arises from the coming together of sense faculty, consciousness, and objects. The sense-faculty consciousness operates continuously upon objects such as form, as if touching them. Yet here, <s>sparśa</s> (contact) itself is not a separate thing. The five unaccumulated <s>vijñānas</s> (consciousnesses), together with the accumulated objects and sense faculties, are endowed with contact because they simultaneously exist as one — yet this is not called "<s>sparśa</s>" as a separate entity. Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) also said, "The coming together of three <s>dharmas</s> is <s>sparśa</s> (contact)." <s>Sparśa</s> arises in the form of the appearance of the apprehended object. Likewise, due to the inability to restrain the relishing of the sensation of contact, the six <s>sparśa</s>-groups give rise to the six <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) groups based on the body. Therefore it is said, "<s>Vedanā</s> (feeling) should be known as born from <s>sparśa</s> (contact)." <s>Vedanā</s> is generated by <s>sparśa</s> — this is a designation meaning "arisen from the cause of contact."

body.text: tatra vedaneti tadvedayitṛtvād vedanā | vedanānubhavaḥ | sukha-duḥkha-aduḥkhāsukhā-saumanasya-daurmanasya-viśiṣṭāḥ | vedanāvabhāsākāravijñapti vikalpanāvaśodbhūtānāṃ trivargabhedena ṣaḍvedanākāyotpādād bhagavatā sparśasahabhavā vedanetyuktam | tadvat kiñcidvedanāsvādasaktā abhiniveśātmikā hi vedanāhetukī tṛṣṇeti tṛṣṇodbhavaḥ | tasmādeva tṛṣṇa ca vedanodgatā ityuktam |
body.translated_text: Therein, "<s>vedanā</s> (feeling)" is so called because it is that which feels; <s>vedanā</s> is experience. It is distinguished as pleasant, painful, neither-painful-nor-pleasant, mental pleasure, and mental displeasure. Because of the arising of the six <s>vedanā</s> groups through the threefold division arising from the power of conceptual proliferation of the cognitive appearance of <s>vedanā</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) said, "<s>Vedanā</s> (feeling) is co-arisen with <s>sparśa</s> (contact)." Likewise, that which is attached to the relishing of some feeling, which has the nature of clinging — since <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) has <s>vedanā</s> as its cause, <s>tṛṣṇā</s> arises. Therefore it is said, "<s>Tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) too arises from <s>vedanā</s> (feeling)."

body.text: tṛṣṇeti tridhāturāgaḥ | rāgo 'dhyavasānam, abhilāṣaḥ, āsaktiraviyogākāṃkṣā, nandanaṃ, prema ityadhivacanam | sā ca indriyaviṣayavijñānabhedena tṛṣṇākāyaḥ ṣaḍdhā vyavasthāpitā | tṛṣṇāvabhāsākāra-vijñapti-vaśodbhūta ṣaṭtṛṣṇā-kāyotpādāt sugatena vedanādhyavasānā tṛṣṇetyuktam | evam adhyavasita-tṛṣṇāvṛddhirupādānam | tasmāt tṛṣṇāvṛddhirupādānam ityuktam |
body.translated_text: <s>Tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) is attachment to the three realms. <s>Rāga</s> (attachment) has the synonyms: determination, desire, clinging, longing for non-separation, delight, and affection. It is established sixfold as the <s>tṛṣṇā</s>-group according to the division of sense faculty, object, and consciousness. Because of the arising of the six <s>tṛṣṇā</s> groups produced by the power of the cognitive appearance of <s>tṛṣṇā</s>, the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One) said, "<s>Tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) is the determination of <s>vedanā</s> (feeling)." Thus, the increase of determined <s>tṛṣṇā</s> is <s>upādāna</s> (grasping). Therefore it is said, "The increase of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) is <s>upādāna</s> (grasping)."

body.text: tṛṣṇā rāgāliṅgitasya iṣṭāviyogasya hetuḥ | kuśalamakuśalama-vyākṛtādi tūpādānam | upādānārthena upādānam | upapañcamādānaṃ upādānam | yathāgṛhīta-svakarma-pathyadanasya paravaśād upādānādutpādaḥ punarbhava ityucyate | tasmādeva upādānodgato bhava ityuktam |
body.translated_text: <s>Tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) is the cause of non-separation from the desired, for one embraced by <s>rāga</s> (attachment). <s>Upādāna</s> (grasping) includes the wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate. <s>Upādāna</s> is so called in the sense of appropriating. <s>Upādāna</s> is the five-fold appropriation. Just as the arising of renewed existence occurs through the appropriation, under the power of others, of the eating of food suitable to one's own <s>karma</s> (actions) as grasped — this is called <s>punarbhava</s> (renewed existence). Therefore it is said, "<s>Bhava</s> (existence) arises from <s>upādāna</s> (grasping)."

body.text: svakarmavāsanāyā yathāvadavabhāsākāra-vijñapti-vikalpanā-vaśenodbhūtasya punarbhavasyābhinirvartanād bhava iti, purnarbhūtatvāt | yathāvat svakarma-vāsanāvaśena iti kuśalākuśalāneñjya-karmavāsanāvaśenetyadhivacanam | evaṃ karmabhavastu hetuḥ syāt | skandhotpādo bhavājjātaḥ | karmabhavasya taddhetoḥ skandhotpādo jātirityucyate | tatra skandhotpādastu skandhānāmutpādaḥ|
body.translated_text: <s>Bhava</s> (existence) is so called because of the production of renewed existence, arisen through the power of conceptual proliferation of cognitive appearances according to the imprints of one's own <s>karma</s> (actions), and because it is a state of becoming again. "According to the imprints of one's own <s>karma</s>" is a designation meaning "through the power of the imprints of wholesome, unwholesome, and unshakeable <s>karma</s>." Thus <s>karmabhava</s> (karmic existence) is the cause. The arising of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) is born from <s>bhava</s> (existence). The arising of the <s>skandhas</s> from that cause, <s>karmabhava</s>, is called <s>jāti</s> (birth). Therein, the arising of the <s>skandhas</s> means the production of the aggregates.

body.text: dhātvāyatanaprāptirapi saṃkṣepeṇa jātirityucyate | tatra skandhastu anekadravyasaṃrāśyarthastu skandhārthaḥ | athavā anityatayaiva dhvaṃsatvāt, utpādānantarameva anityatārākṣasena bhakṣaṇaṃ, pratihananaṃ, vināśanam ityadhivacanam | evamabhinirvṛttau utpādahetunā jātipratyayena jaraiva abhinirvartate, tasmādeva jāterevaṃ jarāpi ca ityuktam |
body.translated_text: The attainment of <s>dhātus</s> (elements) and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases) is also, in brief, called <s>jāti</s> (birth). Therein, <s>skandha</s> (aggregate) means a heap of many substances — that is the meaning of "aggregate." Or alternatively, because of destruction through impermanence itself, immediately after arising there is devouring by the demon of impermanence — this is a designation for striking down and destruction. Thus, through the cause of arising in manifest existence, through the condition of <s>jāti</s> (birth), <s>jarā</s> (aging) itself comes into being. Therefore it is said, "From <s>jāti</s> (birth), thus <s>jarā</s> (aging) also arises."

body.text: jātipratyayābhinirvartitaskandhānāṃ jīrṇatā tu jarā | daurbalya-khālitya-pālitya-balikāpūrṇatā-vibhugnatā-kubjatva-daurbalya-kharakharatva-daṇḍāvaṣṭambha caryāvyakti-indriyabhraṃśa-smṛtibhraṃśāḥ iti tādṛśī tu jāti-pratyayena bhinirvartita-skandhānāṃ svakarmākāriṇī vijñaptyavabhāsa-vikalpanāvāsanā-vaśenotpannā jīrṇatā jaretyucyate | evaṃ jarājīrṇa-skandhānyathātvaṃ maraṇamityucyate | tasmādevoktam -
body.translated_text: <s>Jarā</s> (aging) is the deterioration of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) produced by the condition of <s>jāti</s> (birth). It includes: weakness, loss of hair, graying, filling of wrinkles, becoming bent, hunchback, debility, roughness, reliance on a walking stick, unclear movement, decay of the sense faculties, and loss of memory. Such aging is the deterioration produced by the power of the imprints of conceptual proliferation of the cognitive appearance of the activity of one's own <s>karma</s> upon the <s>skandhas</s> produced by the condition of <s>jāti</s> (birth) — this is called <s>jarā</s> (aging). Thus, the alteration of the <s>skandhas</s> worn down by <s>jarā</s> (aging) is called <s>maraṇa</s> (death). Therefore it is said:

body.text: skandhābhāvo jarāyā yaḥ sa mṛtyuścetyudīryate |
body.translated_text: "That which is the cessation of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) due to <s>jarā</s> (aging) — that is declared to be <s>mṛtyu</s> (death)."

body.text: tatra jareti ślathībhūta-jarāpratyayena maraṇasaṃbhavaḥ | tatra maraṇamiti skandhānyathātvam | maraṇa-mṛta-kālakṛta-paralokagamana-saṃkrānti-gati-skandha-vidhvaṃsana-skandhanāśa-āyuḥkṣaya-jīvendriyanirodhetyetādṛśādi-saṃgraho jarāmaraṇam | maraṇāvabhāsākāra-vijñaptivikalpanāvaśena udbhūtaḥ skandhanāśo maraṇam | antāvasthā, antaśayanaṃ, vijñānasaṃkramaṇaṃ, ūṣmahāniḥ, āyurviyogaḥ, kāyikānukaulyatyāgaḥ, bhavasaṃkrāntiḥ, yaśca vijñānāntimāvasthāśrayocchedādyutpanno bahudhāpralāpaḥ, grahaṇam, daurbalyaṃ, parijīrṇatā, dainyaṃ, nirodhānirodhakaḥ, mukhadaurvarṇyaṃ, anāthatā, svakarmavikalpanodbhūta-yamapuruṣaiḥ paraspara-samādānāvabhāsavijñaptiḥ, svalpamātrao-prāṇāvaśeṣe śvāsapraśvāsodbhavā aratiḥ, prakampaḥ, kaṇṭhapariśoṣaṇam, nāsikācchedaḥ, svedaḥ, kledo malaṃ, svamūtroccāra-lālāśarīralepaḥ, niḥsahāyo, mahāndhakāra-prapāta-parvata-pariṣaṇḍa-gahanāṭavī-śūnyālaya-gṛha-prāsāda-ūrdhva-maṇḍapa-kūṭāgāra-agni-kuṇḍa-mahāhrada-palālaskandhagamanam iva cittaviparyastasya skandhāntaragrahaṇaṃ maraṇamityucyate |
body.translated_text: Therein, through <s>jarā</s> (aging) — through the condition of aging that has become enfeebled — <s>maraṇa</s> (death) occurs. Therein, <s>maraṇa</s> (death) is the alteration of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates). The aggregate term <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> (aging-and-death) includes: dying, being dead, having time run out, departure to the next world, transmigration, passing on, destruction of the <s>skandhas</s>, annihilation of the <s>skandhas</s>, exhaustion of the lifespan, and cessation of the life-faculty. <s>Maraṇa</s> is the destruction of the <s>skandhas</s> arisen through the power of conceptual proliferation of the cognitive appearance of death. The final stage, the last resting, the transmigration of consciousness, the loss of bodily warmth, separation from the lifespan, abandonment of bodily comfort, transmigration between existences, and the manifold delirious raving arisen from the severance of the final support of consciousness — grasping, weakness, complete decay, wretchedness, cessation without a cessator, pallor of the face, helplessness, the cognitive appearance of mutual encounter with the messengers of <s>Yama</s> (the lord of death) arisen from the conceptualization of one's own <s>karma</s>, discontent arising from the breathing in and out when only a small measure of life-breath remains, trembling, drying of the throat, obstruction of the nostrils, sweat, moisture, filth, smearing of the body with one's own urine, excrement, and saliva, being without a helper — and like entering into great darkness, a precipice, a mountain, a dense thicket, an impenetrable forest, an empty dwelling, a house, a palace, an upper pavilion, a tower chamber, a fire pit, a great lake, or a heap of straw — the grasping of another set of <s>skandhas</s> by one whose mind is deluded is called <s>maraṇa</s> (death).

body.text: mūḍhe tu maraṇācchokaḥ | iti satṛṣṇasya antardāhaḥ śokaḥ | antardāhaśca cittaparitāpaḥ | śocanārthena śokaḥ | atha mama priyavastu-iṣṭavastu-viyogo bhaviṣyati iti khidyamānasya santāpācchoka ityucyate | yathākarmodgatākārāvabhāsa-vijñaptyābhibhūtasya ānanda-bhaya-aniṣṭākārotpanno marmoccheda-duḥkha-citta-khedodbhūta-śokāntarotthaḥ-aho, hāhā, kiṃ, kena, katham, kutra śaraṇaṃ gatvā paśyāmi, iha gacchāmi, gato 'ham, gṛhītaḥ, hataḥ, mṛtaḥ, bhakṣitaḥ, vinaṣṭaḥ, pranaṣṭaḥ, aho mātaḥ, aho pitaḥ, bhrātaḥ, bhagini, putra, putri, he bhārya iti anekadhā pralāpo mithyāpadanirnādotpannaḥ pailottakasaṃtāpo daurmanasyam | tasmāt śokataścāpalāpo yo daurmanasyaṃ sa ucyate | ityuktam |
body.translated_text: For the deluded one, from <s>maraṇa</s> (death) arises <s>śoka</s> (grief). That is, for one who has craving, the inner burning is <s>śoka</s> (grief). Inner burning is the torment of the mind. <s>Śoka</s> is so called in the sense of grieving. When one is distressed thinking, "I shall be separated from my beloved and desired things," the anguish from that torment is called <s>śoka</s> (grief). For one overwhelmed by cognitive appearances arisen in the form of one's own <s>karma</s>, when there arises the unwanted form of joy and fear, the grief that wells up from within through the piercing of the vital points, the suffering of the mind, and mental distress — "Alas! Oh! What? By whom? How? Where shall I go for refuge? Let me look! I go here! I am gone! I am seized! I am slain! I am dead! I am devoured! I am destroyed! I am lost! O mother! O father! O brother! O sister! O son! O daughter! O wife!" — such manifold <s>pralāpa</s> (lamentation) produces false utterances and cries, and the anguish like that of a cotton-stuffed doll is <s>daurmanasya</s> (mental displeasure). Therefore it is said, "From <s>śoka</s> (grief), <s>pralāpa</s> (lamentation), and that which is <s>daurmanasya</s> (mental displeasure) — these are declared."

body.text:
daurmanasyasamudbhūtaṃ pañcavijñānakāyikam |
āsātaṃ duḥkhamityuktaṃ kāyasaukhyavidhātakam |
body.translated_text: That which arises from <s>daurmanasya</s> (mental displeasure), pertaining to the five consciousness-groups, the unpleasant is called <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering) — it is that which destroys bodily happiness.

body.text: daurmanasya-samudbhūtam iti tu daurmanasyād eva | paṃcavijñānakāyikamiti tu manojña-rūpa-śabda-gandha-rasa-sparśānusmaraṇopapannaṃ pañcavijñānakāyaduḥkham upaghātakam | āsātamanubhava-kāyasaukhya-vighātātmakaṃ duḥkhākārāvabhāsa-vijñapti-vaśenodbhūtaṃ duḥkhamityucyate |
body.translated_text: "Arisen from <s>daurmanasya</s> (mental displeasure)" means indeed from <s>daurmanasya</s> itself. "Pertaining to the five consciousness-groups" means the <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering) of the five consciousness-groups that is connected with the recollection of pleasant forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and tangibles — it is injurious. The unpleasant experience that has the nature of destroying bodily happiness, arisen through the power of cognitive appearances in the form of <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering), is called <s>duḥkha</s>.

body.text:
duḥkhaṃ manasikārāravyaṃ manasastūpaghātakam |
daurmanasyaṃ ca tajjñeyamanyopakleśahetu yat |
body.translated_text: <s>Duḥkha</s> (suffering) is to be mentally attended to; it is injurious to the mind. And that should be known as <s>daurmanasya</s> (mental displeasure) which is the cause of other afflictions.

body.text: mānasaṃ sukhaṃ duḥkhañcānusmṛtya pūrvahasana-nandana-krīḍana-vistāra-cittavikṣepādi-ayoniśomanasikārasaṃprayuktaṃ mānasaduḥkham | daurmanasyādi upa-saṃkleśajanitvād anyopakleśa hetu yat | ityuktam | yad anyadetādṛśādi upakleśaḥ, sa tu kleśo 'pyucyate, upāyāsa ityucyate | tatra eṣāṃ dvādaśabhavāṅgānām anvartha nāmāni darśayituṃ - tamo 'bhijñānāmarūpāyatasparśavittarṣataḥ | ityuktam |
