body.translated_text: Recollecting mental pleasure and suffering — the mental suffering conjoined with improper attention (<s>ayoniśomanasikāra</s>) such as former laughter, delight, play, expansiveness, mental distraction, and so forth. 'That which arises from affliction (<s>daurmanasya</s>) and secondary afflictions, which is the cause of other defilements' — so it is said. Whatever else of such nature is a secondary affliction (<s>upakleśa</s>), that is also called an affliction (<s>kleśa</s>), and is called distress (<s>upāyāsa</s>). Therein, in order to show the etymologically meaningful names of these twelve limbs of existence, it is said: 'darkness, intention, name-and-form, base, contact, feeling, craving, and so forth.'

body.text: tatra andhakārārthenāvidyā | abhīti abhisaṃskārārthena saṃskārāḥ | pravaṇatvānnāma | ropaṇārthena rūpam | āyatasparśavittarṣataḥ | iti āyadvārārthe nāyatanam | sparśanārthena sparśaḥ | anubhavanārthena vedanā | paritarṣaṇārthena tṛṣṇā |
body.translated_text: Therein, <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is so called in the sense of darkness. 'Abhi-' means in the sense of intentional formation — thus <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations). 'Name' (<s>nāma</s>) is due to its inclining nature. 'Form' (<s>rūpa</s>) is in the sense of implanting. 'Base, contact, feeling, craving, and so forth' — '<s>āyatana</s>' (sense-base) is in the sense of being a gateway. '<s>Sparśa</s>' (contact) is in the sense of touching. '<s>Vedanā</s>' (feeling) is in the sense of experiencing. '<s>Tṛṣṇā</s>' (craving) is in the sense of intense thirsting.

body.text:
tṛṣṇādānabhavotpādaḥ pākanāśa viśokataḥ |
upādānārthena upādānam | punarbhavajananārthena bhavaḥ |
body.translated_text:
From craving: grasping, becoming, birth, ripening, destruction, and sorrow —
<s>Upādāna</s> (grasping) is in the sense of appropriation. <s>Bhava</s> (becoming) is in the sense of generating renewed existence.

body.text: bhāvārthena jātiḥ, pākārthena jarā | vināśārthena maraṇam | śocanārthena śokaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Jāti</s> (birth) is in the sense of coming into being. <s>Jarā</s> (aging) is in the sense of ripening. <s>Maraṇa</s> (death) is in the sense of destruction. <s>Śoka</s> (grief) is in the sense of mourning.

body.text:
vacanādi kāyasaṃpīḍā cittadaurmānasaṃ tathā |
kleśādanvarthakaṃ nāma yathākramamudīritam |
body.translated_text:
Speech and lamentation, bodily affliction,
and mental dejection likewise —
the etymologically meaningful names [of the twelve links]
are declared in their proper order.

body.text: vacanaparidevanārthena paridevaḥ | kāyasaṃpīḍanārthena duḥkham | cittasaṃpīḍanārthena daurmanasyam | upakleśārthena upāyāsāḥ | punastattvāparijñetyādi tu parīkṣārthaṃ pradarśanārtham uktam |
body.translated_text: <s>Parideva</s> (lamentation) is in the sense of vocal weeping. <s>Duḥkha</s> (suffering) is in the sense of bodily affliction. <s>Daurmanasya</s> (mental anguish) is in the sense of mental affliction. <s>Upāyāsa</s> (distress) is in the sense of secondary defilements. Furthermore, 'due to non-comprehension of reality' and so forth is stated for the purpose of examination and demonstration.

body.text:
punastattvāparijñānāda vidyāderyathākramam |
pūrvapūrvebhya utpādo 'pyākhyātaścottarottaraḥ |
body.translated_text:
Furthermore, due to non-comprehension of reality,
from <s>avidyā</s> and the rest in their proper order,
the arising of each successive [link]
is declared from each preceding one.

body.text: tattvāparijñānaṃ tu apratipattirvipratipattiśca | ayoniśomanasikārahetutvād ajñānamaṃ avidyā | avidyāyāṃ satyāṃ vibhinnāḥ saṃskārā abhinirvartante puṇyopagāḥ, apuṇyopagāḥ, āneñjyopagāḥ| tatra puṇyopagānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ puṇyopagameva vijñānaṃ bhavati | apuṇyopagānāṃ saṃskārāṇāmapuṇyopagameva vijñānaṃ bhavati | āneñjyopagānāṃ saṃskārāṇāmāneñjyopagameva vijñānaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: Non-comprehension of reality (<s>tattvāparijñāna</s>) means non-understanding and wrong understanding. Due to being caused by improper attention (<s>ayoniśomanasikāra</s>), this unknowing is <s>avidyā</s>. When <s>avidyā</s> is present, differentiated <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) are produced: those tending toward merit (<s>puṇyopaga</s>), those tending toward demerit (<s>apuṇyopaga</s>), and those tending toward the imperturbable (<s>āneñjyopaga</s>). Therein, the consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) of meritorious formations tends toward merit. The consciousness of demeritorious formations tends toward demerit. The consciousness of imperturbable formations tends toward the imperturbable.

body.text: idamucyate vijñānapratyayaṃ nāmarūpam | nāmarūpavivṛddhayā ṣaḍbhirāyatanadvārai kṛtyakriyāḥ pravartante | tannāmarūpapratyayaṃ ṣaḍāyatanamityucyate | ṣaḍbhyaścāyatanebhyaḥ ṣaṭsparśakāyāḥ pravartante | ayaṃ ṣaḍāyatanapratyayaḥ sparśa ityucyate | yajjātīyaḥ sparśo bhavati, tajjātīyā vedanā pravartate | iyamucyate sparśapratyayā vedaneti | yastāṃ vedanāṃ viśeṣeṇāsvādayati, abhinandati, adhyavasāyaṃ tiṣṭhati sā vedanāpratyayā tṛṣṇetyucyate | āsvādanādhyavasānādhyavasāyasthānādātmapriyarūpa-sātarūpa-viyogo mābhūditi yasya bhūyaḥ praṇidhānamiyaṃ tṛṣṇā pratyayopādānetyucyate | evaṃ prārthayamānaḥ punarbhavajanakaṃ karma samutthāpayati kāyena vācā manasā ca sa upādāna-pratyayo bhava ityucyate | tatkarmanirjātānāṃ pañcaskandhānām abhinirvṛttiryā sā bhavapratyayo jātirityucyate | jātyābhinirvṛttānāṃ skandhānāmupacayana-paripākādvināśo bhavati |
body.translated_text: This is called <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) conditioned <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form). Through the growth of name-and-form, functional activities operate through the six sense-base gateways. That is called the six sense-bases (<s>ṣaḍāyatana</s>) conditioned by name-and-form. From the six sense-bases, six groups of contact (<s>sparśa</s>) operate. This is called contact conditioned by the six sense-bases. Whatever kind of contact there is, that same kind of feeling (<s>vedanā</s>) operates. This is called feeling conditioned by contact. Whoever especially savors that feeling, delights in it, and abides with resolve — that is called craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) conditioned by feeling. From the savoring, resolve, and abiding in resolve, [thinking] 'may there be no separation from what is dear and agreeable to myself' — whoever has this further aspiration, this is called grasping (<s>upādāna</s>) conditioned by craving. Thus aspiring, one generates <s>karma</s> that produces renewed existence through body, speech, and mind — that is called becoming (<s>bhava</s>) conditioned by grasping. The full manifestation of the five aggregates produced from that <s>karma</s> — that is called birth (<s>jāti</s>) conditioned by becoming. The deterioration and ripening unto destruction of the aggregates manifested through birth —

body.text: tadidaṃ jātipratyayaṃ jarāmaraṇamityucyate| pūrvapūrvāṅgānāmuttarottarāṇāṃ hetutvāt, tāni uttarodbhavāt pratyaya eva | evamayaṃ dvādaśāṅgaḥ pratītyasamutpādo-'nyonyahetukodbhūtaḥ |
body.translated_text: that is called aging and death (<s>jarāmaraṇa</s>) conditioned by birth. Since the earlier limbs are causes of the later ones, and the later ones arise from them, they are indeed conditions. Thus this twelve-limbed <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) has arisen through mutual causation.

body.text:
dvādaśāṅgastripravṛttirnityocchedo hyanādijaḥ|
pravṛtterjaladhārāvad vartate 'nādikālikaḥ |
body.translated_text:
The twelve-limbed [dependent origination], with its three modes of activity, neither eternal nor annihilated, beginninglessly arisen,
flows like a stream of water, operating from beginningless time.

body.text: nānityaḥ sa tu satataṃ sthitatvāt | na saṃskṛta iti tu saṃskāraviyuktatvāt | sa na cetanaḥ cittaviyuktatvāt | na pratyayasambhava iti pratyayaviyuktatvāt | na kṣayadharmastūpacayaviyuktatvāt | na nirodhadharmaḥ utpāda-sthiti-vināśa-viyuktatvāt |
body.translated_text: It is not permanent, yet it abides constantly. It is not conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>), since it is devoid of [deliberate] formations. It is not sentient, since it is devoid of mind. It does not arise from conditions, since it is devoid of [independent] conditions. It is not subject to decay, since it is devoid of accumulation. It is not subject to cessation, since it is devoid of arising, persistence, and destruction.

body.text: anādikālapravṛttastu sandhikāla-pariccheda-viyuktatvāt | nadīstrotavat strotodbhūta anucchinnapravāhaḥ |
body.translated_text: Having operated from beginningless time, it is devoid of the demarcation of juncture-moments. Like the current of a river, it flows as an unbroken stream.

body.text: atha āryaśālistambasūtra-ṭīkāyāṃ caturtho 'ntimaḥ paṭalaḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus concludes the fourth and final chapter of the commentary on the noble <s>Śālistambasūtra</s>.

body.text: pratītyasamutpādo 'yaṃ nadīstrotavat avicchinno 'nupravartate | atha cemānyasya catvāryaṅgāni hetuḥ saṃghātakārakāṇi ca, dvādaśāṅgasya pratītyasamutpādasya catvāryaṅgāni saṃghātakriyāyai hetutvena pravartante | tasmāt katamāni catvāri? ityuktam|
body.translated_text: This <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> continues uninterruptedly, like the current of a river. Now, four limbs of this [process] are causes and factors of assemblage. Four limbs of the twelve-limbed dependent origination operate as causes for the activity of assemblage. Therefore, which are these four? It is said:

body.text: avidyā ca tṛṣā karma vijñānaṃ kramaśo matāḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), <s>karma</s> (action), and <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) are held [to be the four], in that order.

body.text: avidyā, tṛṣṇā, karma, vijñānañceti yathākramam | heturvijñānabījaṃ hi | vijñānaṃ bīja-svabhāvatvena hetuḥ | karma kṣetramudīritam | karma kṣetra-svabhāvatvena heturityuktam | avidyā tṛṣṇā ca kleśasvabhāvatvena hetuḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Avidyā</s>, <s>tṛṣṇā</s>, <s>karma</s>, and <s>vijñāna</s>, in their proper order. 'The cause is the seed of consciousness' — <s>vijñāna</s>, being of the nature of a seed, is the cause. 'Karma is declared to be the field' — <s>karma</s>, being of the nature of a field, is said to be the cause. <s>Avidyā</s> and <s>tṛṣṇā</s>, being of the nature of afflictions, are causes.

body.text: karmakleśā vijñānabījatvena vyavasthitāḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) are established as the seed of consciousness.

body.text: karmakleśā vijñānabījaṃ janayanti | tatra
body.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> generate the seed of consciousness. Therein —

body.text:
karma vijñānabījasya kṣetrakāryaṃ karoti ca |
vijñānanāmakaṃ bījaṃ tṛṣṇayā snihyate param |
vijñānabījaṃ cāvidyā kirati snehanena vai |
karma tṛṣṇā tathāvidyā kṣetraṃ sneho 'vakīrṇanam |
vijñāne na karomīdaṃ na vijñānamito matam |
body.translated_text:
<s>Karma</s> performs the function of a field for the seed of consciousness;
the seed called consciousness is supremely moistened by <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving);
<s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) scatters the consciousness-seed with moisture indeed;
<s>karma</s>, <s>tṛṣṇā</s>, and <s>avidyā</s> are the field, the moisture, and the scattering;
consciousness does not think 'I do this,' nor is consciousness conceived as [arising] from this.

body.text: tatra karmaṇo 'pi naivaṃ bhavati ityādi tu karmaṇo 'pi naivaṃ bhavati ahaṃ vijñāna-bījasya kṣetrakāryaṃ karomi| tṛṣṇāyā api ityādi tu evaṃ tṛṣṇāyā api naivaṃ bhavati ahaṃ vijñānabījaṃ snehayāmīti | avidyāyā api ityādi tu avidyāyā api naivaṃ bhavati ahaṃ vijñānabījamavakiromīti | vijñānasyāpi ityādi tu naivaṃ bhavati ahamebhiḥ pratyayairjanitamiti |
body.translated_text: Therein, '<s>karma</s> also does not think thus' and so forth means: <s>karma</s> also does not think 'I perform the function of a field for the seed of consciousness.' '<s>Tṛṣṇā</s> also' and so forth means: likewise, <s>tṛṣṇā</s> also does not think 'I moisten the seed of consciousness.' '<s>Avidyā</s> also' and so forth means: <s>avidyā</s> also does not think 'I scatter the seed of consciousness.' 'Consciousness also' and so forth means: [consciousness] does not think 'I have been produced by these conditions.'

body.text:
tathāpi bījavijñāne karmakleśapratiṣṭhite |
vijñānabījamityuktaṃ kīrṇe 'vidyāsvavaskare |
body.translated_text:
Nevertheless, when the seed-consciousness is established in <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s>,
it is called the consciousness-seed, scattered in the compost of <s>avidyā</s>,

body.text: tṛṣṇājalena saṃsikte
body.translated_text: moistened by the water of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) —

body.text: avidyā-svavaskara iti svavaskareṇa ca sadṛśena svavaskaraṃ sarveṣvanugata-tvāt | kīrṇe svavaskare iti svavaskareṇa pracchādanam | tṛṣṇājalena saṃsikte tṛṣṇaiva jalam | saṃsikte iti tu snehane |
body.translated_text: 'The compost of <s>avidyā</s>' — because compost, being similar [to avidyā], pervades everything through its own compost-nature. 'Scattered in one's own compost' means covered by one's own compost. 'Moistened by the water of <s>tṛṣṇā</s>' — <s>tṛṣṇā</s> itself is the water. 'Moistened' means saturated.

body.text: hetuto nāmarūpayoḥ | aṅkurotpādabhāso hi |
body.translated_text:
From causes, the sprout of name-and-form —
for the appearance of the arising of a sprout [occurs] —

body.text: iti tu hetu pratyayasāmagyā utpādastu nāmarūpāṅkuramabhinirvartayati | nāmarūpāṅkuram ityādestu |
body.translated_text: that is, through the assemblage of causes and conditions, the arising produces the sprout of <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form). As for 'the sprout of name-and-form' and so forth —

body.text: na svaparobhayāditāḥ | nāmarūpamidaṃ jātaṃ |
body.translated_text:
Not from self, other, both, or the like —
this name-and-form has arisen.

body.text: nāmarūpāṅkuramidaṃ tu svayaṃ parata ubhayādito notpannam | atha kīdṛśam iti cet |
body.translated_text: This sprout of name-and-form has not arisen from itself, from another, or from both. If one asks, then what is it like?

body.text: piturmātuḥ samāgamāt | avirodhādṛtoścāpi |
body.translated_text:
From the union of father and mother,
and from the non-obstruction of the season as well —

body.text: piturmātuḥ samāgamād ityādi tu pitṛmātṛsaṃyogo vā saktiḥ, samāgamaḥ, yuktatvam, putraprasūtisāmarthyam, ṛtumatvañca | 'tridivasātyaye rajonivṛttistu' sa hi strīṇām ṛturucyate | tadā puruṣasamāgame śukraśoṇitasaṃyoge, svayaṃ gandharvasyāpi citta-viparyaye 'pi mātāpitṛkriyādhimuktau garbhotpādakrameṇa kalala-arbuda-peśī-ghana-praśākhāvasthāmatikramya prasūtasya, śaiśava-kaumārya-madhyatā-yauvana-vṛddhattvādi-daśāvasthā bhavanti | tasmādapyuktam-
body.translated_text: 'From the union of father and mother' and so forth means: the conjunction of father and mother, or attachment, union, compatibility, the capacity for producing offspring, and the fertility of the season. 'The cessation of menstruation after three days' — that is called the season (<s>ṛtu</s>) of women. Then, upon the union with a man, at the conjunction of semen and blood, when the <s>gandharva</s> (intermediate being) also undergoes a reversal of mind and has inclination toward the activities of the parents, through the sequence of conception in the womb — passing through the stages of <s>kalala</s> (embryonic mass), <s>arbuda</s> (blister), <s>peśī</s> (flesh-lump), <s>ghana</s> (solid mass), and <s>praśākhā</s> (limb-formation) — for the one born, there are the ten stages such as infancy, childhood, middle age, youth, old age, and so forth. Therefore it is also said —

body.text:
kiñcidāsvādave dhitam |
bījavijñānamityuktaṃ mātṛgarbhe kramāccayaḥ |
nāmarūpāṅkurotpādaḥ |
body.translated_text:
Somewhat pierced by relishing,
it is called the seed-consciousness;
in the mother's womb, gradually,
the arising of the sprout of name-and-form [occurs].

body.text: atha ca mātāpitṛsaṃyogād-ṛtusamavāyād anyeṣāṃ ca pratyayānāṃ samavāyāttatrāsvādaviddhaṃ vijñānabījaṃ mātuḥ kukṣau nāmarūpāṅkuramabhinirvartayati |
body.translated_text: Furthermore, from the union of mother and father, from the conjunction of the season, and from the conjunction of other conditions, the consciousness-seed, pierced by relishing, produces the sprout of <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form) in the mother's womb.

body.text:
na vaikalyācca pratyayaiḥ |
virodhatvācca hetūnāṃ māyānairātmyanigrahe |
utpādo 'pi na saṃbhavaḥ |
body.translated_text:
And due to deficiency of conditions,
and due to the contradiction of causes,
in the restraint of the illusory and selfless [nature],
arising also does not occur.

body.text: tasmād asvāmikeṣu dharmeṣu amameṣu aparigraheṣu māyālakṣaṇasvabhāveṣu hetupratyayānāmavaikalyādityuktam |
body.translated_text: Therefore, in <s>dharmas</s> that are ownerless, not 'mine,' unappropriated, and of the nature of illusion — due to the non-deficiency of causes and conditions, so it is said.

body.text: asvāmikeṣu iti tu antaḥ karaṇaṃ puruṣādi anupalambhanasvabhāvamasti | tatrābhiniveśenotpanno ya āgrahaḥ | dharmastu skandhadhātu-āyatana-svabhāvaḥ | amama iti ātmātmīyarahitaḥ | aparigraha iti tu īśvarādi-parigrahānupalambhāt | māyālakṣaṇa-svabhāva iti yathā māyā tu abhūtāpi vividhavyavahāraṃ pratipādayati, tadvat māyāsvabhāvasya sarvadharmeṣu kriyādirvividhopalabhyate | hetupratyaya-saṃnipāta-vyatiriktaṃ hetupratyayādidharmaḥ kiñcidapi na utpadyate, vinaśyati vā | yathāpi hetupratyayavaikalyatvād bhāvānām anutpādastadavabodhayituam upamā |
body.translated_text: 'In ownerless [dharmas]' — the inner person (<s>antaḥkaraṇapuruṣa</s>) and so forth are of a nature that is unapprehended. The grasping that arises therein through attachment [is unfounded]. <s>Dharmas</s> are of the nature of <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases). 'Without mine' means devoid of self and what belongs to self. 'Without possession' — because the possession of <s>Īśvara</s> (God) and so forth is unapprehended. 'Of the nature of the characteristic of illusion' — just as <s>māyā</s> (illusion), though unreal, produces various worldly transactions, so too in all <s>dharmas</s> of the nature of illusion, various activities and so forth are apprehended. Apart from the conjunction of causes and conditions, no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever of cause and condition arises or perishes. Just as, due to the deficiency of causes and conditions, entities do not arise — this analogy makes that understood.

body.text: cakṣurvijñānamapyataḥ | pañcabhirhetubhirjātam | ityuktam |
body.translated_text: Visual consciousness also therefore; arisen from five causes. Thus it was said.

body.text:
tadyathā pañcabhiḥ kāraṇaiścakṣurvijñānamutpadyate | katamaiḥ pañcabhirityādistu -
cakṣūrūpāvabhāsanaiḥ | nabhastajja manaskāraiḥ | iti |
body.translated_text: For example, visual consciousness (<s>cakṣurvijñāna</s>) arises from five causes. Which five? — the eye, form, illumination, space, and the appropriate mental attention born from that.

body.text: tasmāt cakṣuḥ pratītya rūpañcālokañcākāśañca tajjamanasikārañca ityādi uktam | tatra cakṣuriti rūpaṃ draṣṭuṃ cakṣurindriyaṃ vikalaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: Therefore it is said: 'Depending on the eye and form and light and space and the appropriate mental attention born from that' and so forth. Therein, 'the eye' — the eye faculty (<s>cakṣurindriya</s>) for seeing form may be deficient.

body.text: tasmādeva cakṣurvijñānasyāśrayakṛtyaṃ karoti ityuktam | āloka iti candra-nakṣatrāgni-auṣadhi-maṇi-prabhānām abhivyaktyai āloko 'pi upasthitaḥ | ākāśo 'pi nānāvṛtti-vikalo bhavati | tajjamanasikāro 'pi samanvāhāra-kārye 'vikalo bhavati |
body.translated_text: Therefore it is said that [the eye] performs the function of being the support (<s>āśraya</s>) for visual consciousness. 'Light' — the illumination of the moon, stars, fire, medicinal herbs, and gems is also present for manifestation. Space also performs the function of non-obstruction. The appropriate mental attention born from that also performs the function of directing attention without deficiency.

body.text: pañcāvaikalyatastathā | cakṣurvijñānamudbhūtam |
body.translated_text: From the non-deficiency of the five, visual consciousness arises thus.

body.text: cakṣurvijñānasya pratyayeṣu kasyacidapyabhāve na cakṣurvijñānasyotpādaḥ, sati cotpādo bhavati |
body.translated_text: When any one of the conditions for visual consciousness is absent, visual consciousness does not arise; when [all are] present, arising occurs.

body.text: mayā te janitā iti | vikalpo na yathodeti
body.translated_text: 'I have produced you' — such conceptualization does not arise in them.

body.text: iti tatra cakṣuṣo naivaṃ bhavati 'ahaṃ cakṣurvijñānasyāśraya-kṛtyaṃ karomīti | rūpasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati, ahaṃ cakṣurvijñānasyālambanakṛtyaṃ karomīti | ālokasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati ahaṃ cakṣurvijñānasyāvabhāsakṛtyaṃ karomīti | ākāśasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati ahaṃ cakṣurvijñānasyāvaraṇakṛtyaṃ karomīti | tajjamanasikārasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati ahaṃ cakṣurvijñānasya samanvāhāra-kṛtyaṃ karomīti | cakṣurvijñānasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati ahamebhiḥ pratyayairjanitamiti |
body.translated_text: Therein, the eye does not think: 'I perform the function of support for visual consciousness.' Nor does form think: 'I perform the function of being the object (<s>ālambana</s>) for visual consciousness.' Nor does light think: 'I perform the function of illumination for visual consciousness.' Nor does space think: 'I perform the function of non-obstruction for visual consciousness.' Nor does the appropriate mental attention born from that think: 'I perform the function of directing attention for visual consciousness.' Nor does visual consciousness think: 'I have been produced by these conditions.'

body.text: atha ca punaḥ satsveṣu pratyayeṣu cakṣurvijñānasyotpattirbhavati | asatsveṣu na bhavati | evaṃ
body.translated_text: But rather, when those conditions are present, the arising of visual consciousness occurs; when they are absent, it does not. Thus—

body.text: śrotrajñānādikā khilam | utpādasya kramaścaivaṃ
body.translated_text: Auditory consciousness and so forth, all of them; the order of arising is thus—

body.text: tadvat śrotrendriyādīnāṃ pañcabhirhetubhirutpādakramo 'vagantavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Likewise, the order of arising of the ear faculty and so forth through five causes should be understood.

body.text:
hetupratyayasaṅgrahāt |
kartrādīnāṃ ca vaikalyād ahaṃkāraviyogataḥ |
utpādo 'pi yathāpūrvaṃ tathā cāpi pratītyajam |
hetumatsaṃvijānīyāt
body.translated_text: From the gathering of causes and conditions, from the deficiency of agent and the like, from the separation of ego-sense, arising also as before — thus what is dependently arisen should be understood as having causes.

body.text: tathā cāpi hetupratyayakramo 'nantarokta-kramaḥ | evaṃ sarvadharmāṇām utpāda-sthiti-vināśā avagantavyāḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus also the order of causes and conditions is as stated above. Thus should the arising, persistence, and destruction of all <s>dharmas</s> be understood.

body.text: asmāllokāt paraṃnahi |
body.translated_text: From this world to the other, not indeed—

body.text:
kaściddharmo kvacid gantā hetupratyayatastathā |
karmaṇaḥphalamabhyeti
body.translated_text: No <s>dharma</s> whatsoever goes anywhere; yet from causes and conditions, the fruit of <s>karma</s> (action) is obtained.

body.text: tatra dharmastu cakṣuḥ-śrotra-ghrāṇa-jihvā-kāya-mana-ādayo dharmāḥ | rūpa-śabda-gandha-rasa-sparśādayo dharmāḥ, skandha-dhātvāyatana-pratītyasamutpādādayo dharmāḥ | asmāditi tu asmāllokāt paraṃ lokam athavā paralokād amuṃ lokaṃ kaściddharmo na saṃkrāmati | yadyevaṃ nityavādo vā ahetu-pratikūla-hetuvādo vā bhaviṣyatīti cet | ucyate | hetupratyayavaikalyābhāvāt karmaṇaḥ phalamabhyeti iti |
body.translated_text: Therein, '<s>dharmas</s>' refers to the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, mind, and so forth; form, sound, smell, taste, touch, and so forth; <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases), <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), and so forth. 'From this' means from this world to the other world, or from the other world to this world — no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever transmigrates. If so, would this not be eternalism, or the position of no cause or contrary cause? It is said: because there is no deficiency of causes and conditions, the fruit of <s>karma</s> is obtained.

body.text: tatra saṅkrāntyabhāve 'pi karmaphalāvināśitvaṃ pratyakṣānumāna-viśvastāgama-prakhyātena anenodāharaṇena jñātavyam |
body.translated_text: Therein, even in the absence of transference, the indestructibility of <s>karma</s> (action) and its fruit should be known through this illustration, which is well-established through direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), inference (<s>anumāna</s>), and trustworthy scripture (<s>āgama</s>).

body.text:
yathādarśe viśodhite |
dṛśyante mukhabimbāni darpaṇe 'pi ca bimbakam |
saṃkrāmitaṃ bhavennaiva
body.translated_text: Just as in a polished mirror, reflections of the face are seen; yet the image in the mirror has not been transferred at all.

body.text: tasmād uktam | tadyathā- supariśuddha ādarśamaṇḍale mukha-pratibimbakaṃ dṛśyate | na ca tatrādarśamaṇḍale mukhaṃ saṃkrāmati | asti ca mukha prativijñapti rhetupratyayānāmavaikalyāt | evamasmāllokānna kaściccyavate nāpyanyatrotpadyate | asti ca karmaphalavijñaptirhetupratyayānāmavaikalyāt |
body.translated_text: Therefore it is said: for example, in a well-polished mirror surface, a reflection of the face is seen. Yet the face does not transmigrate into that mirror surface. But there is the cognition of the face-reflection due to the non-deficiency of causes and conditions. Likewise, from this world no one departs, nor is anyone born elsewhere. Yet there is the cognition of the fruit of <s>karma</s> due to the non-deficiency of causes and conditions.

body.text:
tadanyonyāvikalpanam |
kartṛkriyāvihīnaṃ tat tathotpādāvabhāsanam |
pūrvavṛddhikramācca syāt
body.translated_text: Their mutual non-conceptualization; that is devoid of agent and action; yet the appearance of arising occurs thus, from the sequence of prior growth.

body.text: taditi tu mukham ādarśaśca | anyonyam iti parasparam anyonyam | avikalpanamiti vikalpanābhāvaḥ | kartṛkriyāvihīnaṃ tad iti tatra kartā kriyā ca na staḥ | kiṃ tannocchidyata iti cet- tathotpādāvabhāsanam ityuktam | kathaṃ kartṛvihīnaṃ kriyā karma ca bhaviṣyatīti ucyate- pūrvavṛddhikramācca syāt |
body.translated_text: 'That' refers to the face and the mirror. 'Mutually' means reciprocally, one to another. 'Non-conceptualization' means the absence of conceptualization. 'That is devoid of agent and action' — therein there is neither agent nor action. If asked 'is it then annihilated?' — it is said: 'yet the appearance of arising occurs thus.' How can there be action and <s>karma</s> without an agent? It is said: 'from the sequence of prior growth.'

body.text:
dūrasthaścandramā yathā |
parītto dakapātrānte dṛśyate na ca krāmati |
asti kriyā ca karmāpi |
body.translated_text: Just as the moon, though distant, appears in a small water vessel, yet does not transmigrate [into it]; and yet there is action and <s>karma</s>.

body.text: tadyathā - candramaṇḍalaṃ [dvi] catvāriṃśadyojana-śatamūrdhvaṃ sthitam | atha ca punaḥ parītte 'bhyudakabhājane candrasya pratibimbaṃ dṛśyate | na ca candramaṇḍalaṃ tasmātsthānāc cyutam | atha ca punaḥ parītte 'bhyudakasthabhājane dṛśyate | asti ca candramaṇḍalaprativijñaptiḥ, hetupratyayānāmavaikalyāt | evamasmāllokānna kaścid cyavate nāpyutpadyate | asti ca karmaphala-prativijñaptiḥ hetupratyayānāmavaikalyāt |
body.translated_text: For example, the disk of the moon stands forty-two hundred <s>yojanas</s> above. Yet in a small vessel filled with water, a reflection of the moon is seen. The disk of the moon has not moved from that place. Yet in the small vessel filled with water, it is seen. And there is the cognition of the moon-disk reflection due to the non-deficiency of causes and conditions. Likewise, from this world no one departs, nor is anyone born [elsewhere]. Yet there is the cognition of the fruit of <s>karma</s> due to the non-deficiency of causes and conditions.

body.text: api ca, tadyathāgnirupādāne pratyaye sati jvalati upādāna-vaikalyānna jvalati | evameva karmakleśajanitaṃ vijñānabījaṃ tatra tatropapattyāyatana-pratisandhau mātuḥkukṣau nāmarūpāṅkuramabhinirvartayati | asvāmikeṣu dharmeṣu aparigraheṣu paraspara-pratyayamanmāyālakṣaṇasvabhāveṣu hetupratyayānāmavaikalyāt |
body.translated_text: Moreover, just as fire burns when fuel — the condition — is present, and does not burn due to the deficiency of fuel, so too the consciousness-seed (<s>vijñānabīja</s>) generated by <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) produces the sprout of <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form) in the mother's womb at the juncture of rebirth in the respective place of birth — in <s>dharmas</s> that are ownerless, without possession, mutually conditioned, of the nature of the characteristic of illusion, due to the non-deficiency of causes and conditions.

body.text: santi te kalpanātmakāḥ | bāhyakarmakriyā hetuḥ
body.translated_text: They are of the nature of conceptualization. External action and activity are the cause—

body.text: tatra bāhyapratītyasamutpādasya kriyākarma-vyavasthā tu kalpanātmikā jñeyā |
body.translated_text: Therein, the establishment of action and activity in external <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) should be known as being of a conceptual nature (<s>kalpanātmikā</s>).

body.text: adhyātmaparatantrataḥ | pañcavijñānasaṃbhūtaḥ
body.translated_text: From internal dependence; arisen from the five consciousnesses—

body.text: tatra paratantra-pratītyasamutpādasya lakṣaṇamadhyātma-pañcendriya-viṣaya-vijñaptyavabhāsākāratvena veditavyam |
body.translated_text: Therein, the characteristic of the dependent (<s>paratantra</s>) nature of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> should be understood as having the form of the appearance of the cognition of the five internal sense faculties and their objects.

body.text: paramārtho 'vicāryataḥ | pariniṣpanna ākhyātaḥ
body.translated_text: The ultimate (<s>paramārtha</s>), without investigation; it is called the perfected (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>)—

body.text: yo vikalpa-paratantrātmākāro vijñaptyavabhāsākārarahito nirvikalpaḥ supariśuddhaśca, abdhātu-suvarṇa-ākāśavat pariśuddhaḥ | kleśa-jñeyāvaraṇa-svarūpa-pariśuddhaḥ candrodayavad, acintyaguṇaḥ, aprameya-prabhāva-bhāsātmakaḥ, asaṃkrāntaḥ sarvasattvārtham anābhogāvicchedakaḥ, ādimadhyāntarahitaḥ, tridhātu-samatīto nirmalo-'malo malaprahāṇa-svarūpaḥ | pratisvasaṃvid-gocarātmaka-kāya-vāk-cittakarma-samatītaḥ, svasaṃvedanaḥ, aparādhīno viśvarūpamaṇiratnarāja iva anuttaro dharmakāya ityucyate |
body.translated_text: That which is devoid of the appearance-form of conceptualization and dependent nature, free from conceptualization and thoroughly pure — pure like the water element, gold, and space; purified in its own nature from the obscurations of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and <s>jñeya</s> (knowables), like the rising of the moon; of inconceivable qualities; of the nature of immeasurable radiance and splendor; without transference; uninterruptedly accomplishing the welfare of all sentient beings without effort; devoid of beginning, middle, and end; transcending the three realms; stainless and without defilement, of the nature of the abandonment of defilements; transcending the activities of body, speech, and mind, being the domain of individual self-realization (<s>pratisvasaṃvedana</s>); self-cognizing; independent; like a wish-fulfilling jewel-king of universal form — it is called the unsurpassed <s>Dharmakāya</s> (truth body).

body.text:
sahetupratyayodbhavaḥ |
sarvadā dvividho jñeyaḥ kartrādirahitastathā |
tucchaśūnyādiniḥ sāraḥ
body.translated_text: Arising from causes and conditions, always to be known as twofold, devoid of agent and the like, empty, void, and without essence—

body.text: tasmāt tatrādhyātmikaḥ pratītyasamutpādaḥ pañcabhirākārairdraṣṭavyaḥ | ityuktam | katamaiḥ pañcabhiḥ? uktam | na śāśvatato | yasmādanye maraṇāntikāḥ skandhā anya aupapattyaṃśikāḥ skandhāḥ | na tu ya eva maraṇāntikāḥ skandhāsta evaupapattyaṃśikāḥ | ya evopapatti-hetavasta eva vināśakāḥ | ya eva vināśa-hetussa evāpi aupapattiko bhaviṣyati | ato maraṇāntikāḥ skandhā nirudhyante aupapattyaṃśikā skandhāḥ prādurbhavanti | ato na śāśvatataḥ | na ca pūrvaniruddheṣu maraṇāntikeṣu skandheṣu iti niruddhaya na ciraṃ gatatvād aupapattyaṃśikā iti aupapattyaṃśe niśritatvād aupapattyaṃśikāḥ skandhāḥ prādurbhavanti | maraṇāntikā aniruddhā eva | aupapattyaṃśikaḥ skandhaḥ prādurbhavet, tada-yuktatvāduktam- api tu maraṇāntikāḥ skandhā nirudhyante, tasminneva ca samaye aupapattyaṃśikā skandhā prārdubhavanti, tulādaṇḍonnāmāvanāmavat | ato nocchedataḥ, visadṛśāḥ sattvanikāyāḥ sabhāgāyāṃ jātyāṃ jātimabhinirvartayanti | ato na saṃkrāntitaḥ parīttakarma kriyate, vipulaḥ phalavipāko 'nubhūyate |
body.translated_text: Therefore, it is said that the internal <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) should be viewed in five aspects. Which five? It is said: not from eternality — because the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) at the time of death are different from the <s>skandhas</s> at the moment of rebirth. It is not the case that the very <s>skandhas</s> at death are the same as the <s>skandhas</s> at rebirth. The very causes of rebirth are the very causes of destruction; the very cause of destruction will itself become the cause of rebirth. Therefore, the <s>skandhas</s> at death cease and the <s>skandhas</s> of rebirth manifest — thus, not from eternality. And it is not the case that when the <s>skandhas</s> at death have previously ceased — called 'ceased' because they have not long departed, and called 'of the rebirth portion' because they depend on the rebirth portion — the <s>skandhas</s> of rebirth manifest while the death-moment <s>skandhas</s> have not yet ceased and a rebirth-portion <s>skandha</s> would manifest; since that would be illogical, it is said: rather, the <s>skandhas</s> at death cease, and at that very moment the <s>skandhas</s> of rebirth manifest, like the rising and falling of a balance beam. Thus, not from annihilation. Dissimilar classes of beings bring about birth within a similar class of birth — thus, not from transference. A limited <s>karma</s> (action) is performed, yet an abundant fruition of results is experienced.

body.text: ataḥ parītta-hetuto vipulaphalamabhinirvartitam | yathāvedanīyaṃ karma kriyate tadāvedanīyo vipāko 'nubhūyate | atastatsadṛśānuprabandhataśca | yaḥ kaścid imaṃ pratītyasamutpādaṃ samyakpraṇītamevaṃ yathābhūtaṃ samyakprajñayā satatasamitamajīvaṃ yathāvadaviparītamajātamabhūtamakṛtamasaṃskṛtamapratighamanālambaṃ śivamabhayamavyupaśamasvabhāvaṃ paśyati | asataḥ tucchataḥ, riktataḥ, asārataḥ rogataḥ, gaṇḍataḥ, aghataḥ, anityataḥ, duḥkhataḥ, śūnyataḥ, anātmataḥ | iti |
body.translated_text: Thus, from a limited cause an abundant fruit is produced. Whatever <s>karma</s> is performed as that which is to be experienced, the corresponding fruition is experienced — thus, also from the continuity of what is similar to that. Whoever sees this <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), well-expounded, as it truly is, correctly with <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), continuously, as lifeless, as it really is, without error, as unborn, as non-existent, as uncreated, as <s>asaṃskṛta</s> (unconditioned), as unobstructed, as without support, as peaceful, as fearless, as having the nature of non-cessation — seeing it as non-existent, as hollow, as empty, as essenceless, as disease, as a boil, as misfortune, as impermanent, as <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering), as <s>śūnya</s> (empty), as <s>anātman</s> (non-self).

body.text: ya imaṃ pratītyasamutpādamiti ādhyātmikapratītyasamutpādam | yadimaṃ samyag iti aviparītam | prajñayā iti lokottaraprajñayā | yathābhūtamiti tu tathatāyathāvat | satatasamitamiti sarvakālamavicchinnam | ajīvam iti prāṇa-kartrādi-viyukta-tvādajīvam | ajātamiti jātirahitatvāt | abhūtamiti sthiti-rahitatvāt | akṛtamiti karturabhāvāt | asaṃskṛtamiti saṃskṛta-lakṣaṇa-rahitatvāt | apratighamiti āvaraṇa-rahitatvāt | anālambanamiti ālambyālambaka-rahitatvāt | śivamiti śāntatvāt | abhayamiti tu utpādādi-bhayarahitatvāt | anāhāryamiti kleśa-pāratantrya-rahitatvāt | avyayamiti satataṃ vyavasthitatvāt | avyupaśamamiti ekāntaśamagatirahitatvāt | 'asataḥ' skandhāt pṛthaganyābhāvāt | tucchata iti muktātmano hrasvalohavad ekāntasya abhāvāt | riktata iti antasthita-svarūpātmadravyābhāvāt | asārata iti spharaṇātmakatābhāvāt | rogata iti rogātmaka-skandhāt pṛthaktvābhāvat | gaṇḍata iti skandhānatiriktabādhakāntarā-bhāvāt | apratighata iti karmakleśātirikta-bādhakasvarūpāntarābhāvāt | anityata iti sahopapādavināśaḥ skandhāt pṛthaganyana svabhāvāt | duḥkhata iti saṃskāravipariṇāmaduḥkhābhyāṃ pārthakyābhāvāt | śūnyata iti kalpanā svabhāvatayā abhūta-parikalpanāyāḥ pṛthakatvābhāvāt | anātmata iti skandhānatiriktamātmadravyābhāvāt |
body.translated_text: "Whoever sees this <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>" means the internal <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>. "Correctly" means without error. "With <s>prajñā</s>" means with supramundane wisdom. "As it truly is" means in accordance with <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), as it really is. "Continuously" means at all times, uninterrupted. "Lifeless" means lifeless because it is devoid of <s>prāṇa</s> (life-breath), agent, and so forth. "Unborn" means because it is devoid of birth. "Non-existent" means because it is devoid of abiding. "Uncreated" means because there is no agent. "<s>Asaṃskṛta</s> (unconditioned)" means because it is devoid of the characteristics of the conditioned. "Unobstructed" means because it is devoid of obstruction. "Without support" means because it is devoid of both the supported and the supporter. "Peaceful" means because of being tranquil. "Fearless" means because it is devoid of the fear of arising and so forth. "Not to be taken away" means because it is devoid of subjugation by <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). "Imperishable" means because it is constantly established. "Without final cessation" means because it is devoid of the path of one-sided quiescence. "Non-existent" — because there is no separate existence apart from the <s>skandhas</s>. "Hollow" — because there is no absolute [self] like a small piece of base metal separated from gold. "Empty" — because there is no substance of an inner abiding essential self. "Essenceless" — because there is no nature of pervasive selfhood. "As disease" — because there is no separateness from the <s>skandhas</s> whose nature is disease. "As a boil" — because there is no afflicting entity apart from the <s>skandhas</s>. "Unobstructed" — because there is no afflicting essential nature apart from <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s>. "Impermanent" — because arising and ceasing simultaneously, there is no separate essential nature from the <s>skandhas</s>. "As <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering)" — because there is no separateness from the suffering of <s>saṃskāra</s> (formations) and transformation. "As <s>śūnya</s> (empty)" — because there is no separateness of false conceptualization from the nature of conceptual construction. "As <s>anātman</s> (non-self)" — because there is no substance of a self apart from the <s>skandhas</s>.

body.text:
kartrādirahitastathā |
tucchaśūnyādiniḥsāraḥ prajñayaivaṃ ya īkṣitaḥ |
kiṃ kathaṃ vā kutaḥ kena kalpavādādi hānitaḥ|
anantācintya guṇyakam | śāntaṃ dharmātmakaṃ kāyam |
body.translated_text:
Devoid of agent and so forth,
hollow, empty, and essenceless — whoever sees thus with <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom),
what, how, from where, by whom are speculative doctrines abandoned?
Of infinite and inconceivable qualities — the peaceful body whose nature is <s>dharma</s>.

body.text: tathatārthaṃ sa eva pūrvāntaṃ na pratisarati ityuktam | kiṃ nvahamabhūvamatīta iti nāyaṃ mohotpādaḥ | asaṃmohe jñānotpādatvād ahamatīta etannara-sadṛśo 'bhūvamityādi ca | ahaṃ devo vā gandharvo vā kiṃ sukhavihāro duḥkhavihāro 'bhūvamityayaṃ moho'bhāva eva | ahaṃ sugatau durgatau vā, ciram, aciram vā kathamabhūvamiti moho 'pyabhāva eva | anāgatānte na pratisarati | kiṃ nvahaṃ bhaviṣyāmyanāgate 'dhvani iti ca āhosvinna bhaviṣyāmi iti moho 'pyatra nāstyeva | kiṃ nvahaṃ bhaviṣyāmyanāgate 'dhvani iti anāgate 'dhvani devo vā piśāco vā naro vā kiṃ vā bhaviṣyāmīti atra mohasyāpyanudbhava eva | sukhī vā duḥkhī vā surūpo vā kurūpo vā kathaṃ bhaviṣyāmi iti moho 'pyatra nāsti | antarapi na pratisarati iti antarna muhyati | kiṃ nvidamiti ātmā nirātmā vā iti | kathaṃ nvidamiti kiṃ sarūpo 'thavā virūpo veti moho 'tra nodbhavati | ke santa iti sukṛta-karmakāriṇaḥ duṣkṛta-karmakāriṇo veti na mohotpādaḥ | ayaṃ sattvo devagaternaragatervā kuta āgata itaścyuto deveṣu manuṣyeṣu narake prete tiryañci vā kutra gamiṣyatīti moho 'tra na sambhavati | śramaṇa-brāhmaṇānāṃ pṛthagloke dṛṣṭigatāni bhaviṣyanti ityādi | dṛṣṭigatāni iti dṛṣṭisthāni | pṛthagiti bhinnameva | tadyatheti tu nidarśanārtham | ātmavāda-pratisaṃyuktānīti skandha-vyatirikta-ātmabhāvaḥ | avicārata ātmātmīyeti svabhāvātmagraha-saṃyuktatvād ātmavādaprati-saṃyuktānītyuktam | viparītadhāraṇā-samutthānārthaṃ pudgalavāda-pratisaṃyuktānītyādi tu punargamanatvāt pudgala iti skandha-vyatiriktaḥ | yasyāmuṃ lokaṃ tyaktvā paraloka-gamanasya paralokaṃ vihāya amuṃ etallokagamanasya cābhāvāt grahaṇa-durviparītagrahaṇamityuktam | kautuka-maṅgalavāda-pratisaṃyuktānīti | kautukastu lokaśilpasthānaṃ, yacca vividhavidyāsthāne utsava-āvāha-vivāha-kalaha-yuddhaiḥ, udyāna-nadī-sāgara-parvata-vaneṣu tattad-bhinneṣu ca āryasya gamana-darśana-saṃkramaṇa-pravṛtti-āvāsānuramaṇakrīḍā-sukhā-svāda-nṛtya-gīta-padālāpa-dhāvana-laṃghanaiḥ, adbhuta-puruṣa-strī-dāraka-dārikā-vigrahakathā-vāda-prahelikoktibhiḥ, gajāśvādi-yodhanaiḥ, dūrvā-dadhi-gorocanā-kṣetrahala-mudgara-puṣpa-phala-kalaśa-śaṅkha-matsyā-dibhiḥ, brāhmaṇa-ṛṣabha-candra-sūrya-graha-nakṣatra-tārā-kṣaṇa-yoga-karaṇādinaimittikā-dibhiḥ ātmaśuddhayanveṣaṇam | viparītānekākāra-pralamba-rajjulambye 'mārge mārgasaṃjñā, aśucau śucisaṃjñā, amunau munisaṃjñayā ṣaḍjagaccakra-praviṣṭa-buddhimato gamanaṃ gamyaṃ ca saṃsāramevānusaranti na tu nirvāṇamiti | teṣāṃ samyak prajñayā darśane caturvidhaviparyaya-rahitatvāt samucchinnamūlāni tālavṛkṣamastakavadanābhāsagatāni āyatyāmanutpāda-nirodhadharmāṇi iti | tasmādevoktam |
body.translated_text: For the purpose of [understanding] <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), it is said that one does not revert to the past. The delusion 'Was I in the past?' does not arise, because knowledge arises in the absence of delusion — nor [the thought] 'I was such and such a person in the past,' and so forth. The delusion 'Was I a <s>deva</s> (god) or a <s>gandharva</s> (celestial musician)? Was I dwelling in happiness or dwelling in suffering?' simply does not exist. The delusion 'Was I in a good destiny or a bad destiny? For a long time or a short time? How was I?' also simply does not exist. One does not revert to the future. The delusion 'Will I exist in the future?' and 'Or will I not exist?' — this delusion too does not exist here. The delusion 'What will I be in the future — a <s>deva</s>, a <s>piśāca</s> (demon), a human, or what?' — this too simply does not arise. The delusion 'Will I be happy or suffering, beautiful or ugly? How will I be?' does not exist here either. 'One does not revert to the present' means one is not deluded about the present. 'What is this?' — whether there is a self or no self. 'How is this?' — whether it has form or is formless — delusion does not arise here. 'What are [these] beings?' — whether they are doers of good <s>karma</s> or doers of bad <s>karma</s> — no delusion arises. 'From where has this being come — from the realm of <s>devas</s> or from the hells? Having fallen from here, will it go to the <s>devas</s>, humans, hells, <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), or animals?' — delusion does not arise here. 'The <s>śramaṇas</s> (ascetics) and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> (brahmins) will have various views in the world,' and so forth. 'Views' means standpoints of [wrong] view. 'Various' means distinct. 'Namely' is for the purpose of illustration. 'Connected with the doctrine of self' means [asserting] the existence of a self apart from the <s>skandhas</s>. 'Self and what belongs to self, without examination' — because of being connected with grasping at an essential self, it is said 'connected with the doctrine of self.' For the purpose of [explaining] the arising of perverted apprehension, 'connected with the doctrine of <s>pudgala</s> (person)' and so forth — <s>pudgala</s> means one who transmigrates, [posited as] apart from the <s>skandhas</s>; since there is no going to another world having abandoned this world, and no coming to this world having left the other world, the apprehension is called a perverted apprehension. 'Connected with the doctrine of auspicious curiosities' — <s>kautuka</s> (curiosity) refers to worldly crafts and arts, and whatever pertains to the various fields of knowledge: festivals, marriages, weddings, quarrels, battles; in gardens, rivers, oceans, mountains, and forests of various kinds — the activities of a noble one such as going, seeing, crossing, engaging, dwelling, delighting, playing, enjoying, tasting, dancing, singing, reciting verses, conversing, running, leaping; tales and debates about marvelous men, women, boys, and girls, riddles and sayings; combat with elephants, horses, and the like; [omens from] dūrvā grass, curds, gorocanā, fields, plows, hammers, flowers, fruits, water-pots, conch shells, fish, and the like; <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, bulls, the moon, sun, planets, <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions), stars, auspicious moments, <s>yogas</s>, <s>karaṇas</s>, and other prognostic signs — seeking self-purification through these. On the wrong path with its manifold perverted, extended, rope-like [entanglements] of depending on the non-path — perceiving a path where there is no path, perceiving purity where there is impurity, perceiving a sage where there is no sage — the intellect that has entered the six-fold wheel of existence follows <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) in its going and destination, but not <s>nirvāṇa</s>. When those [views] are seen correctly with <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), because they are free from the four kinds of error, they are uprooted, rendered incapable of arising again like the crown of a palm tree, gone to a state of non-appearance, having the nature of non-arising and cessation in the future. Therefore it is said —

body.text: tathā kaścicca na cyutaḥ | janmābhāso 'pyasaṃlloke
body.translated_text: And thus no one has truly fallen; even the appearance of birth does not [truly exist] in the world.

body.text: tasmād udāharaṇam-
body.translated_text: Therefore, an example —

body.text:
yathāpādapasaṅgataḥ |
vahnistrotapravṛttiḥ syāt hetuvaikalyatastathā |
nānupravartate hyagniḥ
body.translated_text:
Just as fire arises from contact with wood,
so too is the flow of its progression; when the cause is deficient,
fire does not proceed further.

body.text: tathā iti yathā candrasya rūpe dūrasthite 'pi parīttajalabhājaneṣu jale vipulatailapātreṣu vā avabhāsate | candrarūpasaṃkrāntiranekatvaṃ vāpi nāsti, tathāpi anekajalapātreṣu dṛśyate | evam asmānna kaściccyuto na gato nāgato, hetupratyayavaikalyāt cyuti-gamanāgamanāvabhāsāḥ | tadvajjalabhājanavat sattvasantānasya jagataḥ sthānāntareṣu bahurūpeṇa cittacandrabimbotpādaḥ, hetupratyayāvaikalyāt | kuśalākuśalāneñjyādi-hetoryathākṣepā tatrāvabhāsākārā vijñaptirudbhavati | ātmātmīyaviyuktaḥ sarvabhāveṣu pratītyasamutpādakramo 'vagantavyaḥ | avicchedo - dāharaṇam- yathāpādapasaṅgataḥ | vahnistrotaḥ pravṛttiḥ syāt | karmakleśa-lipta-cittasantānaṃ vahnistrotonibaddhamindhanaṃ tu karmakleśata eva syāditi parīkṣyate | yathā - agnīndhanahetukaṃ jvalanam avicchinnam | indhanābhāve vicchinnam, tadvad atrāpi karmakleśendhanamucchidya saṃkleśālaya-vijñānabījao-santāne jñānāgni-saṃyogād dagdhe sati hetu-nirodhān na phalodbhavaḥ | tasmādevoktam - yānyekeṣāṃ śramaṇa-brāhmāṇānāṃ tadyathā iti ito bāhyānām lokastu lokaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Thus' — just as the form of the moon, though situated far away, appears in small water vessels or in large oil lamps' vessels of water. There is neither a transfer of the moon's form nor multiplicity, yet it is seen in many water vessels. Likewise, no one has died, departed, or arrived from here — due to deficiency of causes and conditions, the appearances of death, departure, and arrival [arise]. Just like water vessels, in various places throughout the world of beings' continuums (<s>santāna</s>), the moon-reflection of mind-consciousness arises in many forms, due to non-deficiency of causes and conditions. In accordance with the propulsion of meritorious, demeritorious, and imperturbable causes and the like, consciousness-appearances arise in those forms. The sequence of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), devoid of self and what belongs to self, should be understood in all phenomena. [As for] non-interruption — the illustration is: 'just as from the connection of trees, the stream of fire proceeds.' The mental continuum stained by <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) is to be examined as fuel bound to the stream of fire, arising from <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> themselves. Just as — burning caused by fire and fuel is uninterrupted; in the absence of fuel, it is interrupted. Likewise here too, having cut off the fuel of <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s>, when the seed-continuum of the defiled <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (store-consciousness) is burned through conjunction with the fire of <s>jñāna</s> (wisdom), due to the cessation of causes there is no arising of fruit. Therefore it is said — 'those of certain <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, namely' — those outside [the teaching]; 'the world' means the world.

body.text: naśyan-naśyan gatyarthaḥ, lujyatatvāllokaḥ | viśīryamāṇa ityadhivacanam | dṛṣṭigatānīti dṛgdarśanam viparīta-śāstraśravaṇacintanādimithyā-jñānodbhavaṃ mithyā-jñānaṃ tu dṛṣṭirityucyate | pṛthak tu bhinnam | tadyathā - ātmavāda-pratisaṃyuktānītyādi tu pañcopādāna-skandheṣu rūpa-vedanā-saṃjñā-saṃskāra-vijñārnoṣvati ātmātmīya-rahiteṣu, ātmatvena samyagdṛṣṭiryā kliṣṭaprajñā sā dṛṣṭiḥ | satkāyāntadṛṣṭi-śīla-vrata-mithyādṛṣṭipūrvakaṃ kuprajñāvidyāsaṃprayuktatvād dṛṣṭiriti | tadavidyāpūrvakaṃ rāgapratighākārāvidyādṛṣṭi-vicikitsopakleśa-saṃprayukto dṛṣṭi-lakṣaṇa-dhātvākārabhedam anadhigamya saṃkliṣṭālaya-vijñāna-vāsanāvasthita-tadākāra-vijñānāvabhāsapoṣaṇāt prāgeva lokottara-mārgāśritacaturāryasatyabhāvanā-bhyāsakrameṇa duḥkha-samudaya-nirodha-mārga-darśana-bhāvanā-vimukti-viśeṣānantareṇa prahāṇa-sākṣātkāraḥ | yaścāpi saptatriṃśadbodhipakṣadharmasmṛtyupasthāna-samyakprahāṇa-ṛddhipāda-indriya-bala-bodhyaṅga-mārga-pratītyasamutpāda-dhyāna-arūpi-apramāṇa-ṣaḍanusmṛtyādiyadharmapudgalanairātmya-bodhicittabhāvanā-samādhi-dhāraṇā-śraddhā-vīrya-samādhi-prajñā-bhūmi-vaśīkārā-bhijñāna-jñāna-pāramitā-vimuktidvāra-kṣānti-bhāvanādi-krameṇa lokottaramārgānugata-tvād adhimukticaryāyāṃ pratisthāpya niryāṇa-prayoga-sākṣātkārād indriya-bala-abhayao-asaṃsṛṣṭa-pratisaṃvid-vyañjana-mahāpuruṣa-lakṣaṇa-ṛddhipādādi bhāvanāṃ paripūrya anuttarasamyak-samavabodhāvabodhāt śamatha-vipaśyanānukūla-samabhāvo bhāvane 'nantā-cintyaguṇyaṃ śāntasvabhāvakāyaṃ, ādimadhyāntavarjitaṃ, jñātvā prāpnoti buddhatvam ityuktam | tatra rūpaskandhastu rūpāvabhāsākāra-vijñaptyavabhāsa-vikalpodbhūto 'neka-dravyātmako bhūtabhautika-rūpa-lakṣaṇa ekādaśao-sāmānyātmaka-pañcadravyākārāropa-saṃghaṭṭitaḥ cakṣuḥ-śrotrādirūpa-śabdādikāma-rūpa-arūpa-pratisaṃyuktābhūtaparikalpanā-lakṣaṇaḥ skandho dhātvāyatana-indriya-vijñāna-viṣayātmako 'tha ca tādṛganyatādṛgrūpa-lakṣaṇo dharmastu rūpaskandha iti |
body.translated_text: 'Perishing and perishing' conveys the meaning of passing; because it dissolves, it is called 'world' (<s>loka</s>). 'That which disintegrates' is the epithet. 'Views' (<s>dṛṣṭigata</s>) means sight and seeing — wrong knowledge arising from hearing and reflecting on perverted teachings; such wrong knowledge is called a 'view' (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>). 'Distinct' means separate. Namely — 'those connected with the doctrine of self' and so forth: in the five aggregates of clinging (<s>upādānaskandha</s>) — form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — which are devoid of self and what belongs to self, the afflicted wisdom that regards them as self is that view. Being preceded by the view of a real self-entity (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), extreme views, attachment to rules and rituals, and wrong views, and being conjoined with corrupt wisdom and <s>avidyā</s>, it is called a 'view.' That [ignorance], preceded by <s>avidyā</s>, conjoined with the secondary afflictions of desire, aversion, ignorance-views, and doubt — without comprehending the distinctions of the characteristics, elements, and aspects of views — due to nourishing the consciousness-appearances of that form established in the habitual tendencies of the defiled <s>ālayavijñāna</s>, abandonment and direct realization [occur] only through the progressive cultivation of the four noble truths relying on the supramundane path, through the special stages of seeing and cultivating the truths of suffering, origination, cessation, and path, followed by liberation. And through the progressive cultivation of the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment (<s>bodhipakṣadharma</s>) — the four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), four right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), five faculties (<s>indriya</s>), five powers (<s>bala</s>), seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), the eightfold path (<s>mārga</s>), dependent origination, <s>dhyānas</s>, formless attainments, immeasurables, the six recollections (<s>ṣaḍanusmṛti</s>) and the like, the selflessness of phenomena and persons, cultivation of <s>bodhicitta</s>, <s>samādhi</s>, <s>dhāraṇī</s>, faith, vigor, concentration, wisdom, the stages (<s>bhūmi</s>), mastery, superknowledges (<s>abhijñāna</s>), knowledge, <s>pāramitās</s>, gates of liberation, patience, and meditation — through following the supramundane path, having been established in the practice of aspiration, through the direct realization of the approach to deliverance, having perfected the cultivation of faculties, powers, fearlessnesses, unmingled [dharmas], analytical knowledges, syllables, marks of a great being, bases of supernatural power, and the like — through the awakening to unsurpassed perfect complete enlightenment, having attained the equipoise favorable to <s>śamatha</s> (calm) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) in cultivation, possessing infinite and inconceivable qualities, a body of peaceful nature, devoid of beginning, middle, and end — having known this, one attains <s>buddhahood</s>, so it is said. Therein, the form aggregate (<s>rūpaskandha</s>) is: consciousness-appearance arisen through the proliferation of conceptualizations of form-appearances — of the nature of multiple substances, characterized by the form of elements and derivatives, of eleven general natures, superimposed with the aspects of five substance-forms, assembled [from] eye, ear, and so forth, form, sound, and so forth, connected with desire, form, and formless [realms] — characterized by unreal conceptualization, the aggregate of elements, sense-bases, faculties, consciousnesses, and objects — and such and other form-characteristics constitute the <s>dharma</s> called the form aggregate.

body.text: tatra vedanāskandha iti sukha-duḥkhobhayākāreṇa āsvādākāra-vijñaptyavabhāsaḥ | viṣayendriyavijñānabhedena vedanā ṣaṭkāyā | dhātvākāraviśeṣabhedena kleśopa-kleśasaṃprayuktatvād anantāḥ prabhedāḥ syuḥ | sukha-duḥkha-saumanasya-daurmanasyo-pekṣānvitatvāt ṣaḍākāramātmadravyameva abhūtasaṃkalpa-vikalpālaya-vijñānavāsanopa-nibaddhatvād rāga-dveṣa-mohāditridhātu-vikalpavaśodbhūta-dravya-saṃgṛhītatvād vedanā-skandha iti | saṃjñā sūkṣma-sthūla-mahāṅgatādi-citrīkārāva-bhāsākāra-vijñapti-rvikalpanāvaśodbhūta-pūrvahasana-nandana-krīḍanādi-kānanusmṛtya strī-puruṣādi-nimittaviśeṣagrahaṇātmikā viṣayendriya-vijñānabhedena ṣaṭkāyā saṃjñā | rāga-dveṣa-moha-nibandhanatvād dhātvākāra-viśeṣabhedena tu anantaprasarā | saṃkliṣṭasyālayavijñāna-vāsanā-sambandhatvād ātmamohādi-saṃyuktātmatā tu saṃjñeti | saṃskārastu saṃprayuktā-prayukta-prajñapti-saṃskṛtā-saṃskṛtāvabhāsāṃkāra-vijñaptiḥ-vikalpanāvaśenodbhūtaḥ | pūrvākṣiptālaya-vijñānād astitva-vāsanā-bhedena tu dhātoḥ ākāra-viśeṣānanta-prasarānvitasya saṃskāra-skandha-saṃgṛhītatvāt saṃskāraskandha iti | tatra vijñāna-skandhastvaṣṭavidhaḥ | viṣayendriya-vijñānānāṃ viśiṣṭāvabhāsākāra-vijñaptiḥ | vikalpanāvaśodbhūtālaya-vijñānasya vāsanopanibaddhatvād dhātorākāra-viśeṣa-bhedenānantaprasaro hi vijñānaskandha iti |
body.translated_text: Therein, the feeling aggregate (<s>vedanāskandha</s>) is: consciousness-appearance of the flavor-aspect in the forms of pleasure, pain, and [neither]. Feeling is sixfold according to the distinctions of objects, faculties, and consciousnesses. Due to conjunction with afflictions and secondary afflictions according to the specific distinctions of elemental aspects, the divisions would be infinite. Being pervaded by pleasure, pain, mental happiness, mental unhappiness, and equanimity, of six aspects, of the nature of self-substance itself — bound to the habitual tendencies of the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> of unreal conceptual proliferation, comprising substances arisen through the force of conceptualization of desire, aversion, and delusion in the three realms — this is called the feeling aggregate. Perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>) is: consciousness-appearance of the variegated aspects of subtle, gross, and great, and so forth — arisen through the force of conceptualization, recollecting former laughter, delight, play, and the like, grasping the specific characteristics of women, men, and such signs — sixfold according to the distinctions of objects, faculties, and consciousnesses. Being rooted in desire, aversion, and delusion, according to the specific distinctions of elemental aspects, it extends infinitely. Due to its connection with the habitual tendencies of the defiled <s>ālayavijñāna</s>, the selfhood conjoined with self-delusion and the like is called perception. The formations aggregate (<s>saṃskāraskandha</s>) is: consciousness-appearance of associated, disassociated, designated, conditioned, and conditioned-appearance aspects — arisen through the force of conceptualization. Due to being comprised within the formations aggregate through the distinctions of existence-tendencies from the previously propelled <s>ālayavijñāna</s>, extending infinitely according to the specific distinctions of elemental aspects — this is called the formations aggregate. Therein, the consciousness aggregate (<s>vijñānaskandha</s>) is eightfold: consciousness-appearance of the distinctive appearances of objects, faculties, and consciousnesses — being bound to the habitual tendencies of the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> arisen through the force of conceptualization, extending infinitely according to the specific distinctions of elemental aspects — this is called the consciousness aggregate.

body.text: teṣāmapyevaṃ dhātvāyatana-sāsrava-saṃskṛta-saṃkleśādi-paryāyabhedena sva-lakṣaṇasambandhena saṃkṣipya skandho dhāturāyatanamiti | evaṃ saṃkliṣṭālayavijñāna-bījānvitā abhūtasaṃkalpasamuttthatraidhātukodgatāste cittacaitasikādayastu saṃsāra iti | tathāpi tatra ādāveva kartrādirahito riktastuccho 'sāra iti viditvā caturāryasatya-bhāvanānulomapravṛttyā nirṇīto lokottara-jñānāgni-samudbhūto-'vidyāndhakārādi-rahito hetupratyayārthatathatāparijñānāt śānto dharmakāyo 'vagamyate |
body.translated_text: Of these likewise, through the various categories of elements, sense-bases, tainted, conditioned, defiled, and so forth, summarized in connection with their own characteristics — the aggregate, element, and sense-base [are understood]. Thus, endowed with the seeds of the defiled <s>ālayavijñāna</s>, arising from unreal conceptualization, emerging in the three realms — mind, mental factors, and the rest constitute <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence). Nevertheless, having understood from the very outset that [all this] is devoid of an agent and the like, empty, hollow, and without essence, through activity conforming to the cultivation of the four noble truths, the <s>dharmakāya</s> — purified, arisen from the fire of supramundane wisdom, free from the darkness of <s>avidyā</s> and the rest, peaceful through the full comprehension of the reality of causes and conditions — is realized.

body.text: tasmād duḥkha-samudaya-nirodha-mārga-darśana-bhāvanāmārgakramaḥ| tatra duḥkha-satyam-anityatā-duḥkhatā-śūnyatā-nairātmya-samyaganudarśanajñānena kṣānti-mukti-prahāṇa-viśeṣānāntaryajñānena ca tad-duḥkhamavagamya kleśālayavijñānavāsanāṃ saṃnihatya pudgaladharmanairātmyam avabudhya, traidhātukāvabhāsitābhūtasaṃkalpodbhūtaṃ asmin cittamātre māyā-marīci-gandharvanagara-alātacakra-pratiśrutka-udakacandra-pratibimbavad vibhāvane, skandhādau dhātau āyatane ca grāhya-grāhakatāṃ vihāya dharmanairātmyasamatāyāṃ praviśe, svacittameva ādyamanutpannamiti śūnyajñānapraveśe, sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvatājñānasya karuṇāmūlaka-bodhicittasya hetūbhūta-vividhopāya-puṇyajñānasambhārasaṃcaye daśapāramitāhetubhiḥ daśabhūmyādhāra daśajñānālambana-daśavaśitāphalānvite 'nantācintya-guṇākāraḥ śāntadharmakāyo 'vabudhyate | evaṃ samudaya-satya-samudaya-hetu-prabhava-pratyaya-ānantarya-vimukti-prahāṇa-viśeṣa-darśana-anuloma-pratiloma-bhāvanākāreṇa saṃkliṣṭa-ālayavijñāna-vāsanā-mala-rahitatve śāntadharmakāye praveśaḥ | nirodha-satye 'pi nirodha-śānta-praṇīta-niḥsaraṇatā-ānantarya-vimukti-prahāṇa-viśeṣa-darśana-bhāvanāmārgakrameṇa saṃkliṣṭā-layavijñānavāsanāsamudghātena ānantarya-prahāṇa-vimukti-viśeṣa-bhāvanayā pudgala-dharmanairātmyādhigame śāntadharmakāyaprāptiḥ | hetupratyayao-rahitatvāt mārgasatye 'pi mārga-nyāya-pratipatti-nairyāṇika-sandarśane evaṃ darśana-bhāvanā-ānantarya-prahāṇa-vimukti-viśeṣamārgānukūlatāyai ālayavijñāne vidyamānāṃ vāsanāṃ saṃnihatya pudgaladharma-nairātmya-samatāvabodhāt trikāyādhiṣṭhāna-śānta-dharmakāyasyācintyā-prameyaguṇa-gaṇasya ādimadhyāntarahitasya avicchinna-nābhogakaraṇātmaka-sarvārthānāṃ anuttaraṃ sarvajñatvaṃ prāpnoti | api coktam -
body.translated_text: Therefore, the sequence of the paths of seeing and cultivation regarding the truths of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path. Therein, by the knowledge of correct contemplation of the truth of suffering — impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self — and by the special knowledge of patience, liberation, abandonment, and uninterrupted [path], having comprehended that suffering, having struck down the <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impressions) of the afflicted <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (store consciousness), having awakened to the selflessness of person and <s>dharmas</s> (<s>pudgaladharmanairātmya</s>), contemplating that in this mind-only, the phenomenal world of the three realms, arisen from unreal conceptualization, is like <s>māyā</s> (illusion), a mirage, a <s>gandharva</s> city, a whirling firebrand, an echo, a moon in water, and a reflection — abandoning the duality of grasper and grasped in the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases), entering the equality of the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s>, entering the knowledge of emptiness whereby one's own mind is primordially unarisen — in the accumulation of the stores of merit and knowledge that are the cause of the <s>bodhicitta</s> (awakening mind) rooted in compassion and the knowledge of the naturelessness of all <s>dharmas</s>, through the various skillful means, endowed with the ten <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) as causes, the ten <s>bhūmis</s> (grounds) as support, the ten knowledges as objects, and the ten masteries as fruits — the peaceful <s>Dharmakāya</s> (truth body) of infinite, inconceivable, and excellent qualities is realized. Thus, through the mode of cultivation in forward and reverse order of the truth of origination — origination, cause, arising, condition — and through uninterrupted, liberation, abandonment, special, seeing [paths], when free from the defilements of the <s>vāsanā</s> of the afflicted <s>ālayavijñāna</s>, there is entry into the peaceful <s>Dharmakāya</s>. Regarding the truth of cessation too — through the sequence of the path of seeing and cultivation of cessation, peace, excellence, and deliverance — by the eradication of the <s>vāsanā</s> of the afflicted <s>ālayavijñāna</s>, through the cultivation of the uninterrupted, abandonment, liberation, and special [paths], upon the realization of the selflessness of person and <s>dharmas</s>, there is the attainment of the peaceful <s>Dharmakāya</s>. Regarding the truth of the path too, since it is free from causes and conditions — through the demonstration of path, correctness, practice, and deliverance — for the conformity with the paths of seeing, cultivation, uninterrupted, abandonment, liberation, and special [paths], having struck down the <s>vāsanā</s> existing in the <s>ālayavijñāna</s>, through the awakening to the equality of the selflessness of person and <s>dharmas</s>, one attains the unsurpassed omniscience (<s>sarvajñatva</s>) of the peaceful <s>Dharmakāya</s> established in the three bodies (<s>trikāya</s>) — possessing inconceivable and immeasurable hosts of qualities, devoid of beginning, middle, and end, of the nature of uninterrupted effortless accomplishment of all aims. Moreover it is said:

body.text: ya evaṃ tathatākṣamaḥ | tasmai vyākriyate nūnaṃ
body.translated_text: Whoever is thus patient with <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) — to that one, prediction is certainly given.

body.text: ya evamanantarokta-pratītyasamutpāda-pudgaladharmanairātmya-tattva-kṣama icchati, sa eva pudgaladharmanairātmyakṣamatānvitatvād anuttarasamyaksambodhiṃ vyākṛtavat paśyet, jānīyāccetyarthaḥ | tasmāt sūtre- yo bhadanta śāriputra kulaputro kuladuhitā vā evaṃvidha-dharmakṣānti-samanvitaḥ, tasya tathāgato 'rhat samyaksambuddho 'nuttaraḥ samyaksambodhiṃ vyākaroti ityuktam |
body.translated_text: Whoever desires the truth of the selflessness of person and <s>dharmas</s> as stated above in relation to <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) — that very one, being endowed with patience regarding the selflessness of person and <s>dharmas</s>, should see [it] as if the prediction of unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarasamyaksambodhi</s>) has been given, and should know [it] — such is the meaning. Therefore in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, whatever son or daughter of good family is endowed with such patience for the <s>Dharma</s>, to that one the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly awakened one, predicts unsurpassed perfect awakening' — thus it is stated.

body.text: maitreyastu svayaṃ tathā | uvāca śāriputrāya
body.translated_text: <s>Maitreya</s> himself likewise spoke to <s>Śāriputra</s>:

body.text: evam śāriputro bodhisattvo maitreyamapṛcchat | bodhisattvo maitreyo 'pi śālistambopamā kṛtā idaṃ sūtram vistareṇa vibhajya bhāṣitavān | bodhisattvamaitreyeṇa bhāṣitāṃ śālistambopamāṃ kṛtvā śāriputrastu tacchrutvā iti śālistambopamā kṛtā | saṃstuto dhṛta sāraśca devasaṃghān iti | dhṛtasāra iti dharmārthatathatāvabodhatvāt sāragrahaṇam | devasaṃghāniti deva-nāga-yakṣa-gandharva-ādi-sahitān | anumoditeti anumodya | saḥstuta iti tvayā yathoktaḥ tathaiva asti nānyatheti, avadhārayan nirjātatvāt |
body.translated_text: Thus <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, asked <s>Maitreya</s>. <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> too, having made the simile of the rice stalk, expounded this <s>sūtra</s> in detail and at length. Having made the simile of the rice stalk spoken by <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>, <s>Śāriputra</s> heard it — thus the simile of the rice stalk was made. 'Praised, held the essence, and the assemblies of gods' — 'held the essence' means grasping the essence because of the understanding of the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of the meaning of the <s>Dharma</s>. 'Assemblies of gods' means together with gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, etc. 'Rejoiced' means having rejoiced. 'Praised' means: ascertaining that 'what you have said is exactly so and not otherwise,' because it has been established.

body.text: gatvottthāya praharṣitaḥ | ākhyātavāṃśca bhikṣubhyaḥ
body.translated_text: Having gone, risen, delighted, he narrated to the <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks).

body.text: tasmādeva sūtre- atha āyuṣmān śāriputro maitreyasya bodhisattvasya bhāṣitam abhinandya utthāyāsanāt prakrānta ityuktam | maitreyeṇa bodhisattvena mahāsattvena evamuktaṃ maitreyeṇa bodhisattvena, evamiti śāriputreṇa kathitam | anumoditam | śāriputraḥ tacchutvā praharṣitaḥ santuṣṭa ityarthaḥ | gatvā bhikṣubhyo gambhīrodārādbhutaṃ sūtraṃ yathāśrutavat sarvasattvahitāya bhāṣitam |
body.translated_text: Therefore in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, having rejoiced at the words of <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>, having risen from his seat, departed' — thus it is stated. 'Thus spoke <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>' — 'thus' was said by <s>Śāriputra</s>. [He] rejoiced. <s>Śāriputra</s>, having heard that, was delighted and satisfied — such is the meaning. Having gone, he spoke to the <s>bhikṣus</s> the profound, noble, and wondrous <s>sūtra</s> as he had heard it, for the benefit of all sentient beings.

body.text:
śālistambasya sūtrasya vistarākhyā subhadrikā |
hīnabuddhi prabodhārthaṃ śatairdvādaśabhiḥ kṛtā |
body.translated_text:
The detailed commentary on the <s>Śālistamba Sūtra</s>, called <s>Subhadrā</s>,
has been composed in twelve hundred [verses] for the awakening of those of lesser intellect.

body.text: ācāryanāgārjunena viracitā śālistambakavistarākhyāṭīkā samāptā |
body.translated_text: The commentary called the <s>Śālistambaka Vistarākhyā</s>, composed by <s>Ācārya</s> <s>Nāgārjuna</s>, is completed.

body.text: bhāratīyopādhyāyena dharmaśrībhadreṇa lokacakṣuṣā bhadantasādhumatinā jñāna kumāreṇa cānūditā | mahāsaṃśodhaka-lokacakṣuṣā bhadanta-śrīkuṭīreṇa saṃśodhya nirṇītā |
body.translated_text: It was translated by the Indian preceptor <s>Dharmaśrībhadra</s>, the Eye of the World <s>Bhadanta</s> <s>Sādhumati</s>, and <s>Jñānakumāra</s>. It was revised and finalized by the great editor, the Eye of the World <s>Bhadanta</s> <s>Śrīkuṭīra</s>.
